items.title: Wave 1–3: RI ID → RINASPACE → RINPO Phone → Connector Gateway
items.body:
## Objective
Ship the narrowest reliable end-to-end loop from the proposed RI Platform Next Build contract (draft PR #223):

`RI ID → RINASPACE → RINPO → authorised action → audit → first value`

## Wave 1 — Identity / provisioning
- Ratify public `RINASPACE` naming through master-spec change control; retain legacy aliases temporarily.
- Audit existing auth/providers and map Google / email OTP / mobile OTP / passkeys into one RI ID.
- Personal RINASPACE creation on verified first login.
- Organisation create/join flow using existing `organization_id` boundary.
- Trial grants / entitlements / async provisioning / first-value telemetry.
- Fail closed on missing entitlement or tenant context.

## Wave 2 — RINPO Phone production shell
- Replace demo Today with authorised real data.
- Ground Ask in current RI ID + org/workspace/role context.
- Actions = proposals / approvals / executions / history.
- Growth shell uses existing campaigns/leads/content capabilities.
- Apps = capability registry + connectors + installed packs.
- Memory/permissions/settings surfaces.
- Avatar click should open the same authenticated RINPO Phone across eligible RINADS surfaces.

## Wave 3 — RI Connector Gateway
- Provider-neutral connection registry.
- OAuth + MCP client layer + webhooks/event ingestion.
- Provider scopes, health, audit, revocation and credential isolation.
- Priority adapters: Google Workspace, WhatsApp, Shopify, Wix, WordPress; logistics and Hootsuite/social after core gate.

## WhatsApp guardrails
- consent proof + category
- suppression/opt-out
- template enforcement where required
- human escalation path
- rate limits
- cost estimate before high-volume send
- approval + queue + delivery reconciliation + attribution + audit

## Acceptance
1. New verified user gets exactly one RI ID.
2. Personal RINASPACE is provisioned idempotently.
3. New business can create/join an organisation without a second account.
4. RINPO Phone reflects server-authorised context only.
5. At least one read-only connector is installable and revocable through the Gateway.
6. At least one approved write connector action flows proposal → approval → execution → audit.
7. No connector credentials are present in browser bundles.
8. Cross-tenant tests pass.
9. First-value event is persisted.
10. Existing production surfaces continue to build and pass release gates.

## Non-goals
- no World implementation in this wave
- no infrastructure migration
- no social-network clone
- no separate database per tenant
- no provider SDK direct from domain code
- no unrestricted L4 actions

items.title: Reduce connector heap when capturing many databases with identical table layouts
items.body:
### Problem

A binlog connector that captures many databases with identical table layouts (a multi-tenant setup: one database per tenant, the same few hundred tables in each) keeps a very large part of its heap after the schema read, most of it duplicated or no longer needed once the snapshot is over. At 1,000 databases x 350 tables the live heap is several GiB, and it grows linearly with the number of databases.

`schema.history.internal.memory.optimization` (dbz#1813) already interns the relational model (`TableId`, `TableImpl`, `ColumnImpl`, ...) and takes this from 6,129 MiB to 4,499 MiB in my setup. The rest is mostly objects it doesn't cover, plus state that is retained for the life of the task.

### Setup

- Debezium 3.7.0.Final, MariaDB connector, MariaDB 11.8, JDK 21, G1, Strimzi-style Connect worker
- `snapshot.mode=no_data`, `schema.history.internal.store.only.captured.tables.ddl=true`, `schema.history.internal.memory.optimization=on`
- 1,000 captured databases x 350 tables (average ~18 columns, 3-4k distinct column definitions overall), identical layout in every database
- "Live heap" = class histogram after a full GC (`jcmd GC.class_histogram`); settled heap with periodic full GCs agrees within ~100 MiB

### What holds the memory (JFR old-object sampling + class histogram)

1. `BinlogSnapshotChangeEventSource.schemaEvents` (a `LinkedHashSet<SchemaChangeEvent>`) is filled while reading the table structure and never cleared after the events are dispatched. The source object lives as long as the task, so all of them (703,001 in this setup) stay reachable. Nothing reads the set afterwards.
2. `AbstractSnapshotChangeEventSource.execute` registers the snapshot context as the `SNAPSHOT_CONTEXT` bean and never removes it, so `capturedTables`, `capturedSchemaTables` and the `tables` model stay reachable through the bean registry for the life of the task.
3. `Tables.CachingTableFilter` memoizes the include decision for every table it is asked about, including the excluded ones. The snapshot asks about every table on the server, so the cache holds one `TableId` per table on the server (3.26M entries on a server with 9,000 databases of which 1,000 were captured), and the `TableId`s are separate copies from the interned ones in the table model.
4. `TableSchemaBuilder.addField` builds a new `ConnectSchema` plus parameter maps for every column of every table (7.5M `ConnectSchema`/30M map entries at this scale, more than half of the heap) although they are equal across tables.
5. `TableSchemaBuilder.convertersForColumns` creates one converter lambda per column per table (7.07M lambdas, 175 MiB), identical for identical columns.

### Proposal

Five small changes, each independent:

1. Clear `schemaEvents` once the events are dispatched.
2. Remove the `SNAPSHOT_CONTEXT` bean after a successful snapshot (the bean registry has `remove`). I found no reader of the bean in the modules in this repository; it is a public constant, so I'd like to hear if anything relies on it after the snapshot.
3. Make `CachingTableFilter` keep included decisions (bounded by what is captured, interned so they share instances with the table model) and a bounded set of excluded ones (cleared when it reaches 10k).
4. Intern the column `Schema` in `TableSchemaBuilder.addField`, through the existing `Interner`, so it follows `schema.history.internal.memory.optimization` (`off` is unchanged).
5. Share the provider's value converter between identical columns through a small pooled wrapper, again through `Interner`; custom converters and column mappers are never shared.

### Measured effect (fresh read, live heap after full GC)

| 1,000 captured databases | live heap |
|---|---|
| 3.7.0.Final, `memory.optimization=off` | 6,129 MiB |
| `on` | 4,499 MiB |
| `on` + 4 (prototype) | 2,348 MiB |
| `on` + 1 + 4 | 1,637 MiB |

On a server that also holds 8,000 databases that are not captured (so items 2, 3 and 5 matter):

| | live heap |
|---|---|
| `on` + 1 + 4 | 1,937 MiB |
| + 2 + 3 | 1,511 MiB |
| + 5 | 1,324 MiB |

Linear scaling afterwards: about 1 MiB per captured database on the same layout. After the changes the heap is dominated by per-table Kafka Connect struct schemas (their field lists and name maps); I'm looking at sharing those separately in Kafka (`ConnectSchema`), which would be a different change.

Streaming is unaffected in my checks (events flow, `execute-snapshot` signals still run); the Debezium test suite has not been run against these changes yet, that is what the pull request's CI is for.

### Questions

- Is extending `schema.history.internal.memory.optimization` to the Connect schemas and converters (items 4 and 5) the right switch, or would you prefer a separate option?
- Anything that depends on the `SNAPSHOT_CONTEXT` bean or on `schemaEvents` after the snapshot has completed?
- One pull request with separate commits, or one per item?

I have this working on 3.7.0.Final and the affected classes are unchanged on `main`; I'll open a pull request with tests unless you prefer a different approach.

items.title: Spike: shared high-density multitenant Hosted engine (entry tier via Elsa multitenancy)
items.body:
Requested by Sipke (28 Sep). Post-#508, not launch-blocking. Design it together with #629 (customer-built images) as one tiered Hosted offer: **Shared** (entry or trial, many customers per engine using Elsa tenants), **Dedicated** (today's managed instance), and **Custom image** (#629).

**Why:** a dedicated engine per customer sets a cost floor on price. A shared engine enables a low-price entry tier or free trial at much better per-customer margin.

**Questions to answer**
1. **Isolation and security:** how strong is Elsa 3 tenant separation (data, secrets, workflow definitions, HTTP endpoints, timers, blob storage)? Is it one database with tenant columns, or a database or schema per tenant? What is the blast radius of a tenant-boundary bug?
2. **Noisy neighbors:** per-tenant quotas, throttling, workflow execution limits, and fair scheduling. How do we detect and move a heavy tenant to Dedicated?
3. **Lifecycle:** one Elsa version for all tenants on a shard. How do upgrades, maintenance windows and rollbacks work? How does a tenant move Shared to Dedicated (and back), and what data migration does that need?
4. **Control model:** is a tenant a first-class instance in Control's model, or a new resource type? What does provisioning, deletion and the customer overview (#630/#631) show for a shared tenant? Who holds the shard-level operator view?
5. **Evidence and trust:** what evidence level does a shared tenant carry? Uptime (#632) is per shard, reported per tenant.
6. **Identity and Studio:** Open Studio handoff scoped to a tenant, and custom domains.
7. **Commercial:** unit economics (tenants per shard, cost per tenant), pricing shape, trial limits, and support boundaries. Pricing and the SLA are Sipke's call.
8. **Constraint:** no custom code on shared shards. Custom images (#629) are Dedicated only.

**Deliverable:** an Architect decision record with a recommended tenancy model, a go/no-go on Elsa 3 multitenancy readiness, and an estimated leaf breakdown.

items.title: [Vision/EPIC] EvoBase — nền tảng business app có kiểu: Builder, Runtime, storage profiles và automation
items.body:
## Quyết định sản phẩm — 03/10/2026

**EvoBase tiếp nhận toàn bộ vision của Votable. Votable không còn là một sản phẩm/roadmap độc lập.** Từ thời điểm này, mọi yêu cầu mới về typed tables, Grid/List/Form, relation/formula, policy, workflow, Builder/Runtime, portable app, local-first và hosted runtime được thiết kế trong EvoBase.

Code Votable cũ trong `vot-workspace` chỉ còn là nguồn migration/reference cho tới khi các capability tương ứng của EvoBase có acceptance rõ và việc gỡ bỏ được theo dõi ở #15.

### Mission

> **EvoBase là nền tảng tạo và chạy business app có kiểu. Người dùng mô hình hóa dữ liệu và nghiệp vụ bằng Builder; AppSpec là SSOT portable; cùng Rust semantic core chạy ở local/self-hosted/hosted profiles; Runtime được sinh/điều khiển bởi AppSpec thay vì code controller riêng cho từng app.**

EvoBase **không phải** Excel clone, SQL workbench, PostgREST wrapper hay một Firebase clone. UX bảng tính là cách authoring dễ dùng; semantics nằm ở AppSpec.

---

## 1. Product model

```text
Builder
  ├─ Tables / fields / typed values
  ├─ Relations / formulas / constraints
  ├─ Policies / commands / state transitions
  ├─ Views / forms / actions
  └─ Automations / connector contracts
            ↓
      Draft AppSpec
            ↓ validate / compile
      Checked AppSpec
            ↓ publish
     Immutable Release
       ↙            ↘
 Local Runtime     Hosted Runtime
 embedded store    tenant-scoped store
       ↘            ↙
        same semantics
```

### Builder và Runtime là hai vai trò khác nhau

- **Builder**: dành cho người thiết kế app; ưu tiên desktop/web, thao tác kiểu spreadsheet, relation mapping, rule/policy, form/view, publish.
- **Runtime**: dành cho người sử dụng app đã publish; list/detail/form/action/approval, responsive Web và native/CMP khi cần.
- Mobile không cần mang toàn bộ modeling UI của Builder.

---

## 2. AppSpec là canonical source

AppSpec định nghĩa bằng stable IDs:

- tables, fields, types, constraints;
- relations, lookup/rollup, captured values;
- formulas/expressions;
- views/forms/actions;
- roles/policies;
- commands, states, transitions và event intents;
- automation/function plans;
- abstract connector/capability contracts.

**Không có hai nguồn sự thật** kiểu “rule trong UI” và “rule khác trong SQL/backend”. UI, text projection, API metadata, local runtime và hosted runtime đều consume cùng checked semantics.

Host-specific facts không nằm trong portable definition: credentials, DB URL, provider tokens, current memberships/grants, secret handles, quotas.

`.evobase` có thể là package/extension đích, nhưng format/version/layout phải được chốt bằng ADR và compatibility tests; không coi đổi đuôi file là migration.

---

## 3. Typed table semantics — phần Votable được hấp thụ

### Quan hệ

Quan hệ là typed identity, ví dụ `Ref<Customer>`, không phải chuỗi ID hay công thức dò text. Rename/reorder/sort không đổi identity.

Hỗ trợ theo profile và acceptance:

- N:1 / 1:N qua canonical Ref + reverse projection;
- 1:1 với scoped uniqueness;
- N:M qua link table/edge semantics;
- relation có dữ liệu nghiệp vụ là record/table thực;
- lookup/rollup là derived value;
- captured value khác live lookup.

Relation **không tự cấp quyền**. Picker/join/lookup/aggregate/export luôn đi qua output policy.

### Công thức và constraints

Formula/query là pure computation, bounded và có kiểu. Command/function mới được phép tạo transition/effect intent. Validation phải dùng cùng semantics ở import, Builder, API và Runtime.

---

## 4. Storage: contract trước, adapter sau

**Sửa hướng cũ:** EvoBase không lấy `database-per-tenant + fixed-layout PostgreSQL` làm định nghĩa sản phẩm. Đó chỉ là một hosted spike.

Yêu cầu cứng ở semantic layer:

1. Builder thêm/sửa logical table/field/relation **không bắt buộc** chạy business `CREATE/ALTER TABLE` ngay tại thao tác cấu hình.
2. AppSpec và runtime semantics độc lập physical layout.
3. Mọi adapter phải vượt cùng conformance tests về types, Ref, constraints, revisions, CAS, transactions, receipts và failure behavior.

Các profile cần được hỗ trợ qua storage contract:

| Profile | Mục tiêu |
|---|---|
| **Local/embedded** | mở app nhanh, offline/local-first, self-contained; storage engine nhẹ là adapter |
| **Self-hosted** | user tự vận hành host + storage |
| **Hosted multi-tenant** | platform quản tenant isolation, durability, jobs, connectors |
| **Compiled relational (optional)** | materialize typed SQL ở controlled publish/migration boundary nếu benchmark cho thấy cần |

Fixed-layout PostgreSQL, schema-per-tenant, shared+RLS, database-per-tenant hoặc embedded engine là **implementation choices**, không làm thay đổi AppSpec semantics. #7 sở hữu storage contract và spikes.

---

## 5. Local-first không phải feature phụ

Vì Votable vision đã nhập vào EvoBase, local/portable phải được xem là profile nền tảng:

- definition/package mở được không cần hosted account;
- local edits/runtime dùng cùng semantic core;
- hosted account chỉ cần khi sync/collaboration/managed effects;
- local snapshot không tự tạo hosted authority;
- sync/reconnect phải revalidate current grants và conflicts;
- export/restore không được replay external effects mù quáng.

#14 sở hữu package/portability/sync/recovery semantics. Nó **không phụ thuộc chatbot/messaging**.

---

## 6. Authority, commands và workflow

```text
authorized =
    verified_host_scope
  AND current_host_grants
  AND app_policy
  AND applicable_restrictions
```

- Missing/expired/revoked context → deny.
- Write kiểm old/new state, immutable fields, constraints và expected revision.
- Request key bind immutable normalized intent; retry không lặp business effect.
- Command + state + event/outbox intent cần atomic consistency boundary ở hosted adapter.
- Functions/automation là declarative finite plans trước; arbitrary scripting/plugin runtime không phải MVP.

#6, #16, #17, #18 là các owner chính của layer này.

---

## 7. Hosted capabilities là capability layer, không phải lõi định nghĩa sản phẩm

Sau khi typed app core ổn định, host có thể cung cấp:

- durable functions/jobs/timers;
- Email/webhook/Zalo connectors;
- managed inbox/messaging;
- realtime subscriptions;
- scoped service actor/chatbot.

Các capability này phải được khai báo/bind qua AppSpec + host bindings, không hard-code theo một domain demo.

**Không để connector/chatbot chặn local-first core.**

---

## 8. Priority roadmap

### P0 — typed app core

- #4 AppSpec kernel + typed table/import
- #5 relations + formulas
- #6 policies + checked commands
- #16 declarative constraints
- #17 generic commands/state/events
- #7 storage contract + local/host adapters

### P1 — usable product loop

- #3 Builder shell/design system
- #8 preview/publish/schema evolution
- #9 generated Runtime Web/CMP
- #18 generic Gateway
- #19 versioned protocol/thin clients
- #14 portable package/local-first/sync-recovery

### P2 — managed hosted capabilities

- #10 durable functions
- #11 connectors
- #21 realtime
- #12 inbox/messaging
- #13 scoped bot
- #20 explorer/tenant console

Thứ tự chi tiết theo dependency từng issue; **không dùng #15 như product dependency graph**.

---

## 9. Migration / archive ownership

#15 là **migration ledger**, không phải epic sản phẩm thứ hai. Nó theo dõi:

- capability nào từ Votable cần absorb/reimplement;
- phần nào từ legacy EvoBase/archive chỉ dùng làm reference;
- mapping identity/data/package cần giữ;
- readiness trước khi xóa Votable khỏi `vot-workspace`;
- source/license/provenance.

Archive code không được port chỉ vì “đã tồn tại”. Chỉ reuse khi phù hợp contracts hiện tại.

---

## 10. Non-goals

- Một SQL table/controller/repository riêng bắt buộc cho mỗi logical table/app.
- Domain Money/Order/Pay/Ship trở thành common core.
- Builder cho chạy arbitrary SQL/JS/Rust như mặc định.
- Tuyên bố database-per-tenant là hard isolation tuyệt đối.
- Tuyên bố exactly-once external delivery.
- Bắt user biết Rust/SQL để tạo app.
- Dùng AI/chatbot làm authority hoặc tự sửa policy.

---

## 11. Acceptance của vision

- [ ] Hai AppSpecs nghiệp vụ **không liên quan nhau** chạy qua cùng Builder/core/storage contract/Runtime mà không thêm domain-specific controller/repository branch.
- [ ] Stable IDs giữ nghĩa qua rename/reorder/import/export; invalid/cross-scope Ref bị chặn.
- [ ] Cùng AppSpec qua codec/local/hosted adapters cho cùng supported semantics.
- [ ] Local profile chạy được không cần hosted account; hosted sync revalidates authority.
- [ ] Thay đổi logical schema không bắt buộc business DDL tại mỗi thao tác Builder.
- [ ] Storage adapters vượt cùng conformance suite; benchmark quyết định physical strategy, không ngược lại.
- [ ] Policy/commands enforce qua actual boundary; retry/CAS/rollback/restart giữ invariants.
- [ ] Preview không tạo external delivery; published release immutable/pinned; migration có impact/recovery.
- [ ] Builder → publish → Runtime tạo được một app hữu dụng bằng UI, không cần Rust/SQL.
- [ ] Votable legacy chỉ được gỡ sau khi #15 chứng minh capability/data migration hoặc explicit disposition.

**Kết luận kiến trúc:** EvoBase sở hữu vision Votable, nhưng nâng nó thành một platform có AppSpec portable và nhiều execution/storage profiles. Hosted SaaS là một profile mạnh; local-first/self-hosted vẫn là first-class.

items.title: [feat]External SQL Server / PostgreSQL data-exchange connector
items.body:
Problem / verified gap

OpenMES already provides ERP-facing REST APIs, reusable import services, production/quality/stock export endpoints, webhooks, scheduled jobs, optional modules, tenant isolation and encrypted integration configuration. Its Laravel database configuration declares PostgreSQL (pgsql) and SQL Server (sqlsrv) drivers. However, application database support is not an external data-exchange connector: the current integration configuration does not provide independent connections to third-party databases, table/column mappings or managed inbound/outbound SQL synchronization. The standard Docker image includes pdo_pgsql, but not the SQL Server client runtime.

Many manufacturing and enterprise applications exchange data through dedicated SQL staging/import/export tables rather than REST APIs. An optional reusable connector for Microsoft SQL Server and PostgreSQL would cover this established integration pattern without introducing vendor-specific logic into OpenMES core.

Competitive context: Ignition/SQL Bridge demonstrates configurable, bidirectional database integration in industrial software. Other MES vendors commonly offer ERP integration, but their public documentation does not necessarily demonstrate a generic SQL mapping designer. The requested feature is deliberately narrower than a general-purpose ETL platform.

Requested delta only

1. External database connections

  • Add an optional external SQL exchange module supporting independently configured Microsoft SQL Server and PostgreSQL connections, separate from the OpenMES application database and allowing multiple named connections per tenant.
  • Reuse Laravel's database abstraction and existing integration/module conventions. Add the missing SQL Server driver and required runtime dependencies for supported server/container builds; reuse the existing PostgreSQL driver. Fail gracefully if a driver is unavailable.
  • Extend configuration only as necessary: connection name, host, port, database, optional schema, credentials, TLS settings, enabled state and Test connection. Store secrets encrypted and never return or log them.
  • Restrict each configured flow to explicitly approved tables/views and columns; use parameterized, bounded statements and least-privilege accounts. Do not offer arbitrary SQL execution or direct writes to OpenMES core tables.

2. Bidirectional exchange via existing OpenMES services

  • Inbound (external SQL → OpenMES): read configured exchange tables/views, map their rows to existing canonical import/domain contracts and reuse current services for supported entities such as work orders, products and materials. Any supported execution feedback must use existing validated production-domain services rather than directly mutating statuses or counters.
  • Outbound (OpenMES → external SQL): send configured data such as work-order details, execution status, produced/rejected quantities and completion information to designated exchange tables using controlled INSERT/UPDATE operations. Reuse existing domain events, exports and models.
  • Introduce a minimal, versionable mapping profile per connection/flow covering source/target table, permitted columns, entity, direction, key mapping, field conversions and any source-defined acknowledgement fields. Do not introduce a generic visual ETL designer or a second ERP/MES domain model.
  • Support external identifiers and a configurable mapping between source records and OpenMES entities; reject ambiguous matches rather than guessing.

3. Reliable incremental synchronization

  • Reuse the existing scheduler/queue to poll inbound tables periodically. Use available domain events for outbound delivery where appropriate, with periodic reconciliation to recover missed events. Database CDC is not required.
  • Persist synchronization progress per tenant, connection, flow and direction. Detect both newly inserted and modified external rows. Support a source-provided modification timestamp/version/processed marker, or a bounded keyed comparison when no reliable cursor exists.
  • Make retries and replays idempotent, including failures after a remote write but before a local checkpoint is committed. Do not advance progress past unsuccessful validation/persistence; isolate and report erroneous rows without blocking unrelated valid records.
  • Make acknowledgement semantics configurable per exchange profile, because a source may own its processed flag while a destination may require an explicit acknowledgement. Never assume that similarly named flags have the same ownership or meaning.
  • Distinguish absolute versus incremental quantities, cumulative versus per-cycle time and known time units. Never double-count confirmations, and do not silently interpret unspecified units.
  • Reuse existing logs/admin UI patterns to expose Test connection, Run now, last run/success, processed/updated/skipped/failed counts and actionable per-row errors. No separate monitoring platform is required.

Generic integration example (illustrative, not a vendor contract)

Direction | External exchange dataset | Expected behavior -- | -- | -- External SQL → OpenMES | WorkOrders_Exchange | Import/update identified work orders and quantities through existing validation services External SQL → OpenMES | Items_Exchange | Import/update products or materials through the existing master-data services OpenMES → external SQL | ProductionResults_Exchange | Write production completions, good/scrap quantities and timestamps without duplicate postings OpenMES → external SQL | WorkOrderStatus_Exchange | Publish current status and relevant external identifiers incrementally

Table names are examples only. Each deployment defines its actual tables, columns, keys and field meanings in its mapping profile. The connector must not assume that a sheet, machine cycle, operation or batch always corresponds to exactly one work order; only map execution quantities or time where the source identifies the corresponding OpenMES entity unambiguously.

Acceptance criteria

  • Both PostgreSQL and SQL Server external connections work from supported OpenMES deployments; missing drivers, invalid credentials and TLS errors are handled safely.
  • An authorized administrator can configure, test, enable/disable and manually run a tenant-isolated connection without exposing secrets.
  • A configured external table imports or updates a supported work order or master-data entity through an existing OpenMES service, preserving its validation and audit rules.
  • A configured destination table receives production or work-order data without duplicate records after retry, replay or restart.
  • Changes to an existing external row are detected, not only newly inserted keys; checkpoints and acknowledgements advance only after successful processing.
  • Field mapping supports stable external identifiers and explicitly configured numeric/time semantics; ambiguous identifiers or unknown time units result in a validation error, not a guessed posting.
  • Failed rows remain diagnosable/retryable; logs show run status and useful counts without credentials or sensitive SQL payloads.
  • Cross-tenant reads, writes and configuration access are denied.
  • Automated tests cover both database engines, restart/retry/idempotency, updated-row detection, acknowledgement ownership, cumulative metrics and tenant isolation; existing ERP API, production, stock and machine-connector regression tests remain green.

Explicitly out of scope

  • Replacing the existing ERP REST API or reimplementing its domain rules.
  • Building packaged connectors for specific ERP, nesting or machine-software vendors.
  • Introducing a general-purpose ETL platform, drag-and-drop SQL designer, arbitrary SQL scripting endpoint or mandatory ODBC/JDBC abstraction.
  • Implementing database CDC, distributed transactions across the two databases or guaranteed exactly-once transport. Achieve effectively-once business effects through idempotent application logic.
  • Inventing stock/accounting postings, shared-batch allocation rules or execution measurements not provided unambiguously by the source contract.

Relevant baseline and benchmark references

  • OpenMES release baseline: https://github.com/Mes-Open/OpenMes/releases/tag/v0.27.0
  • Existing ERP interface: https://github.com/Mes-Open/OpenMes/issues/21
  • Existing ERP and warehouse integration: https://github.com/Mes-Open/OpenMes/blob/v0.27.0/docs/warehouse-erp-rollout.md
  • Current driver configuration: https://github.com/Mes-Open/OpenMes/blob/v0.27.0/backend/config/database.php
  • Current Docker extensions: https://github.com/Mes-Open/OpenMes/blob/v0.27.0/backend/Dockerfile
  • Ignition external database connections: https://docs.inductiveautomation.com/docs/8.3/platform/database-connections

items.title: [Storage] Storage contract + local embedded profile + hosted isolation spikes · EvoBase
items.body:
## Product/storage correction — 03/10/2026

Votable vision đã được hấp thụ vào EvoBase. Issue này **không còn được hiểu là “chọn fixed-layout PostgreSQL làm storage của EvoBase”**. Nó sở hữu **storage contract + conformance**, sau đó mới đo các adapter/profile.

Thứ tự đúng:

1. **Storage contract/conformance:** facts, Ref, constraints, revision/CAS, atomic mutation, receipt/outbox, scan/query budgets.
2. **Local/embedded profile:** adapter nhẹ cho local-first/offline/self-hosted; không cần hosted tenant registry để chạy.
3. **Hosted PostgreSQL spikes:** fixed-layout là candidate; database-per-tenant/schema/shared+RLS là isolation candidates cần benchmark/ADR.
4. **Optional compiled relational adapter:** chỉ ở publish/migration boundary nếu cần hiệu năng; không đổi AppSpec semantics.

Yêu cầu sản phẩm là **logical config không bắt buộc business DDL ở mỗi thao tác Builder**. Physical layout là quyết định của adapter.

## Phạm vi và trạng thái

Thiết kế/skills/PR prompts theo [vision #1](https://github.com/loveoverflowcom/evobase/issues/1). **Chưa triển khai sản phẩm.** Leptos web, CMP mobile và Rust backend là stack đích; lượt này chỉ chuẩn bị design và các PR nhỏ để làm tuần tự. Prototype có dữ liệu mẫu, không auth/backend/SQL/provider thật.

Đo fixed-layout engine store và database-per-tenant, giữ lựa chọn ADR chưa settled production.

## Preview M3 Expressive

Desktop: static design frame, không phải browser screenshot.

![tenant-ops desktop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/loveoverflowcom/evobase/6ae452f144e49f8aaa5f8d5fb6b3e681c4c4ef6e/design/m3-expressive/previews/tenant-ops-desktop.png)

<details>
<summary>Compact/mobile reference (target anatomy, không phải native CMP evidence)</summary>

![tenant-ops mobile](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/loveoverflowcom/evobase/6ae452f144e49f8aaa5f8d5fb6b3e681c4c4ef6e/design/m3-expressive/previews/tenant-ops-mobile.png)

</details>

## Gói đính kèm nhẹ, pin cố định

- [Tải source ZIP của riêng issue này](https://github.com/loveoverflowcom/evobase/blob/6ae452f144e49f8aaa5f8d5fb6b3e681c4c4ef6e/design/m3-expressive/packages/evobase-05-hosted-isolation-source.zip?raw=true), 95,814 bytes

- ZIP gồm editable SVG, HTML/CSS/MJS fixture, canonical tokens, fonts, Apache 2.0 license/notice và component/accessibility contracts. Source ZIP không chứa raster; PNG representative ở trên, mọi màn có SVG bên dưới. Expanded PNG review packs được bàn giao riêng; không dùng private download URL trong issue công khai.

- Design pin: `6ae452f144e49f8aaa5f8d5fb6b3e681c4c4ef6e`; blue-family curated roles, không khẳng định HCT output/official Material compliance

### Màn thuộc gói

## Thứ tự PR và prompts

1. [060-isolated-fixed-store.md](https://github.com/loveoverflowcom/evobase/blob/ed2536c3a2e976e53aafc07a4c52c895f7ecbfa1/docs/work-plan/060-isolated-fixed-store.md)

Prompt pin: `ed2536c3a2e976e53aafc07a4c52c895f7ecbfa1`. Làm từng PR đúng boundary, review gate trước bước tiếp theo; gói02 tách kernel rồi grid, gói06 tách release rồi evolution. Không gộp rewrite toàn platform vào một PR. [Skill/prompt plan](https://github.com/loveoverflowcom/evobase/blob/ed2536c3a2e976e53aafc07a4c52c895f7ecbfa1/docs/work-plan/README.md).

## Dependencies

Storage contract + local adapter có thể bắt đầu sau #4/#5 và codec/core gates. Hosted isolation/authority acceptance cần #6. Release/evolution nối #8; API/tenant evidence nối #18/#20/#21.

Không bắt local-first profile đợi hosted auth, connector, messaging hoặc chatbot. Fixed-layout/database-per-tenant chỉ được chốt sau conformance + benchmark/ADR.

## Acceptance trước khi bật capability

- [ ] Hai tenant DB + provisioner/runtime role separation; runtime no DDL/BYPASSRLS
- [ ] Thêm logical table/optional field/Ref/publish không business SQL DDL; actual catalog evidence
- [ ] Records/edges/index/unique/revision/outbox atomic; concurrency/restart/failure vectors
- [ ] Tenant negative tests gồm API/Ref/cache/subscription/blob/log/bot; resource/latency measurements + support envelope ADR

## Prompt thực hiện sau khi được yêu cầu code

Đọc linked PR prompt và skills liên quan trước; đối chiếu design pin/vision/current source. Chỉ implement scope của PR kế tiếp, giữ canonical token identity và stable IDs. Đề xuất/chốt ADR qua review gate, cùng unsupported subset ở gate cần thiết, không biến fixture thành lời hứa feature đã chạy. Báo rõ passed/failed/not-run với commit/build/scenario; source→adapter→mounted consumer, web/native CMP và simulated/real provider phải là bằng chứng riêng. Dừng ở draft PR để review; không merge/deploy/default-branch switch, live migration hay legacy retirement.

## Evidence và giới hạn

250 checks là static source/ZIP/hash/contrast checks trên design kit; reviewer đã kiểm anatomy/light-dark/navigation/font provenance. Không phải Leptos browser interaction, native CMP Android/iOS, Rust/storage conformance, benchmark hay provider pass. Builder compact là summary; Runtime mobile là target native anatomy. 1:1/N:M/migration/offline/provider capabilities chỉ bật sau ADR/conformance, chưa coi là baseline đã hỗ trợ.


<!-- evobase-archive-gap-plan-2026-10-03:start -->
## Kế hoạch registry/storage dùng chung — 03/10/2026

Theo [Vision #1](https://github.com/loveoverflowcom/evobase/issues/1); [#15](https://github.com/loveoverflowcom/evobase/issues/15) chỉ theo dõi migration/disposition, tái sử dụng lessons registry/provisioning/CAS/event persistence của archive; không restore OrderRepository/UserRepository/demo tables làm common data model.

**PR-A:** durable tenant/app registry và idempotent provisioning operation identity; persisted progress/ready/failure, restart/retry/recovery. Separate provisioner/migrator/runtime privileges/credentials, verified scope selects binding.

**PR-B:** fixed-store executor consume generic checked writes/event intents (#17/#18). Canonical facts/derived structures/CAS/pin/revision/audit/outbox/receipt atomic; current authority trước replay/commit. Archive transition và publish riêng operations là failure case cần sửa, không implementation để copy.

**PR-C:** real two-tenant/no-DDL/catalog/races/failure-injection/restart/resource measurements; #20 operator status projection, #8 release/evolution.

- [ ] Hai unrelated app schemas dùng cùng fixed store, không thêm business SQL table/repository per app.
- [ ] Registry/provision failure/retry giữ một consistent operation/binding; runtime không dùng admin privilege.
- [ ] Revoked/raced authority và stale CAS reject; state/event/receipt rollback cùng nhau.
- [ ] #21 chỉ stream committed authorized events; invalid writes không phát events.

Sau #6 và supported core gates; không migrate production hoặc chạy DB/CI trong lượt kế hoạch.
<!-- evobase-archive-gap-plan-2026-10-03:end -->

items.title: Fivetran lineage binds same-named tables to the first service in dbServiceNames
items.body:
### Connector

Fivetran

### Feature area

Lineage

### Describe the bug

When several services in `lineageInformation.dbServiceNames` hold a table with the same database, schema and name, the Fivetran connector attaches every connector's lineage to the first listed service.

`_resolve_table` in `pipeline/fivetran/metadata.py` loops over `dbServiceNames` in order and returns the first service where `<service>.<database or *>.<schema>.<table>` exists. It never uses which source the Fivetran connector actually reads from. Sharded or per-tenant estates, where several databases share one schema, are the common case.

In our instance six MySQL services hold the same `evo` schema, one per Fivetran connector. With all six in one agent's `dbServiceNames`, all six connectors' 273 table edges were attached to the first service. Nothing was logged and the run reported success.

### To Reproduce

1. Two database services, A and B, each with table `db.schema.t`.
2. Two Fivetran connectors, one syncing from A and one from B.
3. A Fivetran agent with `dbServiceNames: [A, B]`.
4. Both connectors' lineage originates from A.

### Expected behavior

The source service is chosen from the Fivetran connector's own source (for example its configured host, or its database/service type), or the ambiguity is reported and the edge skipped rather than bound to the first match.

Our workaround is one Fivetran agent per source service, each with a `pipelineFilterPattern` and only its own service in `dbServiceNames`.

### OS

Kubernetes (ingestion-base image)

### Python version

3.12

### OpenMetadata version

2.0.6

### OpenMetadata Ingestion package version

openmetadata-ingestion==2.0.1.0; same logic on main.

### Pre-submission checklist

- [x] I searched for duplicate issues.
- [x] I removed credentials, hostnames, emails, and other sensitive data from logs and config.

items.title: Roadmap: modular ERP and business-process library for Effect
items.body:
effect-biz is a comprehensive, modular ERP and business-process library for Effect 4, built to be **embedded in other applications**: each business domain is a package of Effect services that a host app composes with the layers it chooses.

This issue is the plan of record. Its sub-issues are the area epics, and each epic's sub-issues are the slices. Decisions recorded here (body or later comments) override anything older; `AGENTS.md` mirrors them. This body consolidates every decision up to 2026-10-29, including the **merge of effect-finance into this repository**.

## Owner decisions

| Topic | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| effect-finance | **Merged into this repository** (migration done in a separate session). Payments, ledger, chart of accounts, journals, invoices, bills, credit notes, AR/AP, tax, fixed-asset depreciation, budgets and financial reports are packages here. Finance work is tracked by the Finance epic #111. |
| Package boundaries | **Full merge, no boundary**: any package may import any other (no cycles). Finance documents reference parties and products **directly** rather than through snapshots. The finance-bridge package is dropped; cross-module flows are ordinary event subscribers and direct service calls (#18). |
| Master data | One set of parties and one catalogue serve both the operational and the finance modules. |
| Persistence | Ports + in-memory + `@effect/sql` layers. **Postgres and Cloudflare D1 are both production dialects**; SQLite for tests/embedded. Commands are *load → decide → commit one atomic batch of version-guarded writes* (#128); optional Durable Object coordinator for hot keys (#143). |
| Tenancy | **One** tenant + multi-company context for every package, finance included. Shared database or one database per tenant via `TenantDatabase` (#129). Independent of effect-auth Organizations. |
| Integration | Typed domain events + transactional outbox; idempotent subscribers; durable `effect/workflow`. External delivery as CloudEvents via webhooks, Cloudflare Queues, SNS/SQS, Kafka, NATS (Distilled-based cloud adapters, Alchemy resources) (#120). |
| Surfaces | Services + **JSON:API v1.1 HttpApi groups (effect-jsonapi)** + `effect/rpc` groups. `effect-biz-client` with typed clients and legation resources (#131). No UI. No MCP/AI integration for now. |
| Authorisation | effect-auth's `Authorizer` (#130); no RBAC or authentication of our own. |
| Money | An exact `Money`/`Currency` type built here, in core or the finance foundation, before catalogue pricing (#25, #111). |
| Commercial | Document currency + base-currency amounts at the captured rate; inventory valued in base currency; tax-inclusive or exclusive pricing per list/document; `SalesChannel` port + Shopify connector (#133, #134); inter-company transactions (#144); recurring contracts (#147). |
| Documents & reporting | Typed document data + optional HTML/PDF renderer (#137); event-fed report projections with a typed query API (#138); analytic dimensions through to journal lines (#152). |
| Privacy | Personal-data annotations, subject export, anonymisation with legal holds, retention, sensitive-access log (#140). |
| Import | Import framework + migrators for Xero, MYOB, Shopify, Odoo/ERPNext, including financial history (#139). |
| Localisation | Neutral core; **Australia first** (#17). |
| Payroll | Calculation, journals and export; no ATO lodgement. |
| Runtimes | Node 22+ and Cloudflare Workers for every server package (#142). |
| Consumer | No first consuming app; the example host app (#23) is the integration spec. |
| Releases | npm under `@thomasfosterau/effect-biz*`, **all packages version in lockstep** (one Changesets `fixed` group). The merged `@thomasfosterau/effect-payments*` packages are **renamed** into the `effect-biz-*` family, so they fall inside the lockstep group; the exact names are settled in the migration work. |
| Sequencing | Foundation → Party + Catalogue → Sales → Purchasing + Inventory → the rest (order in the first comment); finance packages slot in alongside, per #111. |

## Planned packages

| Package | Area |
| --- | --- |
| `@thomasfosterau/effect-biz` | Foundation: ids, decimals, Money, tenancy, errors, repositories, events/outbox, numbering, localisation ports, authorisation helpers, reports, privacy, import framework, documents data, dimensions |
| `-sql` | `@effect/sql` infrastructure for Postgres, D1, SQLite |
| `-workflow` | Durable workflows and approvals |
| `-party`, `-catalogue`, `-sales`, `-purchasing`, `-inventory`, `-manufacturing`, `-crm`, `-hr`, `-projects`, `-payroll`, `-service`, `-assets`, `-pos`, `-quality`, `-field-service` | Operational modules |
| Finance packages (from effect-finance) | Payments, renamed from `effect-payments*` into the `effect-biz-*` family (core + Stripe, PayPal, Airwallex), plus the ledger, invoicing, AR/AP, tax, budgets and fixed-asset modules planned in #111 |
| `-au` | Australian localisation (operational and finance rules) |
| `-webhooks`, `-cloudflare`, `-aws`, `-kafka`, `-nats` | Event delivery adapters |
| `-alchemy` | Alchemy infrastructure resources |
| `-documents` | HTML/PDF rendering |
| `-client` | Typed clients + legation resources |
| `-shopify` | Sales channel connector |
| `-docusign`, `-dropbox-sign` | E-signature adapters |
| `-import-*` | Migrators |

Each domain package follows one layout: `src/<Entity>.ts`, `src/<Entity>Repository.ts`, `src/Memory.ts`, `src/Sql.ts` + migrations, `src/HttpApi.ts`, `src/Rpc.ts`, `src/Events.ts`, plus a client-safe `src/Api.ts` for definitions.

## Label note

`needs-effect-finance` now means **depends on a finance module in this repository** (#111), not on another repository.

items.title: Performance: establish speed, efficiency and scalability as product contracts

milestone.title: Operate
milestone.description: Operate milestone: daily-use governed AI capabilities (search, assistant, scenarios, verticals), SME enablement, editions boundary, and close-out of all open Platform/Enterprise items. Plan: docs/plans/2026-07-11-operate-milestone.md

items.body:
Parent: #352

## Outcome
Make speed and resource efficiency measurable product properties across SME single-node, managed enterprise and private-cloud deployment profiles.

## Principles
- Set budgets before optimizing.
- Measure p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, errors, CPU, memory, database pressure and per-tenant fairness.
- Do not trade correctness, auditability or tenant isolation for headline throughput.

## Child slices
<!-- axis-audit-children -->
- [ ] #361 — Performance: define workload profiles, SLOs and a reproducible baseline
- [ ] #362 — Performance: close database transactions before external model and workflow awaits
- [ ] #363 — Performance: enforce query budgets, pagination and index evidence
- [ ] #364 — Performance: reduce connector console request fan-out with a scoped read model
- [ ] #365 — Performance: benchmark ingestion streaming, concurrency and backpressure

## Done when
Representative workloads run reproducibly in CI or a controlled performance environment, regressions have budgets, and operators can diagnose bottlenecks.

items.title: [cluster] A project parameter cannot be bound from the TenantSpec, and the spec creates no users
items.body:
### What happens

Managed tenants are the right tool for "one database per customer" (`TenantSpec`, idempotent `createTenant`, refusals as results, durable `waitReady`), but:

- **Parameters**: `configuration.parameters` creates the `mailer` connector in the tenant's registry, but the project's `mailer` parameter stays "(not bound)". There is no binding by name (checked for a connector and for a plain value), and `GET /tenant/configuration` has no section for bindings. So each end customer has a manual step in their portal.
- **Users**: the spec only creates the invited admin; users and their roles per project must be added by hand in each tenant.
- `inviteAdmin()`: it is not said whether the link is emailed to the customer or must be passed on by the operator.
- There is no documentation of managed tenants at all: everything came from `cluster.d.ts` (well commented).

### Expected

`projects: [{ name, package, parameters: { mailer: { ref: 'mailer' } } }]` in `TenantSpec`, or an implicit binding to a registry entry of the same name and type; `users: [{ email, roles: { app: ['Accountant'] } }]`; a documentation page "selling an app as SaaS / multi-tenant".

### Environment

```text
Codenotch CLI
- CLI version: 1.2.3
- Node.js version: v25.9.0
- Platform: win32 x64
Codenotch runtime
- Version: v1.2.3
```

items.title: Roadmap: Elsa Control + Cloud after first-public Hosted
items.body:
[Codex control room] On behalf of @sfmskywalker.

## Current delivery control (4 Nov 2026)

#83 owns the full accepted program and its current integration queue. #508 remains the first delivery boundary and is NO-GO. Accepted outcomes below remain in scope; the 20 Oct freeze in #868 controls their start. #629 is an accepted design spike, while the customer-built-image Phase4 build is explicitly uncommitted under the [4 Oct owner decision](https://github.com/valence-works/elsa-control/issues/629#issuecomment-5982135076) until a later owner build decision. That candidate remains visible and is not silently dropped. Native dependency edges now encode #508 before #731, #633, #629, #795 and Elsa 4 build #872–#874. Implementation, merge, deployment, live acceptance and operational handover are separate gates.

_Posted by Elsa Control Architect (Grok Bot) on behalf of the Elsa Control team._

Refs #83, #508

This is the order of work after the first public Hosted launch, with dependencies, across Elsa Control, Elsa Cloud, the connector and the runtime image. It re-sequences the "Later phases" in `docs/product/delivery-roadmap.md`, because the founder decisions of 4 Oct (#436 and #633 raised to P1; #629 scope extended) pull BYO and the shared tier ahead of #131/#132/#133. The GitHub Project and native issue relationships stay authoritative for live status.

## Guiding principle

Elsa Control should make it easy for IT operations and DevOps teams to get Elsa deployed, and Elsa Cloud runs on top of it. Every phase below has to make an operator's or a pipeline's job simpler on one of three deployment targets:

1. **Our Hosted** (Valence-operated, in our customer-workload subscription, ADR-0016).
2. **The customer's BYO Azure subscription** (Valence operates through Azure Lighthouse: #430/#433/#434/#435 done, #436 open).
3. **Customer-run engines through the connector** (#499; customer operates, Control observes).

Standing rules this roadmap keeps:
- Cloud is the customer product and the Control Console is an operator tool. Cloud never proxies the Console. A customer need becomes a purpose-built Control endpoint on the Cloud BFF allowlist, with its own authorization and tests, added only when a real need exists.
- Connected and customer-built engines top out at `SelfReported` evidence (#499 condition A, #614). They are never shown as "verified". The connector `displayName` is a label only.
- The connector is outbound-only. Control never dials into customer networks.
- Control PRs merge under the applicable current Control gate in `AGENTS.md` and `.github/reviewers.md`: the normal exact-head Code Review gate or the explicitly authorized availability/self-merge conditions. Required-green exact-head CI, main freshness and pinned sequential merges remain mandatory. Live proofs go through QA. This follows the later owner decision recorded by #868; it does not waive acceptance. PRs in other repositories follow their own current instructions and authority; the Control exception is not transferred to Hub PRs.
- Azure spend matters: the ideal ceiling is €500/month; the current figure is being reconciled by the CEO (#672) and isn't quoted here. Costs below are "unmeasured estimate" unless a measured figure is cited.

## Three targets, one model

We build one set of foundations. Each target is a configuration of them, not a parallel architecture (ADR-0007).

| Foundation | Hosted (Dedicated / Shared) | BYO Azure | Connected engine |
|---|---|---|---|
| **F1 Deployment target and placement.** An instance records *where* it runs without provider IDs leaking into intent (ADR-0007). Assignments are fingerprinted and never silently retargeted (ADR-0016). | Dedicated: per-instance resources in the Valence workload subscription. Shared: a tenant placed on a shard (#633; placement record #352). | Per-org/per-assignment subscription overlay (#436), Lighthouse bind (#434) | No placement; a connection record (#481/#489) |
| **F2 Image catalog, provenance and trust levels** (ADR-0015 cosign verification; `VerifiedManifest` / `SupportedRelease` / `SelfReported`) | Governed Valence Runtime image (`VerifiedManifest`) | Same Valence image (cross-tenant AcrPull, #430 P3). Later, customer-built images (#629), always `SelfReported` | Always `SelfReported` (#614) |
| **F3 Desired-state and revision model** (ADR-0007 resolved plan; #340 promotion contract; Phase 3 epic) | Provider applies image/infra; the engine applies config and workflows | Same as Hosted | The connector applies config and workflows; never infra or image |
| **F4 Telemetry and health** (#266, #632 uptime, connector heartbeat) | Per instance. Shared: per shard, reported per tenant (#633 Q5) | Per instance, in the customer subscription | Heartbeat only (15 s default, #614) |
| **F5 Billing hooks** (entitlement snapshot + commercial gate; providers `stripe` / `internal` / `azure-bound` #435; `MaxInstances` #502) | Stripe plans; Shared needs per-tenant quotas (#349) | `azure-bound`; Azure bill ≠ Elsa fee | Plan and entitlement per #406/#484 |

### Where #633 (Shared) and #436 (BYO) share foundations
- **F1:** both are "place this instance somewhere other than the default per-instance Valence resources". #436's overlay and #633's shard placement should be two kinds of the same placement record. They must not be two separate code paths in the provider runner.
- **F2:** both run the same governed Valence Runtime image and catalog.
- **F5:** both go through the same commercial gate and entitlement snapshot. Only the provider (BYO) or the quota profile (Shared) differs.
- **F4:** the same lifecycle telemetry and uptime model (#632).
- **Customer view:** the same Cloud views (#625/#631); the placement kind is a field, not a new page.

### Where they diverge
- **Isolation boundary.** BYO uses **subscription isolation**: the blast radius stays in the customer's subscription and the customer pays Azure. Shared uses **tenant isolation inside one Elsa process and database**: logical isolation only, so ADR-0009 forbids arbitrary customer packages and custom images (#633 Q8).
- **Lifecycle.** BYO provisions a full instance per customer, as today, just in a different subscription. Shared provisions a tenant inside an existing shard: no Azure resources per customer, one Elsa version per shard, and moves between Shared and Dedicated need data migration (#633 Q3).
- **Cost to us.** BYO adds near-zero Valence Azure spend per customer, apart from ops time and registry pull (unmeasured estimate). Shared adds a shard (recurring, unmeasured estimate) but lowers the cost per customer.
- **Threats.** Shared needs the #110-derived gates, the two-org negative matrix (#348) and the noisy-neighbour exercise (#350). BYO needs least-privilege Lighthouse roles (#434, RBAC narrowing path in the #430 spike doc).

## Sizes

The repo defines `size:S` (under one day of agent work with review), `size:M` (1–3 days) and `size:L` (3–7 days; larger must be split). There is no `size:XL` label. Here **XL means "larger than L; must be split into L-or-smaller leaves before arming."** Sizes on unsized issues are estimates.

## Phases

### Phase 0: Finish the first-public Hosted launch (#508), P0
- **Goal:** #508 GO, with every acceptance row proven and none waived.
- **Issues (open blockers named in #508's sub-issues and the 4 Oct Issue Bus mirrors):**
  - **Row 13** (compatible and incompatible release states + rollback): #719 / #720 / #723 / #727, PR #728, plus elsa-cloud#144/#146 for no-forward. After merge it needs a fresh staging freeze and QA in both fixture modes. #730 is filed and closed for its recorded staging pairs, including Control 234→233→234. That proof does not apply to a new pair. Current #508 row 13 remains Unproven, with #781 and Hub update-state QA still pending; use the living matrix for the remaining acceptance.
  - **Row 8** (confirmed Delete → provider absence → tombstone → reusable allowance): needs the final-rehearsal Create plus clean Delete, with provider reads (#508 comment 5973823967).
  - **Row 26** alert: #657 (+ #659).
  - Recovery: #601 / #603. Delete/UI: #602, #605, #548, #549, #670.
  - Billing: #669 live proof, #684. Studio permissions: #565 + elsa-production-image#73 (QA Combined hold). Workspace: #667.
- **Dependencies:** none upstream. Everything else waits on it.
- **Spike vs build:** build and QA live proof. #719 is the only spike.
- **Size:** remaining leaves are S/M. #508 itself is `size:M`.
- **Cost:** bounded staging windows only. No new paid capacity.
- **Exit criteria:** all #508 acceptance criteria checked. The go/no-go and remaining Preview limits are recorded on #459 and #122.

### Phase 1: P1 foundations and spikes (parallel tracks, start at #508 GO)
The 20 Oct owner decision (#868) supersedes the earlier design-work exception: these tracks, including their design work, wait for #508 GO. The only freeze exception is Elsa 4 managed-readiness design #870/#871; build #872–#874 waits for GO.

**1A. BYO Azure: finish and prove (#436).**
- **Goal:** create an instance in a customer's subscription through Lighthouse, without breaking the ADR-0016 Valence default.
- **Issues:**
  - #436: per-org overlay; preflight that works with Lighthouse identities (the identity can live in the Valence subscription); no silent retarget.
  - Done foundations: #430, #433, #434, #435.
  - Design-partner live proof #740 under #436; its post-GO and subscription/cost-decision gates remain open.
- **Dependencies:** Phase 0. 1D is written inside #436's scoping pass.
- **Spike vs build:** build. A short scoping pass comes first (#436 comment, 4 Oct).
- **Size:** L (#436) plus a scoping pass (S) and a live proof (M).
- **Cost:** the live proof runs in the partner's or a scratch subscription. If the scratch subscription is Valence-owned, it's new spend (unmeasured estimate). The customer subscription pays its own Azure bill.
- **Exit criteria:**
  - #436 AC1–AC6 pass.
  - One live create → Ready → Open Studio → confirmed Delete in a customer subscription, with bind `Active` and an `azure-bound` entitlement.
  - Copy stays guided / design-partner, Preview with no SLO, and says "Azure bill ≠ Elsa fee".
  - The Cloud surface is only the existing waitlist, plus BFF endpoints if a real design partner needs them.

**1B. Shared entry tier spike (#633).**
- **Goal:** the #633 deliverable: an Architect decision record covering the tenancy model (database per tenant vs. shared database), a go/no-go on Elsa 3 multitenancy readiness, cost per tenant and a leaf breakdown.
- **Dependencies:** start after #508 GO under #868, including design. A live measurement also needs cost clearance.
- **Spike vs build:** spike. **Size:** M (estimate; unsized).
- **Cost:** design-only, zero Azure spend. Any measurement shard needs CEO cost clearance.
- **Exit criteria:** answers to all of #633's questions 1–8; a recommended tenancy model; a statement of whether the tenant is an Elsa Instance with a placement kind (recommended, which keeps Cloud/BFF unchanged) or a new resource type; cost per tenant under the ceiling; pricing inputs handed to Sipke.

**1C. Connector L4–L7 (#499).**
- **Goal:** a supported, published connector, with the public pairing gate (#609) lifted.
- **Issues:** #615 (L4 rotate/revoke/re-pair) → #616 (L5 nuget.org trusted publishing, SBOM, guide) → #617 (L6 #485 matrix live, QA) → #618 (L7 lift the #609 gate). L1–L3 are done (#612, #613, #614). Architecture: `Connector.Core` plus `Connector.Elsa3` now, `Connector.Elsa4` later (#499 comment, 28 Sep). The Elsa 4 adapter is filed as #873 under #869; build waits for its capability contract, connector prerequisites and #508 GO.
- **Dependencies:** start after #508 GO under #868, then follow #615→#616→#617→#618 and worker capacity.
- **Spike vs build:** build. **Size:** L total (estimate; leaves unsized).
- **Cost:** L6's live runtimes can run outside Azure (unmeasured estimate). No author-signing certificate (deferred because it costs money, #499).
- **Exit criteria:** #499's AC met. Customer-built hosts are labelled `SelfReported`.

**1D. Shared foundations note: deployment target and placement model (#739, inside #436's scoping pass).**
- **Goal:** one placement abstraction (F1) that #436's overlay and #633's shard placement both use. It also says how F2/F5 extend for both.
- **Dependencies:** start after #508 GO under #868, inside #436's scoping pass. **Spike vs build:** design (ADR amendment or short ADR). **Size:** S–M.
- **Exit criteria:** an ADR merged under the applicable current Control gate in `AGENTS.md` / `.github/reviewers.md`, with required-green exact-head CI and fresh main. #436's leaf references it. The #633 decision record conforms to it.

**1E. Customer-built image spike (#629, including Sipke's 4 Oct scenario).** Designed together with #633 as one tiered offer: Shared / Dedicated / Custom image.
- **Goal:** answer #629's questions, including the 4 Oct ones: is it useful, which pipeline integration, the minimum host contract, and where it sits.
- **Architect position going in:**
  - **Useful for a specific segment:** .NET teams that already build their own ASP.NET Core host with the Elsa packages and custom activities. Today managed hosting gives them nothing (#406: arbitrary images unsupported).
  - **Against "just use your own pipeline":** if they only want "run my container", their pipeline wins. Control adds value when they want:
    - the tested Elsa topology in their subscription (SQL, identity, Key Vault, Container Apps via our Bicep);
    - lifecycle (health, recovery, confirmed delete);
    - Studio handoff;
    - compatibility checks;
    - one view next to Hosted and connected engines;
    - later, promotion across environments.
  - **Overlap:** a customer can already self-deploy and attach the connector (`SelfReported`). #629's differentiator is that Control owns the infrastructure lifecycle in their subscription.
- **What the build would take:**
  1. **Pipeline:** the customer's CI pushes the image to their own ACR in the BYO subscription. A CI step or GitHub Action calls a Control API with the image digest plus an SBOM/provenance attestation reference. Control registers a "customer image release" (`SelfReported`) and sets the desired revision. The provider deploys it into the BYO subscription, pulling by digest with the workload identity's AcrPull on the customer ACR (same tenant).
     - Rejected for now: **Control builds from source** (supply-chain risk, build compute on us, ADR-0009).
     - Rejected for now: **a Valence-owned registry per workspace** (cost, registry authority #284).
     - Pipeline authentication should prefer workload-identity federation over long-lived tokens. The spike decides.
  2. **Minimum host contract:** health endpoint; configuration/env contract; secrets via managed identity and Key Vault references only; Studio handoff (#127) optional; connector package (#613) **required** so Control gets status and the Phase 3 channel.
  3. **Compatibility contract checks:** Elsa version within the supported range, connector protocol supported, health contract answered. Any failure blocks deploy (fail closed).
  4. **Lifecycle:** create, restart, delete and recovery as for BYO. **No Valence release updates**, because the customer owns upgrades. Rollback means redeploying the previous digest revision.
  5. **Trust and copy:** always `SelfReported` / "customer image", never "verified".
- **Dependencies:** the design spike starts after #508 GO under #868. **The build depends on BYO (1A)**, F2, and the Phase 3 revision contract.
- **Spike vs build:** spike only (no build commitment, per Sipke). **Size:** M (estimate).
- **Exit criteria:** a design note on #629 (decision, rejected alternatives, constraints, deferred items, build leaves), plus a pricing-shape proposal for Sipke (#629 CEO comment).

### Phase 2: Shared high-density entry tier, build (#633 leaves, to file from the 1B decision record)
- **Goal:** a low-price entry tier or trial on shared shards using Elsa tenants.
- **Issues:** leaves to file from #633. They reuse #349 (capacity profiles and quotas), #352 (stamp placement and capacity accounting), #348 (two-org negative matrix), #350 (noisy-neighbour exercise), #632 (uptime per shard, reported per tenant), #625/#631 (Cloud views).
- **Dependencies:** Phase 0 GO; #633 go; 1D; Sipke's pricing, trial-limit and SLA calls.
- **Spike vs build:** build. **Size:** XL (must be split).
- **Cost:** one shard is new recurring spend (unmeasured estimate). It must be shown to fit the €500 ceiling, or to replace per-trial Dedicated spend, before provisioning.
- **Exit criteria:**
  - #110-derived threat gates pass, including the #348 and #350 exercises.
  - Built-in packages only (ADR-0009).
  - Per-tenant quotas enforced.
  - A tested Shared → Dedicated move.
  - Truthful Cloud copy.
  - Measured cost per tenant recorded.

### Phase 3: Desired-state delivery to engines (configuration + workflow definitions), epic #731
**Goal:** Control pushes configuration and workflow definitions to connected engines and to managed engines (Hosted and BYO) through **one** desired-state path, without breaking the outbound-only trust model.

**Current state (what this builds on):**
- The connector only reports status and opens Studio. Its capabilities are `connection.status` and `studio.open` (#499 design); it has no Control-to-connector commands (#614, deferred).
- Control already has desired-state revisions and immutable artifacts (ADR-0007).
- Control has a workflow artifact runtime applier with an apply journal for exactly-once application (#32, closed).
- Control has a durable poll / claim / lease / report command channel (ADR-0004; #318 extends it).
- #500 (governed artifact deployment to external engines) and #501 (runtime controls) are open and blocked behind #484's separate permissions (`ExecuteDeployment` / `ExecuteControls`).
- #731 and its filed leaves #732–#738 cover configuration delivery and managed-engine parity; they remain accepted work, not a delivered capability.

**Design constraints (this epic's contract):**
- **Pull, never push.** Control publishes a desired revision. The connector learns the current desired revision pointer on its heartbeat (15 s default), fetches the bundle over its authenticated outbound connection (bound to org / workspace / connection / runner lease, #635), applies it through the host adapter, and reports the applied revision and result. No inbound port, and Control never dials the engine.
- **Signed, content-hashed, versioned bundles.** A bundle has a monotonic revision id per engine, a parent revision, a content digest over canonical content, an item list (kind / id / digest), and a Control signature whose key id is separate from the handoff key (#318). The connector verifies signature and digest before applying.
- **Allowlisted content only:** workflow definitions (existing `elsa.workflow-definition` artifact envelope) and allowlisted configuration keys. **No packages, assemblies or scripts. No remote code execution.**
  - Honest note: workflow definitions can contain expressions that Elsa runs. The boundary is "the same authority as authoring in Studio, by an operator with `ExecuteDeployment`". It does not introduce new code classes.
  - Secrets travel as references only, resolved locally. Values are never copied (#340, ADR-0011).
- **Idempotent apply** keyed on revision id plus digest (reuse #32's apply-journal semantics).
- **Dry-run / diff:** the connector computes a value-free diff against local state and reports it. Control can require operator confirmation before apply.
- **Rollback:** publish a new revision whose content equals a previous one (hash-equal, #340 AC). The connector keeps the last-known-good revision to restore if an apply fails.
- **Per-engine opt-in, on both sides:**
  - customer-side connector setting (default off);
  - an advertised capability (e.g. `desired-state.apply`);
  - per-connection enablement in Control by a holder of `ExecuteDeployment` (#484 invariants).
  - Revoked, stale, offline or incompatible connections cannot fetch new revisions.
- **Audit:** value-free records of publish, confirm, fetch, apply and result (actor, connection, revision, digests, outcome).
- **Evidence:** a connected engine's applied-revision report stays `SelfReported`. On Control-deployed Valence images, Control holds its own deployment proof, so higher grades are possible (#614 decision).
- **One path for all three targets:** build the connector into the Valence Runtime image (elsa-production-image), so Hosted and BYO engines use the same channel. Image and infrastructure changes stay with the provider (managed only). Connected engines never get image or infrastructure authority.
- **Source of desired state:** #340 environment sets and promotion. A promotion produces a new desired-state revision on the target (#340 objective). A single engine with no environment set is an environment of one.

**#316 / ADR-0011: recommendation on runtime commands.**
- **Recommended:** runtime commands (#501) **ride the same outbound channel.** The connector identity, runner lease and heartbeat are the only engine-side trust anchor. Two message classes share that transport:
  1. declarative desired-state revisions (this epic);
  2. imperative allowlisted commands (#501), using the existing durable command / lease / replay contract.
  They keep separate permissions (`ExecuteDeployment` vs `ExecuteControls`), separate capabilities, and separate confirmation and audit (#484 invariants).
- ADR-0011 is amended to say:
  - the connector is the **engine-level** agent;
  - a customer-side **infrastructure** reconciler (#317–#321 Docker reconciler) stays deferred and must not be folded into the connector;
  - #317's DeploymentAgent aggregate is re-scoped onto the existing connector identity (#480/#488/#490/#635) rather than becoming a second enrollment model.
- **Rejected alternatives:**
  - A second agent identity or channel for commands: it doubles the enrollment, rotation and revoke surface we already shipped.
  - Inbound webhooks, or Control calling the engine: these break outbound-only.
  - A long-lived WebSocket/SignalR push: it adds stateful Control infrastructure and spend, and is fragile through customer proxies. It can be revisited as a latency optimisation.
  - GitOps-only as the primary path: it gives Control no truthful applied-revision evidence and needs customer git infrastructure. Exporting a signed bundle for a pipeline to apply stays possible as an option.

**Filed leaves under #731, in order (D1 retains its existing parent #131):**
- **D0. #732 Spike/ADR (M):** delivery ADR covering the bundle format, signing key, drift policy, protocol impact (including whether connector protocol 1 can carry a desired-revision pointer without a version bump) and the ADR-0011 amendment. #316's gap analysis is folded in as input.
- **D1. #340 domain contract (M, existing):** content and promotion contract, also covering single-engine revisions.
- **D2. #733 Revision store and signed bundle publication (L).** Depends on durable artifact storage (#356, ADR-0012).
- **D3. #734 Heartbeat pointer, bundle fetch, applied-revision report, opt-in and permissions (M).** #500 is re-scoped into D3/D4.
- **D4. #735 Connector Core fetch / verify / dry-run / apply / report / rollback state machine, plus the Elsa3 adapter (L).**
- **D5. #736 Connector built into the Valence Runtime image, managed path (M).**
- **D6. #737 Console operator UI (M).** Cloud BFF allowlisted endpoints only when a real customer need exists (S–M).
- **D7. #738 QA live proof (M):**
  - connected engine, public and private outbound-only;
  - a managed engine;
  - rollback;
  - revoke during apply.

**Epic summary:**
- **Dependencies:** 1C (published connector); D0 starts after #508 GO under #868; D2 needs #356; D5 needs elsa-production-image release flow; Phase 0 for any live proof.
- **Spike vs build:** D0 is a spike; the rest is build. **Size:** M spike + XL build (split as above).
- **Cost:** mostly code. Bundle storage on the durable artifact store is small (unmeasured estimate). No new compute.
- **Exit criteria:** D7 passes on all target kinds. ADR-0011 is amended. #500 is closed or superseded.

### Phase 4 candidate: Customer-built images on BYO (uncommitted build after #629/1E)
This remains a roadmap candidate, not an accepted implementation commitment. [Sipke's 4 Oct input](https://github.com/valence-works/elsa-control/issues/629#issuecomment-5982135076) accepts the spike only. Do not file or arm build leaves until the spike output and explicit owner build decision establish the committed scope. The criteria below describe the candidate outcome if approved.

- **Candidate goal, if approved:** Sipke's 4 Oct scenario, end to end: a customer pipeline deploys its own Elsa-based ASP.NET Core app into its BYO subscription through Control, also reachable from Cloud.
- **Dependencies:** explicit owner build decision after the accepted #629 spike; 1A (BYO proven), 1E (design note), Phase 3 revision contract (D1/D2), F2 extension for customer image releases.
- **Spike vs build:** build. **Size:** XL (estimate; split per 1E).
- **Cost:** the Azure bill is the customer's. Valence adds Control load only (unmeasured estimate).
- **Candidate exit criteria, if build approved:**
  - Live proof: pipeline push → digest and provenance registered → compatibility checks → deploy → health → rollback to the previous digest, all in a customer subscription.
  - `SelfReported` labelling throughout.
  - Support boundary and plan/entitlement published (#629 Q6).

### Later (re-baselined, not scheduled here)
- #131 environments and promotion UI (#341–#346).
- #501 runtime controls on the Phase 3 channel.
- Governed managed Elsa 4 Preview #869: #870/#871 are the accepted pre-GO design exception; build #872–#874 (including connector Elsa 4 adapter #873) waits for #508 GO and the capability/release dependencies. The epic retains VerifiedManifest deployment, handoff and workflow-execution proof; Elsa 3→4 migration is a separate boundary.
- #132 Dedicated hardening.
- #133 Private custom code on Valence infrastructure.
- #134 enterprise federation.

## Dependency graph

```mermaid
graph TD
  P0["Phase 0: finish first-public Hosted (508)"]
  BYO["1A BYO Azure: 436 scope, build, design-partner proof"]
  F1["1D Target and placement model (739, in 436 scoping)"]
  MTS["1B Shared tier spike (633)"]
  CON["1C Connector L4-L7 (615-618)"]
  CIS["1E Customer-built image spike (629)"]
  MTB["Phase 2: Shared entry tier build (633 leaves)"]
  DS0["Phase 3 D0/D1: delivery ADR, 316 input, 340 contract"]
  DSB["Phase 3 D2-D7: desired-state delivery (733-738)"]
  CIB["Phase 4 candidate: customer-built images on BYO (uncommitted)"]
  CID["Owner build decision after 629 spike"]
  LATER["Later: 131 promotion UI, 501 runtime controls, Elsa4 adapter, 133 Private"]

  P0 --> BYO
  P0 --> F1
  P0 --> MTS
  P0 --> CON
  P0 --> CIS
  P0 --> DS0
  F1 --> BYO
  F1 --> MTB
  P0 --> MTB
  MTS --> MTB
  CON --> DSB
  DS0 --> DSB
  P0 --> DSB
  BYO --> CIB
  CIS --> CID
  CID --> CIB
  DS0 -->|revision contract| CIB
  DSB --> LATER
  MTS -.->|tiered offer designed together| CIS
```

## Decisions needed from Sipke
1. **Shared tier commercials** (#633 Q7): price, trial limits (including whether the free trial moves to Shared) and support/SLA boundary.
2. **BYO live-proof subscription:** a design partner's subscription (their bill) or a Valence-owned scratch subscription (new spend against the €500 ideal).
3. **Where customer-built images run** (#629 Q1): confirm BYO first, with custom images on Valence-hosted infrastructure "not now" until #133's Private evidence exists.
4. **ADR-0011 direction** (#316 is `needs:decision`): accept "the connector is the engine-level agent, runtime commands ride the same pull channel, the infrastructure reconciler stays deferred, #317 is re-scoped onto the connector identity".
5. **Default drift policy for Control-managed content on connected engines:** detect-and-report (recommended default) or enforce (overwrite local Studio edits on next apply). Also which plan includes desired-state delivery (#406/#484 packaging).
6. **#340's open decision:** may production pin a different release line than non-production? Recommendation in #340: same line, patch may differ.

## Explicitly not now
- Custom code or custom images on Shared shards (ADR-0009; #633 Q8).
- Customer-built images on Valence Hosted infrastructure (needs #133 Private evidence first).
- Control building customer source code; Valence-owned per-workspace registries.
- Any inbound path into customer networks, remote code execution, or package/assembly delivery through the connector.
- Infrastructure lifecycle (stop / restart / upgrade / scale / delete) for connected engines (#484 invariants); a customer-side infrastructure reconciler (#317–#321) beyond the ADR-0011 amendment.
- Elsa 4 adapter build until Elsa 4 host touch points are known.
- Connector sidecar, Key Vault/HSM signer, author-signing certificate (deferred in #499).
- Multi-region, GA, 99.9% or other SLA claims; self-serve BYO claims before productized Lighthouse onboarding.
- Marketplace listing (#559) and any outreach or marketing items.

## Open verification gaps (not yet checked in code)
- Whether managed Hosted engines run the #32 runtime applier today.
- Whether connector protocol 1 accepts a new capability string, and whether the heartbeat response can carry a desired-revision pointer (D0 settles this).
- Sizes for #633, #629 and #615–#618 are estimates; #317 re-scope is an inference from titles plus #318/#103.

## Filed issues

Original issue map filed 4 Oct, reconciled 4 Nov. Live issue/PR/claim/dependency state and #83's integration queue govern current execution; these entries are not a claim that every issue remains Backlog (#730 is closed). Project 7 access is unavailable to this control-room App, so no board update is claimed. Open owner decisions remain on their named issues.
- **Phase 0 (P0):** #730 "#508 row 13: Control rollback proof (staging)", sub-issue of #508.
- **Phase 1 (P1):**
  - #739 1D "Shared placement model for BYO overlay and Shared shard placement (ADR)", sub-issue of #436.
  - #740 1A "BYO Azure design-partner live proof", sub-issue of #436 (decision 2).
  - 1B (#633), 1C (#615–#618) and 1E (#629) use the existing issues; no new issues. #633 (decision 1) and #629 (decision 3) have roadmap comments.
- **Phase 3 (P2):** epic #731 (decision 5) with these leaves:
  - D0 #732 (spike/ADR);
  - D1 #340 (existing; its parent stays #131, decision 6 commented);
  - D2 #733;
  - D3 #734;
  - D4 #735;
  - D5 #736;
  - D6 #737;
  - D7 #738.
  - #500 is re-scoped into D3/D4 and stays open (comment posted).
  - #316 has a comment with decision 4.
- **Filed later:** connector Elsa 4 adapter #873 under #869; its capability, connector and #508 GO gates remain. **Not yet elaborated:** Phase 2 build leaves follow the 1B decision; Phase 4 build leaves require the 1E output and explicit owner build commitment. Neither is expanded speculatively.
