- **[security]** `deploy/configuration.mdx:71` `FORCE_HTTPS` redirects plain HTTP. **Truth:** private-IP and localhost hosts are never redirected. **Evidence:** `proxy.ts:49-59`.
- `deploy/configuration.mdx:27, 170, 176, 60` `neoboard env` generates secrets; `stop && start` restarts; `--validate` checks malformed; `NEXTAUTH_URL` default. **Truth:** docker mode no-op; `start` without `--full` leaves the app down; presence only; no app default. **Evidence:** `cli/src/commands/env.ts:28-82`; `start.ts:45, 158`; `env-config.ts:53`.
- `deploy/deployment-checklist.mdx:95, 136`, `deploy/backup-restore.mdx:241` `MIGRATE_ON_START=0 docker compose …`. **Truth:** compose files do not forward it; container migrates. **Evidence:** `docker/docker-compose.prod*.yml` environment blocks; `Dockerfile` `ENV MIGRATE_ON_START=1`; `cli/src/commands/db/restore.ts:226-227`.
- `deploy/backup-restore.mdx:236, 58` `cp .env.source app/.env.local`; `neoboard-postgres` / `neoboard` containers. **Truth:** prod compose reads `--env-file`; prod containers are `<project>-postgres-1`. **Evidence:** `docker-compose.prod-full.yml` header; `docker-compose.full.yml:18, 58`.
- `deploy/monitoring.mdx:43, 60, 143, 161` degraded = slow DB; healthcheck in compose; structured logs "when configured"; `docker logs neoboard`. **Truth:** degraded only from OIDC config warnings; healthcheck from the Dockerfile; JSON by default; no such container. **Evidence:** `env-config.ts:133-147`; `health/route.ts:116-118`; `Dockerfile` HEALTHCHECK; `logger.ts:8-9`.
- `start-here/troubleshooting.mdx:236, 203, 263, 164, 69, 21, 156, 151` credentials purge SQL, "decryption failed", `logs app`, `env --regenerate` re-syncs, CLI rewrites `.env.local`, four packages, host health probe, `status` waits. **Evidence:** `schema.ts:112-122`; `crypto.ts:110`; `cli/src/commands/logs.ts:10-18`; `env.ts:45-102`; `docker.ts:49-59, 189-209`; root `package.json` workspaces; `status.ts:84-96`.
- `start-here/install.mdx:47, 80, 26` `neoboard env` writes `.env.local`; first signup needs no token; `doctor` health-checks services. **Evidence:** `cli/src/lib/config.ts:181`; `env.ts:77-82`; `signup.ts:59-77`; `doctor.ts:90-121`.
- `start-here/tour.mdx:149` restart with plain `start`. **Evidence:** `docker.ts:110`; `start.ts:45`.
- `start-here/migration-from-neodash.mdx:230, 214` `connectionMapping` key `""`; SSO for everyone. **Truth:** key is `neodash-default`; SSO is enterprise. **Evidence:** `api/dashboards/import/route.ts:32, 62-65`; `features/registry.ts:25-50`.
- `cli/commands.mdx:300, 54, 96, 333, 160, 119, 131` logs `app`; `start` has no options; status migrations; `db migrate --status/--dry-run`; `env --validate`; `doctor` exit codes; demo seed. **Evidence:** `logs.ts`; `cli/src/index.ts:48-66, 117-122`; `status.ts:49-58`; `db/migrate.ts:53-77`; `env.ts:14-22`; `doctor.ts:44-147`; `scripts/seed-demo.mjs:225-316`.
- `cli/index.mdx:18` `setup --mode local` runs databases in Docker. **Evidence:** `start.ts:80-84`.
- `README.md:82` two demo connections. **Truth:** four. **Evidence:** `scripts/seed-demo.mjs:283-316`.
- `CONTRIBUTING-enterprise.md:28, 82` missing package boots as community; `docker/docker-compose.keycloak.yml`. **Truth:** env var alone sets the edition; the compose file does not exist. **Evidence:** `features/registry.ts:39-55`; `extensions/bootstrap.ts:77-84`; `scripts/setup-enterprise.sh:145-147`.
- `.github/CONTRIBUTING.md:20, 81, 82` demo script then `npm run dev`; ESLint on commit for all; no default exports. **Evidence:** `scripts/setup-local-demo.sh:12-20`; `package.json:46-60` lint-staged; `scripts/generate-connector-imports.mjs:104`.

## Cause

Drift since the 2026-09-04 docs cleanup (#1316 and follow-ups). Pages were written from intent and not revisited when the code moved: roles and connection permissions, SSO wiring, the scheduler's priority header, the CLI's Docker/local split, and chart option schemas all changed underneath them. The existing guards in `scripts/__tests__/docs-accuracy.test.mjs` and `app/src/lib/__tests__/docs-accuracy.test.ts` check specific tokens and phrases (env var names, CLI commands, chart counts, HKDF in the repo docs, links), so a false sentence that uses only real tokens passes.

## Required tests

- **Docs accuracy guard per security claim** (Vitest, `scripts/__tests__/docs-accuracy.test.mjs`, no DOM): one `it` per **[security]** item above, each asserting its page no longer contains the false phrase. Each guard must fail on today's `release/1.5` text, pass after the correction, and be worded narrowly so a correct sentence (for example "no HKDF derivation", "no envelope") still passes. Prove each by restoring the old phrase in a scratch edit and watching it fail.
- **Build:** `npm run build --prefix docs` stays green (MDX valid after the rewrites).
- **Suites:** `npm run verify` and `npm run test:scripts` green.
- Behaviour-severity and minor items are corrected in prose; no per-item guard is required for them.

items.title: [CANONICAL MEMORY][Owner App] ChatGPT operating contract, connectors, serial state & handoff
items.body:
# Owner App — Canonical ChatGPT Operating Memory

This issue is the durable handoff/source-of-truth for ChatGPT/AI work on **Relife Owner App**.

## Trigger phrase
If the user starts a new chat and says **“Owner App” / “Owner Apps”**, treat that as an instruction to:
1. Open this issue first.
2. Open Issue #134 for the active serial execution contract.
3. Check latest GitHub `main`, open PRs/issues, CI, and Render production state before proposing or performing implementation work.
4. Continue from the current serial item; do not restart planning from scratch.
5. Keep Relife Owner App (`avatarbd1/relife-owner-app`) separate from Relife Clinic OS/Telegram bot (`avatarbd1/relife-clinic-os`).

---

## 1. Project identity
- Product: **Relife Owner App / Web App**
- Repository: `avatarbd1/relife-owner-app`
- Stack: Next.js 16 + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind + Supabase integrations + Google Sheets operational data during current migration phase.
- Production hosting: Render service `relife-owner-app`
- Canonical brand: **Relife**

## 2. ChatGPT’s role
ChatGPT is not just a code generator. Its job is to act as the **technical director / verifier / release controller** for this repo.

ChatGPT must:
- keep the roadmap and serial order stable;
- convert the user’s intent into precise implementation prompts for Claude/other coding AI when appropriate;
- independently inspect the actual repo instead of trusting AI summaries;
- review PR/diff/tests/CI before accepting claims;
- verify Render deploy state after merges;
- separate `merge`, `deploy`, and `live smoke` as distinct states;
- preserve accounting/security/domain invariants;
- stop duplicate/parallel implementations;
- report exact evidence, not optimistic claims;
- teach the user one small developer concept tied to each real task/message.

## 3. Claude / coding-AI role
Claude may implement code, tests, commits, branches and PRs when instructed.

ChatGPT must independently verify Claude’s:
- branch/base;
- diff and changed files;
- canonical writer/rule reuse;
- tests and their meaningfulness;
- CI/build status;
- PR state;
- merge state;
- deployment state;
- live evidence.

**Claude saying `complete` is never sufficient evidence by itself.**

## 4. User authorization rules
- User saying `start / koro / shuru` authorizes implementation.
- It does **not** automatically authorize merge.
- Merge only after explicit user authorization such as `merge / marge`, unless a previously explicit conditional merge authorization applies to that exact PR.
- Never direct-write application code to `main`.
- Use fresh branch from latest `main`, Draft PR by default.
- Documentation-only GitHub issues/comments may be used without code PRs.

## 5. Connector/tool operating model
Use connected systems directly when relevant.

### GitHub connector
Use for:
- repo truth;
- branches/commits;
- issues;
- PRs/diffs/reviews;
- CI/workflow evidence;
- merge status.

### Render connector
Use for:
- service state;
- deploy status;
- deployed commit SHA;
- logs/errors/5xx;
- health/performance metrics;
- production verification.

Render workspace confirmed: **My Workspace** (`tea-d9akevo458ps73ft87n0`).
Production service: `relife-owner-app` (`srv-d9vhmn5bedkc73bqrbl0`).

### Supabase connector
Use for any Supabase-specific work: schema, database, Edge Functions, Auth, Storage, RLS, migrations, cron/queues, etc. Inspect before changing.

### Google Drive / Sheets connector
Use for connected Sheets/Docs/Drive when live operational sheet structure/data must be inspected or edited. Current migration rules still matter: do not silently replace the operational authority.

### Other connectors
Use any connected connector that materially improves verification or execution; do not substitute guesses for connected evidence.

## 6. Mandatory state check at the start of meaningful Owner App work
Before deciding “what next”:
1. Fetch latest GitHub `main` SHA.
2. Check open PRs.
3. Check relevant open/closed tracker issues.
4. Check CI for the active code state when applicable.
5. Check Render production deployed SHA/status after merges or before live smoke.
6. Compare GitHub vs Render by **tree/content**, not SHA alone when history-only commits exist.
7. Identify active serial item from Issue #134.

## 7. Merge vs deploy vs live verification
These are separate:
- **Merged** = code entered GitHub `main`.
- **Deployed** = Render production is running that app content.
- **Live verified** = real production flow/device/role scenario was executed successfully.

Never use one as proof of another.

## 8. Current Phase 0 serial tracker
Execution/reporting contract: **Issue #134**.

### P0-01 — Dental Billing Forward-Port ✅ MERGED
- PR #131
- Merge commit: `ba077f81654910191fcfbc70f3c0b78015212e9d`
- Dental treatment charge updates billed receivable / patient bill and due.
- Treatment save does not create payment/receipt/cash collection.
- Stable request-id protects retry idempotency.

### P0-02 — Cash Approval RBAC Hardening ✅ MERGED
- Issue #132
- PR #133
- Merge commit: `420e4faa2a5c39612f60298148b00112bd139410`
- signed session → current access context → explicit Owner → Owner PIN → canonical `decideCashMovement()`.
- audit actor = authenticated Owner `staffId`.

### P0-03 — Performance Metrics Verification ✅ COMPLETE
- Issue #135 closed/completed.
- Verification-only; no code change/PR required.
- 514/514 tests, 59 suites, 0 failures reported/verified as supporting repository evidence.
- Missing metrics remain `null`/unavailable, never fabricated `0`.
- Incomplete coverage remains provisional; no official score/rank when incomplete.
- XP, normalized score, Reward Credit, Performance Bonus remain distinct.
- Live verification intentionally deferred to P0-04.

### P0-04 — Live E2E + Device Smoke ⏭️ CURRENT
Deployment gate already checked:
- Render service live and not suspended.
- Render deployed commit: `420e4faa2a5c39612f60298148b00112bd139410`.
- GitHub main later became `fae3aa6de513a2757202797437a8108c6333cb07` because of two history-only commits.
- Compare `420e4f...` → `fae3aa...`: 2 commits ahead, **0 changed files**, therefore deployed application content is equivalent to current main tree.
- Current deploy window had no observed app error and no observed HTTP 500/502/503/504 in checked logs.
- Old Google Sheets HTTP 503 errors existed before this deploy and must not be misrepresented as current-deploy failures.

P0-04 must verify controlled production/device flows for:
- Dental billing + duplicate retry protection + payment boundary;
- Cash approval RBAC Owner/non-Owner/PIN paths;
- Performance null/provisional/official-rank separation;
- role/department isolation;
- at least one Android/mobile production smoke.

### P0-05 — Finance Reconciliation
Not started yet.
Must preserve exact terms:
- Billed Services
- Collections
- Outstanding
- Cash Handover
Cash Handover is custody movement, never revenue.
Physio/Dental remain isolated.

## 9. Frozen roadmap after Phase 0
### Phase 1A — Relife Physio completion + proving
Build:
- Shift Scheduling
- Leave Management
- SMS v1 outbound-only
- Correction Center append-only
- Analytics v1 with Billed Services / Collections / Outstanding / Cash Handover separated

Harden existing, do not rebuild:
- Settings
- Attendance reporting
- Bulk import/export
- Chamber chat
- PWA
- Staff management

### Phase 1B — SaaS conversion
- Next.js + Supabase retained
- tenant/clinic isolation with `clinic_id`/`tenant_id` + RLS
- no clinic-per-database/schema design
- staged provisioning/subscription/platform-admin work only after current system is proven

### Phase 2 — controlled rollout
Wave-based clinic rollout after proof/reconciliation/security gates.

## 10. Architecture invariants
- One user action → one canonical command/query → one domain rule → one repository/transaction → one audit event.
- No duplicate canonical writer.
- No parallel business-rule engine.
- Extend existing route/domain/service first.
- Critical writes fail closed.
- No silent fake/demo data in production.
- Financial/clinical corrections stay append-only/compensating, not destructive.

## 11. Source of Truth / migration rules
During Phase 0 + Phase 1A:
- Google Sheets remains operational authority for legacy/current operational domains unless an already-approved domain is explicitly cut over.
- PostgreSQL/Supabase is used for selected newer transactional/gamification paths and analytics/migration staging.
- Never silently change authority.
- Supabase cutover happens domain-by-domain with rollback/parity verification.

## 12. Finance invariants
- Reception → Home Treasury / Bank = internal cash transfer, not revenue or expense.
- No double count between cash movement and expense.
- Collections source remains canonical payment records (`06_Payments`) for current Sheets authority.
- Billed Services ≠ Collections.
- Outstanding ≠ Collection.
- Salary master ≠ salary paid/advance.
- Physio and Dental accounting stay isolated.

## 13. Booking vs operating invariant
Physio booking and live operation are separate.

Booking:
- 60 min ±5
- capacity/gender/duplicate-patient hard guards
- no fixed bed/machine reservation
- therapist overlap advisory
- machine demand planning only

Live operation:
- Arrived → Start Treatment → machine Start/Finish → Complete
- live resources tracked at execution time
- treatment cannot complete while machine is running

## 14. Role / department model
Roles include Owner, Manager, Receptionist, Therapist, Dentist, Dental Assistant/Auditor paths as implemented.
Departments: Physio / Dental / Owner-All scope.

Core rule:
- Dental staff must not see/edit Physio data without explicit approved scope.
- Physio staff must not see/edit Dental data without explicit approved scope.
- Owner can have All scope.
- Finance/clinical access remains permission-gated by canonical access context.

## 15. User-facing implementation reporting format
After every implementation/PR/merge, report in serial order:
1. Serial + task name
2. What changed
3. Logic/function flow and canonical reader/writer
4. How Owner/staff uses it in app
5. App impact
6. What remains untouched
7. Data/accounting/security invariants
8. Verification evidence: focused tests, full tests, lint, build, CI
9. Live verification YES/NO and exact remaining smoke
10. Branch/PR/head SHA/merge state/merge commit
11. Next serial item

## 16. Teaching / coaching rule
For **every meaningful user message/task**, provide one small developer-learning item tied to the actual work.
Do not dump a full curriculum.
Preferred learning chain:
**Problem → Flow → Function → Rule → Test**

Common concepts to teach gradually:
- Reader vs Writer vs Guard
- `null` vs `0`
- Source of Truth
- canonical Writer
- permission/RBAC
- failure path/fail closed
- idempotency/duplicate safety
- tests vs evidence
- PR/Diff
- CI/Build
- Merge vs Deploy vs Live Smoke
- local/sandbox work vs repo evidence

When Claude is about to do work:
- give the user a tiny relevant concept first;
- provide an exact Claude prompt;
- independently verify afterward;
- then ask one small question.

## 17. Evidence hierarchy
Strongest evidence order:
1. Live production/device evidence
2. Render deploy/log evidence
3. GitHub main/PR/diff/CI evidence
4. Meaningful automated tests
5. Source inspection
6. AI-written summary

Never reverse this hierarchy.

## 18. Known history note
There was an accidental `noop` file commit directly to main and immediate cleanup. Final tree returned byte-equivalent to the pre-accident app tree. Git history contains the two commits; do not claim history untouched. This is why production deploy SHA may differ from current main SHA while app content remains identical.

## 19. New-chat recovery procedure
When a new chat begins with “Owner App”:
- read this issue;
- read Issue #134;
- inspect current GitHub repo state;
- inspect Render if deployment/live status matters;
- identify active serial task;
- report current state before proposing next work;
- continue without making the user re-explain the project.

## 20. Do not do
- Do not confuse Owner App with Telegram bot/Clinic OS.
- Do not trust Claude completion claims without repo evidence.
- Do not direct-write app code to main.
- Do not merge without authorization.
- Do not create duplicate systems/writers.
- Do not call verification-only work “merged”.
- Do not call merged work “deployed” without Render evidence.
- Do not call deployed work “live verified” without executed smoke evidence.
- Do not fabricate metrics, finance rows, patient data, smoke results or coverage percentages.

This issue should remain open and be updated when the operating contract, serial state, connector topology, or canonical workflow changes.

items.title: Playwright specs + ephemeral CI stack (prod / app-dev login verification)

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
## Why

[#304](https://github.com/EnterpriseBT/portal-ai/issues/304) shipped the Playwright harness and agent-guided browser sessions — the `@portalai/e2e` package, devcontainer browser bake, reusable Auth0 `storageState`, seeded fixture org, Playwright MCP wiring, and the `/smoke-walk` skill — but deliberately deferred the **automated** tier and scoped everything to the **local** dev stack. Today nothing runs Playwright in CI (`packages/e2e`'s `test:unit`/`test:integration` are no-ops, `src/specs/` is empty), and nothing — CI or agent — can authenticate against `app-dev` or `prod`: both are Google-only, the dev sign-in affordance is stripped from deployed builds, and the QA users exist only in the local Auth0 tenant.

This ticket closes three gaps, each with a deliberately different scope:

1. **PR-time walk of a newly provisioned org** (`test:e2e`, ephemeral CI stack) — a basic browser walk proving login succeeds and the app's core loop works on a fresh org.
2. **Post-deploy login verification** — after a `deploy-dev` / `deploy-prod` run, CI logs in to *that* environment to prove authentication works. Login only, nothing more.
3. **Agent browser sessions against `app-dev` and `prod`** (outside CI) — so an in-container Claude session can verify actual deployed behavior, walk tedious workflows, and reproduce / confirm customer bug reports, instead of handing every authenticated deployed-env check back to a human.

Depends on **#304** (the harness this builds on), which has landed.

## Deliverables

**Deployed-env identity (shared by 2 and 3)**
- [ ] A **dedicated QA Database-connection user per deployed Auth0 tenant** (`app-dev`, `prod`): Database connection enabled on the SPA application with **sign-ups disabled**, three QA users (**owner, admin, member**), MFA off, strong passwords held in AWS Secrets Manager (per-env), never in the repo. Normal users never see it — the app's login pins the Google connection.
- [ ] A **guarded sign-in path that ships in deployed builds** and selects the QA Database connection explicitly (the #304 affordance is `import.meta.env.DEV`-only and stripped from deployed bundles). Its guard and threat model are decided in discovery and recorded; it must not widen the login surface for anyone without the QA credential.
- [ ] Operator runbook for the vendor-side setup (Auth0 connection + user per tenant, secret placement) — on the post-deploy / release checklist so it isn't missed the way #873's Auth0 step was.

**Dedicated QA org per deployed env**
- [ ] A **dedicated QA org** in `app-dev` and `prod`, owned by the QA user, provisioned through `portalai` (admin-cli), on a **tier grant with no Stripe subscription** (no live charges). This is the **only** org each QA identity (owner, admin, member) is a member of; the admin and member join it by invitation.

**1. Ephemeral-stack walk (PRs)**
- [ ] `*.spec.ts` under `packages/e2e/src/specs/` walking a **newly provisioned org** per run through the core loop: **login → dashboard → CSV connector import → entity records visible → create a station → open a portal**. **No live LLM / agent chat** (no Anthropic key in CI, no per-PR cost, no nondeterminism).
- [ ] `test:e2e` runner wired through Turbo (the deferred script #304 left out), plus a headed/UI variant for authoring.
- [ ] A GitHub Actions workflow that boots the full stack per run — Postgres (+ Redis) via `docker compose … --wait`, migrations applied, API on `:3001`, web on `:3000` — with no dependence on any developer's stack. Follows `integration-test.yml` (`./.github/actions/setup`, teardown in `if: always()`).
- [ ] **Unattended auth on the ephemeral stack**, decided and documented, so specs need no interactive login in the spec body.
- [ ] Failure artifacts uploaded on red: traces, screenshots, video, and the HTML report.
- [ ] The workflow runs on PRs but is **not** a required check at first (see Out of scope).

**2. Post-deploy login check**
- [ ] A login-only spec run as the final job of `deploy-dev.yml` and `deploy-prod.yml`, against the environment just deployed, as that env's QA user. Credentials fetched at run time from that env's Secrets Manager via the deploy role (scoped to read that one secret).
- [ ] On failure the deploy run goes **red** with trace + screenshot attached; **no automatic rollback** (rollback stays a human decision).

**3. Agent sessions against app-dev / prod**
- [ ] An `e2e:auth --env <app-dev|prod>` path that fetches the QA credential from that env's Secrets Manager (AWS-IAM, as `cli-env` does), signs in through the guarded path, and writes a per-env, git-ignored `storageState` the Playwright MCP can load (alongside the local one, without clobbering it).
- [ ] A documented way to point an agent session at a given env (base URL + storageState), and the switch back to local.
- [ ] Agent conduct in deployed envs documented in `packages/e2e/README.md` (and `CLAUDE.md`): reads and writes are allowed **only inside the QA org**; a customer bug is reproduced by **recreating its conditions in the QA org**, never by entering a customer org; created data is cleaned up or clearly labelled.

**Multi-role verification (owner / admin / member)** — amended 2026-10-27
- [ ] **PR walk:** CI admin and member users in the dev tenant (`E2E_CI_AUTH0_USERNAME_ADMIN` / `_MEMBER` + passwords; the local e2e admin/member identities are reused). A `roles` spec on the ephemeral stack: the owner invites both from Settings → Members, each signs in through the invite link and accepts, lands in the owner's org with exactly one membership, and sees the affordances its role allows — with the server refusing what the UI hides.
- [ ] **Deployed:** QA admin and member users per tenant, invited into the QA org, credentials in Secrets Manager. `e2e:auth --env <app-dev|prod> --identity <admin|member>` signs each in (first sign-in through the invite link), and an agent session can switch identity per env.
- [ ] The post-deploy check stays a **login-only check as the QA owner**.

**Browser-container topology (decision deferred from #304)**
- [ ] Decide whether the browser runs as its **own service** (official `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v<ver>` image via `--cdp-endpoint`) vs. the single-image bake #304 ships. Weigh cross-container networking, an extra Auth0 Allowed-Callback-URL + `storageState` origin mismatch, MCP-over-CDP/SSE vs stdio-local, and no CPU saving. (Full analysis in #304's discovery/spec.)

## Acceptance criteria

- `npm run test:e2e` runs the Playwright suite green from a clean checkout.
- The PR workflow boots its own Postgres, API, and web, provisions a fresh org, walks login → dashboard → CSV import → records → station → portal, and tears down — succeeding on a machine where no dev stack was ever started.
- A red run uploads a trace/screenshot/report artifact sufficient to diagnose the failure without re-running locally.
- Authentication is unattended in every CI run; adding a new spec requires no interactive login in the spec body.
- After a `deploy-dev` / `deploy-prod` run, a login check against that environment succeeds as its QA user; a broken login (e.g. a stale Auth0 Action, as in #873) turns the deploy run red with artifacts, and the deploy is not rolled back automatically.
- An in-container agent session can sign in to `app-dev` and `prod` as the QA user unattended and walk the app inside the QA org.
- The PR run signs in as owner, admin and member. The admin and member join the owner's org through the invite link without a personal org being provisioned. A member sees no Members tab and is refused `POST /api/organization/invitations` (403); an admin sees Members but no Delete organization, and is refused the org delete (403).
- An agent session in `app-dev` / `prod` can act as the QA owner, admin or member, switching without editing any file by hand.
- Each QA identity (owner, admin, member) is a member of exactly one org per env, the QA org; none can read or reach any customer org (unreadable == 404).
- The QA Database connection has sign-ups disabled, and a normal user's login flow is unchanged (still Google, no password field shown).
- No credential or `storageState` for a deployed env is committed or uploaded as a CI artifact.
- The PR workflow appears on PRs and does not block merge.
- The covered flows fail **loudly, not flakily** when a deliberate regression is introduced.

## Out of scope

- **Promoting the PR workflow to a required check.** Deferred until the suite demonstrates stability — the promotion (branch-protection change + a stated flake threshold) is its own follow-up.
- **Access to customer orgs** (support access / impersonation with consent + audit). Bugs are reproduced in the QA org; entering a customer org is a separate feature.
- **Automatic rollback** on a failed post-deploy check.
- **Live agent chat / LLM calls** in CI specs.
- **Broad flow coverage** beyond the core loop — connector sync, agent chat, tier changes get specs as their features land.
- **Visual-regression / screenshot-diff testing.**
- **Retiring existing `.smoke.md` docs** — they narrow to the non-automatable remainder as flows gain spec coverage.

## Sizing

`full` — new CI workflow, a new test tier (`*.spec.ts` + `test:e2e`), a deployed-build auth surface in prod, a secrets/unattended-auth surface across three envs, deploy-workflow changes, and a browser-container-topology decision. Multi-axis and contract-touching.

## References

- Parent capability: **#304** (harness + agent sessions) · PR #488
- #304 discovery → "What this doesn't decide" and spec → "Out of scope" (browser-container topology analysis)
- #873 — the prod login loop a post-deploy login check would have caught
- `.github/workflows/integration-test.yml`, `.github/actions/setup` — the ephemeral-services pattern to follow
- `.github/workflows/deploy-dev.yml`, `deploy-prod.yml` — where the post-deploy check lands
- `docker-compose.yml` — `postgres`/`postgres-test`/`redis`/`mcp-net`
- `packages/e2e/` (the harness), `.mcp.json`, `packages/cli-env` (AWS-IAM credential access), `packages/admin-cli` (org provisioning)



## Docs

- Discovery: [E2E_BROWSER_VERIFICATION.discovery.md](https://github.com/EnterpriseBT/portal-ai/blob/feat/489-e2e-browser-verification/docs/E2E_BROWSER_VERIFICATION.discovery.md)
- Spec: [E2E_BROWSER_VERIFICATION.spec.md](https://github.com/EnterpriseBT/portal-ai/blob/feat/489-e2e-browser-verification/docs/E2E_BROWSER_VERIFICATION.spec.md)
- Plan: [E2E_BROWSER_VERIFICATION.plan.md](https://github.com/EnterpriseBT/portal-ai/blob/feat/489-e2e-browser-verification/docs/E2E_BROWSER_VERIFICATION.plan.md)
- Runbook (durable): [E2E_DEPLOYED_QA.runbook.md](https://github.com/EnterpriseBT/portal-ai/blob/feat/489-e2e-browser-verification/docs/E2E_DEPLOYED_QA.runbook.md)

items.title: A retried batch sends empty event arrays: SaveChangesAsync commits the documents, silently drops the events, and reports success
items.body:
## Summary

On a production incident we found a `SaveChangesAsync()` that

1. failed with an Npgsql read timeout while executing its operation batch,
2. **persisted part of that batch anyway** — all document inserts/deletes committed, but only 8 of 69 appended events, and
3. **never surfaced an exception to the caller** — Wolverine logged the message as successfully processed, one attempt, no retry, no dead letter.

The application only noticed five days later, because the missing events were the ones that remove a work item from a read model, so the item kept coming back on every projection rebuild.

I can't reproduce it on demand (it needs a batch that actually times out mid-flight), so this is a forensic report rather than a repro. Everything below is measured from the event store and the container logs, not inferred.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Marten | 9.22.6 |
| JasperFx / JasperFx.Events | 2.46.0 |
| Npgsql | 10.0.3 |
| .NET | 10 |
| PostgreSQL | 16 (AWS RDS) |
| `EventAppendMode` | `QuickWithServerTimestamps` (the Marten 9 default) |
| Event tenancy | `TenancyStyle.Conjoined` + `UseTenantPartitionedEvents = true` |
| Tenancy | multi-database, ~512 shard databases, tenants assigned via a database pool table |
| Session | opened by Wolverine's `OutboxedSessionFactory` → `store.OpenSession(new SessionOptions { Tracking = DocumentTracking.None })` |
| Connection lifetime | `AutoClosingLifetime` (per `SessionOptions.buildConnectionLifetime`: `OwnsConnection && OwnsTransactionLifecycle`, `ReadCommitted`, `UseStickyConnectionLifetimes = false`) |

## What the code does

A message handler loads N pending read-model documents, appends one event per document to the document's own stream, deletes the documents, and inserts one guard document per line — all on one session, committed once. Simplified:

```csharp
public static void After(IReadOnlyList<PendingLine> lines, IDocumentSession session)
{
    foreach (var group in lines.GroupBy(x => x.StreamKey))
    {
        session.Events.Append(group.Key, events: group.Select(x => new PreparedForInvoice { LineId = x.Id, Amount = x.Amount }));
    }

    session.DeleteObjects(lines);

    foreach (var line in lines)
    {
        session.Insert(new ConcurrencyGuard { Id = line.Id });
    }
}
```

Wolverine's generated handler shows there is exactly one session and exactly one `SaveChangesAsync` — no second commit anywhere:

```csharp
public override async Task HandleAsync(MessageContext context, CancellationToken cancellation)
{
    await using var serviceScope = _serviceScopeFactory.CreateAsyncScope();
    // Building the Marten session
    await using var documentSession = _outboxedSessionFactory.OpenSession(context);
    var message = (InvoiceLines)context.Envelope.Message;

    (var lines, var config, var routing) = await Handler.LoadAsync(message, documentSession, ...);

    var outgoing1 = Handler.Handle(message, config, routing, lines);

    // Outgoing, cascaded message
    await context.EnqueueCascadingAsync(outgoing1).ConfigureAwait(false);

    RecordCauseAndEffect(context, context.Runtime.Observer);
    Handler.After(lines, documentSession);

    // Save all pending changes to this Marten session
    await documentSession.SaveChangesAsync(cancellation).ConfigureAwait(false);

    await context.FlushOutgoingMessagesAsync().ConfigureAwait(false);
}
```

For this particular run, N = 69 lines spread over 65 streams.

## The failure

`After` created the 69 event objects at `13:19:50.114443Z` (client-assigned timestamps — `QuickWithServerTimestamps` sends `timestamps[]` from the client, per the note in `QuickAppendEventsWithServerTimestampsOperation`). `SaveChangesAsync` then failed ~5.3 s later.

Marten logged the failure through `LogFailure(NpgsqlBatch, Exception)`, which emits one `LogError` per `batch.BatchCommands` entry — so the 215 error records below are **one** batch failure, and they give an exact inventory of the batch:

| operation | count | log window (UTC) |
|---|---|---|
| `select public.mt_quick_append_events($1,…)` | **65** | 13:19:55.390–.403 |
| `insert into public.wolverine_incoming_envelopes` | 10 | .404–.405 |
| `delete from public.mt_doc_<pending>` | **69** | .406–.445 |
| `insert into public.mt_doc_<guard>` | **69** | .445–.459 |
| `update public.wolverine_incoming_envelopes` | 1 | .460 |
| (1 more) | 1 | .461 |

Every one of them carried the same exception:

```
Npgsql.NpgsqlException (0x80004005): Exception while reading from stream
 ---> System.TimeoutException: Timeout during reading attempt
   at Npgsql.Internal.NpgsqlConnector.ReadMessageLong(Boolean async, DataRowLoadingMode dataRowLoadingMode, Boolean readingNotifications, Boolean isReadingPrependedMessage)
   at System.Runtime.CompilerServices.PoolingAsyncValueTaskMethodBuilder`1.StateMachineBox`1.System.Threading.Tasks.Sources.IValueTaskSource<TResult>.GetResult(Int16 token)
   at Npgsql.NpgsqlConnector…
```

### Why it timed out at 5 s (probably worth its own look)

`AutoClosingLifetime.ExecuteBatchPagesAsync` sets `batch.Timeout = CommandTimeout`, which comes from `StoreOptions.CommandTimeout`. That property defaults to `StoreOptions.DefaultTimeout = 5` and is only raised from a connection string in `StoreOptions.Connection(...)` (`StoreOptions.cs:610`).

In a multi-database tenancy setup the shard connection strings never pass through that code path, so `Command Timeout=300` on every shard connection string had no effect and the effective batch timeout stayed at **5 seconds** — for a batch of 215 operations against a loaded database. If that is intended, it is a sharp edge: the connection string of the database the batch actually runs against is ignored, and there is no warning.

## What actually persisted

Verified in the database five days later:

| | expected | present |
|---|---|---|
| appended events | 69 | **8** |
| document deletes | 69 | 69 (all gone) |
| guard document inserts | 69 | 69 |
| `wolverine_incoming_envelopes` writes | 11 | 11 (all 10 cascaded messages were delivered and handled) |

Two details that pin this down:

- The 8 surviving events carry the client timestamps from *this* attempt (`13:19:50.114443Z`/`.114444Z`), so they are that batch's own event objects, not a later retry's.
- The guard documents carry `mt_last_modified = 13:19:55.502928Z` (their insert SQL uses `transaction_timestamp()`), i.e. ~40 ms **after** the last of the 215 error records was written. So something committed after the failure was logged.
- Sequence numbers are contiguous around the survivors (the 8 events sit on consecutive `seq_id`s, immediately followed by the next unrelated events) — the 57 missing appends never drew a sequence number, and there are no tombstones in that range.

## What did not happen

No exception reached the caller. Wolverine logged `Finished processing` for that envelope 4 s later, exactly one `Started processing`, no retry and no dead letter — and the application has explicit retry policies for `MartenCommandException`, `ConcurrencyException`, `EventStreamUnexpectedMaxEventIdException`, `DocumentAlreadyExistsException` and `AggregateException`, so a thrown exception would have been visible.

Reading the two relevant lifetimes, both look like they should have rolled back and rethrown:

- `AutoClosingLifetime.ExecuteBatchPagesAsync` — `try { tx = BeginTransactionAsync(); foreach page { … } } catch { tx.RollbackAsync(); Logger.LogFailure(new NpgsqlCommand(), e); TransformAndThrow(e); }`
- `TransactionalConnection.ExecuteBatchPagesAsync` — same shape, plus `if (exceptions.Count == 1) → rollback + rethrow` and `if (exceptions.Any()) → rollback + AggregateException`.

So the two things I cannot explain from the code are exactly the two that hurt:

1. **How a single transaction ended up partially committed** — 8 of 65 `mt_quick_append_events` calls, but all 138 document operations and all 11 envelope operations. A `ROLLBACK` on a broken connector should have left nothing, and a partial commit should not be reachable at all.
2. **How `SaveChangesAsync` returned normally** after `LogFailure` had been called for all 215 commands.

Is it possible for the batch pages to be executed outside the transaction that `ExecuteBatchPagesAsync` begins — or for a broken-connector rollback path to swallow the original exception and return? A `Timeout during reading attempt` leaves the connector in a state where the rollback itself fails; `AutoClosingLifetime` has an inner `catch (Exception rollbackEx)` around the rollback that logs and rethrows, but `TransactionalConnection` does not, so there at least the rollback failure would replace the original exception.

## Why this is nasty in practice

The write was split across two kinds of storage that the application assumed were atomic together. The document side (delete the work item, claim the line) committed; the event side (record that the work item was handled) did not. Because read models are rebuilt from events, every later projection rebuild resurrected work items that had already been processed — including some already sent to an external party. Nothing anywhere reported a failure.

Happy to run more queries against the affected database or to try building a repro with a deliberately short `CommandTimeout` and a slow trigger, if that would help.

items.title: Multitenancy in the DMS

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
How will we design multi-tenancy in the DMS? What terminology will we use to describe tenants / instances / etc? We may want to be more expansive and flexible in terms than in the ODS/API.

[Azure: Fundamental Concepts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/ready/considerations/fundamental-concepts) may be a useful reference.

----

SaaS providers typically think of three multi-tenancy models for data storage:

1. Complete database segregation.
2. Segregation within a database, by schema
3. Segregation within a table, by column

My own current thinking is that we probably want the flexibility of supporting two models. The schema approach is not as clean as the column approach, and we wouldn't pursue option 2.

items.title: 工程脚手架：Connector SPI 多模块 + Flink/SeaTunnel 作业骨架（可独立运行）
items.body:
## 背景

为 `data-foundation` 建立**可独立开发 / 编译 / 调试 / 运行**的工程脚手架——数据底座（流批采集 + 湖仓 + 统一计算 + Connector SPI）。核心是把 **Connector SPI** 的"加插件不动主干"骨架先立起来（信创刚需收敛点）。

> 依赖：主仓 [libs-java HashMatrixData/hashmatrix#1](https://github.com/HashMatrixData/hashmatrix/issues/1)；设计见架构 [03-技术选型](https://github.com/HashMatrixData/hashmatrix/blob/main/docs/architecture/03-技术选型.md) / [04-工程与部署](https://github.com/HashMatrixData/hashmatrix/blob/main/docs/architecture/04-工程与部署.md)。

## 任务清单（DoD）

**Maven 多模块（独立可构建运行）**
- [ ] `connector-spi/`：定义 SPI 接口（连接 / 元数据扫描 / 读写）
- [ ] `connector-jdbc/`：标准 JDBC **参考实现**（PostgreSQL/MySQL）
- [ ] `connector-dialect-*/`：达梦 / 人大金仓 / OceanBase 方言插件**占位**（**新增数据库 = 加一个插件 jar，不改主干**）
- [ ] `ingest/`：Flink + Flink-CDC（流）/ SeaTunnel（批）作业**骨架**（本地 mini-cluster 可跑）
- [ ] `app/`：服务骨架，`<parent>` + `import` BOM + `starter-tenant`（**Maven 坐标引用**）；**只 clone 本仓即可 `mvn package`**

**多租户与配额**
- [ ] 采集 / 计算 / 湖仓**按租户隔离 catalog/database**（Doris/Paimon per-tenant）；作业受租户配额约束

**测试与 Mock**
- [ ] 复用 `starter-test`；Connector SPI 契约测试（参考实现）；**Mock 数据脱敏**（`acme`/`tenant-demo`）
- [ ] Flink 作业本地集成测试（Testcontainers / mini-cluster）

**本地独立运行/调试**
- [ ] `docker-compose.local.yml`（PG + MinIO + 可选 Doris/Kafka）；`Dockerfile`；健康检查通过

**交付汇入**
- [ ] Helm 子 chart 占位到主仓 `deploy/charts/data-foundation` → 关联 HashMatrixData/hashmatrix#2
- [ ] CI：多模块构建 + 测试 + 镜像

## 边界

- **数据采集（本仓·主链路·搬行数据）≠ 元数据采集（`governance`·旁路·取结构）（AD-15）**：二者**共用 Connector SPI + 数据源统一管理**，连接器只实现一次。

## 约束

- 🔴 红线见 `CLAUDE.md`（公开仓，禁甲方信息，示例脱敏）。

## 验收

只 clone 本仓 → `mvn package`（多模块）通过 → `connector-jdbc` 契约测试绿 → `docker-compose up` + Flink 样例本地跑通。

Substantive B1 `governance_release_assurance`. Independent from implementation and from principal-authorized B0 checks.

Do **not** issue substantive PASS while PR #29 is still dependent on a non-authoritative convergence base. After PR #26 is integrated, implementation_operations must retarget/reconcile PR #29 to current authoritative `main`, prove the intended M1 delta is preserved, record the resulting trusted base SHA and exact candidate SHA, then clear this blocker.

1. M1 implements the canonical Mission Contract's shared-PostgreSQL/tenant-owned evidence-first direction without reintroducing database-per-client or premature runtime architecture.
2. Global Source/Framework/Requirement/Control catalog remains separate from tenant/customer truth.
3. `Requirement != Control != ClientImplementation != Evidence != Assessment != ProfessionalReview` remains structurally represented.

10. No speculative enterprise risk/asset/vulnerability platform, migration, deployment, customer connector, real client data or compliance/certification verdict is introduced.
11. The checked-in SQL is explicitly a design contract, not a migration, and is coherent with the machine-readable model and synthetic coverage contract.
12. Exact-head GitHub validation is green after final reconciliation.

## Verdict

After the dependency clears, write exactly one formal `PASS`, `FAIL` or `INDETERMINATE` with evidence and blocking findings. Worker B must not repair, merge, migrate, deploy or authorize real client data.

items.title: Measure and bound storage, transport, and maintenance growth
items.body:
## Outcome and ownership

Make Dactyl's storage operations predictable as repositories accumulate more history and payloads. Measure and reduce transport, allocation, and physical maintenance overhead while preserving SQLite compatibility, ordered atomic writes, typed results, and explicit backend selection.

This is the adapter companion to [decapod #1630](https://github.com/DecapodLabs/decapod/issues/1630). decapod owns canonical semantic records, content identity, events, projections, retention, and migration ordering. The authenticated service owns remote authorization, database execution, and resource policy. Dactyl owns parameter binding, physical execution, transport, normalization, and the documented maintenance primitives.

Dactyl is a Rust storage driver. Its production source does not implement an agent harness, transcript store, semantic event journal, or application checkpoint system. Its own `.decapod/data/decapod.db` is a separate decapod dogfooding store; measuring that store is an explicit deliverable below. Do not create a second copy of decapod's semantic schema inside this crate.

## Reviewed baseline and evidence boundary

Source review is pinned to main commit [1fa52a232e1d34a27be28d158298805ffc175ffc](https://github.com/DecapodLabs/dactyl/tree/1fa52a232e1d34a27be28d158298805ffc175ffc), crate version 0.11.1. These are code observations, not benchmark results.

| Surface | Current behavior and consequence to measure |
|---|---|
| [Public contract](https://github.com/DecapodLabs/dactyl/blob/1fa52a232e1d34a27be28d158298805ffc175ffc/src/contract.rs) | `OpenOptions` exposes access mode and lock timeout, with no public result-row, cell-byte, aggregate-result, or batch-operation budget. `StorageContext` validates an opaque versioned object rather than interpreting tenant fields. |
| [Row representation](https://github.com/DecapodLabs/dactyl/blob/1fa52a232e1d34a27be28d158298805ffc175ffc/src/rows.rs) | `Rows(Vec<Row>)` owns complete results. Each public `Row` owns column-name strings and JSON values. Blob parameters serialize as JSON byte arrays; returned blobs use per-byte JSON values. The memory and wire expansion need measurements. |
| [Local adapter](https://github.com/DecapodLabs/dactyl/blob/1fa52a232e1d34a27be28d158298805ffc175ffc/src/adapter/sqlite/mod.rs) | `query_rows` materializes the full result and clones column metadata per row. Mutating atomic batches collect results inside one transaction. `inspect_schema` performs an exact row count for every table. SQLite itself owns its pager and journal. |
| [Supabase adapter](https://github.com/DecapodLabs/dactyl/blob/1fa52a232e1d34a27be28d158298805ffc175ffc/src/adapter/supabase.rs) | Existing 4 MiB serialized request/response limits, 5-second connection and 15-second request budgets, bounded response reader, redirect refusal, and credential redaction are useful starting points. Request serialization allocates the complete JSON body before checking its length. Decoding and normalization add allocations beyond body bytes. Each request builds its blocking client in a joined worker thread. |
| [Neon adapter](https://github.com/DecapodLabs/dactyl/blob/1fa52a232e1d34a27be28d158298805ffc175ffc/src/adapter/neon/mod.rs) | The existing response path calls `response.bytes()` without an explicit bounded reader. Equivalent request/body budgets are not configured in this adapter. Do not claim Supabase's current limits cover every backend. |
| [Recovery implementation](https://github.com/DecapodLabs/dactyl/blob/1fa52a232e1d34a27be28d158298805ffc175ffc/src/adapter/sqlite/recovery.rs) | Logical rebuild already steps source rows individually. It converts values and prepares/executes an insert for each row. Measure repeated preparation, conversion, transaction, and sync overhead; do not describe it as loading an entire table into memory. |

No actual dogfooding database was available to this review. No Dactyl database size, per-agent growth rate, tenant capacity, compression ratio, or performance improvement has been established.

## 1. Inventory Dactyl's native decapod store first

Run the supported native decapod diagnostic surface against `dactyl/.decapod/data/decapod.db`, using the inventory contract developed in decapod #1630. This is Dactyl's member of the coordinated repository inventory. Its size has not been supplied and must be measured, not inferred from another repository.

Record the database and decapod versions, collection time, workload window, and whether the sample was live or quiesced. Keep these quantities distinct:

- Main-file apparent bytes and allocated filesystem bytes; WAL, SHM, rollback journal, and associated backup/artifact bytes.
- Page size, total/free pages, table/index allocation where supported, and live logical payload bytes. Explain unavailable metrics rather than treating them as zero.
- Counts and byte distributions for the caller-owned record families, including large values, repeated payload hashes, and projection/event copies where the native diagnostic identifies them.
- Growth over a reproducible operation window, including reads, writes, retries, concurrent processes, and agent activity. One person can generate many agent operations; a person count is not a storage workload.
- Estimated reclaimable space versus retained live evidence, with no deletion, vacuum, journal change, or recovery as part of inventory.

Use supported native interfaces for machine-owned state, not ad hoc SQL or direct file edits under `.decapod/data`. If the diagnostic capability is missing, record that dependency and obtain it through the decapod companion issue. Add only the smallest physical read-only Dactyl primitive it requires; semantic classification stays in decapod.

Publish redacted aggregate findings and deterministic synthetic fixtures. Do not commit live databases, raw evidence, tokens, customer identifiers, or source payloads. The tracked legacy SQLite test fixture is a compatibility fixture, not a measurement of the dogfooding store.

## 2. Specify resource budgets before changing representation

Add an explicit, versioned resource contract with documented defaults, units, enforcement points, and compatibility treatment. Prefer additive construction/options APIs; changing a public struct used in literals can itself break consumers.

Define budgets for SQL/context/parameter bytes, maximum cell bytes, result rows, aggregate decoded result bytes, serialized request/response bytes, operations per atomic batch, and operation duration. Separate raw payload bytes, JSON bytes, decoded values, and transient allocation estimates. A 4 MiB body is not a 4 MiB memory guarantee.

Use checked arithmetic and bounded serialization so oversized requests stop before constructing an arbitrarily large second copy. Bound response reading and parsing, including metadata, nesting, column counts, error bodies, and one very large cell. Include exact-limit, limit-plus-one, empty, malformed, and integer-overflow cases.

Map violations to stable typed outcomes with redacted diagnostics. Distinguish a local resource limit from a remote policy denial and from a malformed response. A truncated result must never appear to be a complete successful query.

Document which guarantees are per call or connection and which require caller concurrency limits. Dactyl must not acquire a hidden scheduler, unbounded queue, or process-global tenant policy. If timeout/cancellation cannot stop an executing backend operation, state the remaining work and uncertain-outcome boundary.

Carry equivalent bounded behavior into the retained Neon adapter through a documented compatibility path. Keep disabled-feature behavior, explicit route selection, and cloud failure without local fallback.

## 3. Reduce copying and support bounded reads

Measure column metadata duplication, JSON value cloning, binary expansion, and whole-result materialization separately. Optimize avoidable copies inside normalization without changing observable scalar values, column ordering, affected counts, generated keys, or error categories.

The current owned `Rows` API must remain usable. If changing its public fields would break compatibility, introduce an additive bounded row visitor, cursor, or page representation rather than silently replacing them. Shared column metadata is useful only if ownership and lifetimes remain explicit.

Specify the bounded API's termination, cancellation, resource release, partial failure, and consistency behavior. A consumer stopping early must release statements and connections predictably. Never implement a supposedly bounded remote read by fetching an unlimited result and slicing it in memory.

Pagination keys, stable ordering, query selection, and semantic completeness belong to the caller/service. Dactyl may carry a versioned opaque continuation and capability information; it must not rewrite arbitrary SQL into guessed pagination or reconstruct a domain query language. Prove the supported profile with actual remote execution. Existing read-only batches must not acquire an undocumented cross-query snapshot guarantee.

Preserve NULL versus empty values, signed integer boundaries, finite reals, text, blobs, and supported alias behavior. Local positional duplicate-column behavior and the Supabase object's duplicate-alias restriction need explicit compatibility tests.

The current wire uses JSON byte arrays. Any compact binary encoding or compression requires a negotiated/versioned extension and old/new peer tests. Define compressed-body, decompressed-body, raw-cell, and decoded-memory limits independently; cover expansion bombs, malformed streams, unknown codecs, and cancellation. Compression is optional optimization after measurement, not a substitute for normalized data or bounded reads.

## 4. Preserve atomicity and control retry amplification

Set batch limits before starting a local transaction or sending a remote mutation whenever possible. A single atomic batch stays one physical transaction; never split it into independently committed chunks to satisfy a byte or operation limit.

For local execution, detect result-budget violations while rollback is still possible. For a hosted operation, require the service to enforce its own execution and response budgets within the transaction where that guarantee is supported.

Explicitly distinguish:

| Outcome | Required meaning |
|---|---|
| Preflight rejection | No mutation was attempted. |
| Confirmed transactional failure | The service/backend proves rollback of the batch. |
| Timeout, disconnect, or invalid/oversized response after execution | Commit may have occurred; client-side rejection does not prove rollback. |

Keep automatic write retries out of Dactyl. A retryable error category is not permission to repeat an uncertain mutation. Caller/service idempotency and reconciliation must remain effective across response loss, concurrent retries, and version changes.

Test failures after the first operation and around commit/response delivery. Verify no unintended duplicate state or evidence when the caller retries through its documented idempotency protocol. Report attempted requests, committed logical operations, wire bytes, and storage growth separately so retry amplification cannot disappear inside a successful-operation average.

When decapod replaces repeated bodies with immutable content references, transport the identifier/digest/version as opaque values. The semantic owner defines canonical bytes, digest scope, collision handling, authorization, reference integrity, garbage collection, and retention. Dactyl must not compute competing identities, deduplicate across security boundaries, or expand references into stored duplicate bodies.

## 5. Keep physical diagnostics and maintenance bounded

Provide a lightweight physical inventory path that does not require exact counts of every table on routine connection open. Preserve existing catalog behavior or introduce explicit options/capabilities; report sampled/estimated and exact measurements distinctly.

Benchmark backup and logical rebuild separately from normal reads. Recovery already streams source rows. Investigate prepared-insert reuse, unnecessary value conversion, and transaction/sync frequency before adding another abstraction.

Bound private staging work and publish its disk-space, elapsed-time, lock, and interruption behavior. Batching writes to an unpublished rebuild destination is a separate optimization from splitting a public atomic batch. Preserve all existing recovery guarantees: original and sidecars retained, private staging permissions, source identity checks, validation before activation, no-clobber publication, directory sync, and explicit rollback/failure reporting.

No automatic vacuum, checkpoint-policy changes, retention deletion, schema migration, or repair on open/read/write. SQLite remains the local file format; Dactyl must not reintroduce a custom snapshot or journal. Existing compatible files remain usable without deleting or converting user state.

## 6. Coordinate schema and wire compatibility

decapod #1630 owns canonical data refactoring and migration sequencing. The hosted service owns its implementation of the corresponding portable operations and authorization. This issue owns transporting and executing that contract without duplicating its semantic schema.

Before consumer adoption, record a compatibility matrix covering old/new caller, adapter, and service versions; wire version; supported scalar profile; batch limits; paging capability; and explicit rejection of unsupported combinations. A generic adapter capability does not prove a deployed service accepts every SQL statement or value type.

Use one caller-owned schema/conformance fixture revision for the new data shape and retain representative existing-file fixtures. Prove fresh initialization, upgrade/reopen, failed migration rollback, and unsupported downgrade through the caller's migration harness. Dactyl supplies atomic physical operations and capability errors; it does not maintain a second applied-migration ledger.

Roll out limits and transport extensions without silently reinterpreting old requests. Keep a documented library/service rollback path. If a semantic migration makes an older caller unsafe, refusal must occur at the owning compatibility boundary, not as accidental query failures after partial writes.

## 7. Reproducible growth and failure proof

Build synthetic, deterministic workloads with controllable record count, payload size, duplicate-body ratio, column width, history depth, batch size, and reader/writer concurrency. Include small routine requests, large single values, many narrow rows, repeated binary values, mostly distinct values, and retry storms.

Use staged dataset sizes, for example 10,000, 100,000, and 1,000,000 records where the dedicated benchmark budget permits. These are proposed benchmark scales, not measured production loads. Keep ordinary CI bounded and provide a reproducible larger-run command with environment metadata.

Measure baseline and candidate under the same conditions:

- Main-file/live-payload/index/WAL/staging bytes and growth per committed operation.
- Serialized and decoded bytes, peak process memory, and allocations/copies where measurable.
- Query, write, batch, backup, and rebuild latency distributions; lock time; rows processed; and throughput.
- Connection/client/worker setup cost and peak concurrent resources, including free-function versus explicit connection reuse.
- Read amplification, commit/rollback behavior, and bytes spent on rejected or retried work.

Do not add unlike storage measures together or present SQLite file size as PostgreSQL capacity. A fixed-page read should have a resource envelope tied to its requested page/cell limits rather than total stored history. A single oversized cell should fail predictably. The owned legacy API's remaining materialization cost must be documented.

Choose numeric regression thresholds from the recorded baseline and intended budgets, then check them into the benchmark contract. Report overhead reductions separately from changes in canonical payload retention. No unmeasured compression or deduplication savings count as acceptance.

## Acceptance and existing work

- [ ] Native decapod inventory for Dactyl's own dogfooding database is recorded, or explicitly blocked on unavailable input/capability; no inferred size or fabricated zero.
- [ ] Resource contract covers raw, serialized, decoded, and transient growth with deterministic boundary tests and a consumer compatibility path.
- [ ] Local and remote supported reads can remain bounded; oversized results cannot silently truncate.
- [ ] Batches preserve ordered results and all-or-nothing mutation semantics; uncertain commit outcomes and retry amplification are tested.
- [ ] Existing-file compatibility and backup/recovery custody survive large-payload, contention, fault, and interruption tests.
- [ ] Shared fixtures exercise the agreed compact semantic shape without moving ownership into Dactyl.
- [ ] Existing `storage_fixtures`, `supabase_contract`, `supabase_service`, `sqlite_maintenance`, and recovery tests are extended at their actual seams; feature combinations and existing regression gates remain green.
- [ ] Evidence labels distinguish local SQLite, synthetic HTTP, an executing SQLite remote mock, real PostgreSQL, and protected hosted execution. Unavailable live evidence is never recorded as passed.
- [ ] Public API/service documentation, living architecture/interface specs, and release notes reflect the supported behavior and measured limitations.

This issue adds the growth/resource contract rather than replacing [#91](https://github.com/DecapodLabs/dactyl/issues/91) adapter work, [#100](https://github.com/DecapodLabs/dactyl/issues/100) logical connector/session work, or [#94](https://github.com/DecapodLabs/dactyl/issues/94) release adoption. Preserve [#52](https://github.com/DecapodLabs/dactyl/issues/52) schema ownership, [#55](https://github.com/DecapodLabs/dactyl/issues/55) contention/error semantics, and [#88](https://github.com/DecapodLabs/dactyl/issues/88)/[#95](https://github.com/DecapodLabs/dactyl/issues/95) maintenance guarantees. Existing remote conformance work remains the evidence dependency, not a reason to treat a mock as deployed proof.


## Decapod consumer evidence (2026-11-14)

[Decapod PR #1682](https://github.com/DecapodLabs/decapod/pull/1682) records actual official 0.144.4 native read-only inspection of Dactyl's local dogfood store: main apparent length 25,985,024 bytes before/after; overall sampled coverage; unmigrated v1 storage metadata. This is an actual local inventory, not measured compaction savings or hosted service proof. [Decapod PR #1678](https://github.com/DecapodLabs/decapod/pull/1678) separately adopts SDK 0.16.1 with explicit bounded consumer compatibility and pending hosted verification. No Dactyl schema ownership or SDK-global budget policy is moved into Decapod.

Inventory delivery update: Decapod PR #1682 merged as `fded2dd0b5f02f9c874301d4b98cfd59ad188357`. The recorded observations retain their sampled/local-only scope; merger does not establish compaction savings, hosted cutover or the remaining Decapod #1630 acceptance conditions.

items.title: Shared Developer Runtime v1 — approved fresh-install contract for multi-project recovery
items.body:
# Shared Developer Runtime v1 — one shared host, reliable project handoff

Contract Revision: 5

TaskState: ACCEPTED_ON_BOUNDED_REAL_WORLD_EVIDENCE / FURTHER_DEEP_TESTING_NOT_REQUIRED

**Delivery boundary:** The reviewed shared-runtime v1 source is integrated on protected `main`. Its core execution passed a **fresh exact-current-main install on hNL01-Key**, and existing **connected Test v0.1.15** passed the PTY/Browser client subset. The two hosts/versions were tested separately; neither fresh-current-main client refresh nor exhaustive fault conditions are claimed. The Owner has accepted this **bounded practical verification as sufficient** for the current shared-runtime stage (see the revised verification section). Immutable Stable [v0.1.16](https://github.com/ach1992/ai-server-agent/releases/tag/v0.1.16) is now published at `42ce69959dc08c3a85f1aa3e6c7312f0648599b0` and includes the source remediations from PRs #168/#169. **Release publication is not installation:** existing occupied Development/Validation Agent hosts retain their independently installed versions until a separately authorized update. This Issue's bounded tests and closure do not authorize host deployment.

**Approved first-install baseline:** new runtime capability work targets an authorized empty supported Linux host; do not manufacture speculative migration logic for older Agent generations. This does not waive future update discipline, direct-client contract compatibility, or recovery *within* the newly installed generation.

**Historical local archive resolved:** The obsolete, local-only `archive/issue137-local-unique-tests-945d999` branch (commit `945d9995d2e37fe78fa73dd21668ea30ae44e314`) contained one pre-merge patch and four older tests. Its two distinct cases were ported into [PR #169](https://github.com/ach1992/ai-server-agent/pull/169) and are on `main`; the one-deadline/foreign-terminal and service-claim-quota cases also have current tests. After verifying those exact counterparts, the unneeded local archive branch was deleted under the Owner's cleanup authorization. Do **not** recreate or cherry-pick its obsolete implementation. No unique reviewable active work was discarded.

## Outcome and boundaries

- **Product:** a vendor-neutral, single Agent+Executor MCP development/control plane on one dedicated Linux host. Different projects' Masters may work concurrently; **only one active Master per project outcome**, with successor chats following the same GitHub Issue/PR. The Agent does **not** implement Master elections, project ownership registry or chat migration.
- **Durable truth:** Git/GitHub owns source, Issues, scope, PRs, commits, review, CI and releases. Agent owns only a **small protected bounded execution state**. Successor Masters use existing repository/worktree discovery to verify remote, branch, HEAD, uncommitted changes and worktree before touching runtime.
- **Resource economy:** share one Agent/Executor, host, systemd, toolchains/caches, pinned Node/Playwright/Chromium installation. Separate **only** per-operation CWD, bounded job/service identity/lifetime, same-principal terminal handles, and opt-in browser cookies/storage. No new database, always-on monitor, scheduler/queue, generic process registry, distributed lock, port allocator, per-project Agent/container/UID, or second Browser installation.
- **Security truth:** keep the existing bearer/TLS/policy/approval/audit/root-vs-worker boundaries. Workspace/path labels and per-workspace filters **do not** provide filesystem sandboxing or project ACLs; projects may share the same authenticated principal and worker UID. Root actions retain their current authorization requirements. Do not expose other principals' terminal/Browser handles.

## First-install decisions (avoid useless work)

- Build/test from **empty Agent state** in an authorized disposable clean environment. Reuse the existing Go executor, protected job state, session broker, systemd runner, repository/worktree tools and Browser engine; **no total rewrite**.
- **No requirement:** support version-1 claim files, old `operation_id` fingerprints, old status/profile directories, previous installer migration, old tool-schema adapters or lossless legacy update. Old-compatibility code that is no longer useful may be deleted as part of related source changes; don't create new migration tests or dual state engines.
- **Required within the new installation:** an ongoing new-baseline job/service/terminal must be observable/recoverable when the **chat or Agent/Executor process** reconnects/restarts to the extent its documented backend survives; no blind side-effect replay, no unbounded state growth. **Host reboot need not restart transient services**. Long-term cross-version state migration is **not** a v1 completion gate.
- Ordinary existing MCP tools/defaults should be retained when low-cost and helpful to integrations, but compatibility with a prior installed runtime is **not a reason** to add special code. Stable behavior/security improvements must remain easy to implement from this baseline.

## Accepted slice A — Workspace and cold-chat visibility (implemented; bounded verification accepted)

1. Add optional canonical, **existing** worker `workspace` CWD to `run_command` and `start_job`; validate under configured workspace root, reuse established path checks, fail on invalid/ambiguous workspace. When omitted, use the **workspace root as default worker CWD**. For the new first-install baseline, unify **worker HOME and XDG config/cache/data across `run_command`, `start_job`, Terminal/LSP/DAP** using the **already-provisioned, root-validated, worker-owned `state_dir/worker-home`**. This is one shared private worker HOME for all projects, **not per-project HOME or another cache system**; reject a missing/untrusted home instead of reverting to a writable project path. The prior implementation's one-shot HOME=`workspace_root` is historical and is not required to persist in this fresh-install target. Preserve `run_root_command` and root-job HOME/CWD/authority under `/root` and existing approval gates. For `start_job(root=true)`, a supplied worker-only `workspace` must **fail clearly** instead of being silently ignored. **A workspace may be any existing permitted directory, not necessarily a Git repository**: do not run Git discovery or create worktrees automatically on every command. For repository-backed development, the Master separately verifies remote/branch/HEAD via existing Git tools rather than trusting a workspace name. No claim that arbitrary shell commands cannot traverse outside CWD.
2. Every **new** persistent job (including no caller-supplied `operation_id`) receives **one small durable protected record** with job ID, principal/class, canonical effective CWD, `kind=task|service`, creation/status and a bounded non-secret purpose (**required for `kind=service` so successors can recognize it; optional for tasks**). Reuse job status/log/claim infrastructure, **not a second registry**. New idempotency keys remain principal-scoped; material fingerprint includes command, authority, effective CWD and kind. **Cross-project collision guard:** multiple Masters can share one MCP principal, so callers must choose a stable, non-secret, per-project/per-task-unique `operation_id` (not bare reusable `build`/`serve`). Reusing a key with a different CWD/kind must fail closed; do not introduce a global Master/key registry. A lost reply must be reconciled before any differently keyed retry.
3. Implement **one bounded read-only `runtime_list`** for **tasks, services, and recoverable Terminal records** using existing job files/systemd/terminal recovery records. Optional exact `workspace` and `kind` filters, **active-first then newest deterministic order**, fixed small output cap, observation timestamp and explicit `truncated` indicator; **do not add pagination unless real usage justifies it**. An active filtered job/service should not disappear behind completed history. Return truthful state, opaque handles only where permitted, age/retention and capacity indicators. **Passive inventory must not call mutating `job_status`, expiry-reap/stop, cleanup, mkdir or claim-reconciliation paths.** Do not return or audit raw `systemctl list-units` descriptions (they can contain command strings); parse only verified unit identifiers. Races/invalid records -> honest unknown/limited result, never fabricated proof. Never include command text, logs, secrets, arbitrary process lists or infer Master ownership.
4. **Do not duplicate `browser_status` in `runtime_list`**: existing `browser_status` already reports Browser engine readiness and busy/lease state. If better busy diagnostics are needed, improve that existing tool instead. Terminal handles: discover only the same authenticated principal and exact workspace; worker terminal first. Root-terminal discovery must not bypass existing explicit privileged approval/authority (omit root handles from v1 discovery if that cannot be proven without an extra framework). Verify epoch/TTL/backend on reconnect; avoid cross-principal takeover. Preserve the current **one-hour Terminal lifetime**; an expired/vanished PTY is not recoverable merely because its old ID can be listed. Discovery is passive and must not refresh expiry.

## Accepted slice B — service lifecycle on the existing Job engine (implemented; bounded verification accepted)

- `start_job` defaults to a finite `task`; an explicitly marked `service` is an intentional long-running **foreground** development process supervised within the existing systemd unit. Do not rely on `nohup`, `&` or double-fork escaping its unit; `accepted` means **launched, not application-ready**. For HTTP/DB readiness, use existing `run_command` probes and `job_output`; no health-check service/registry. Reuse **one** protected job record/claim/log/status/stop path, **one `ai-job-*` unit namespace** and existing lifecycle lock/systemd execution; no second process manager.
- Keep the current finite task cap (four) and a separately bounded, **conservative** service cap. Count *all* active Agent-owned systemd units and classify only from **trusted matching records**. The service label aids discovery; it is **not** an ownership proof or another unique-name registry. Missing/corrupt type or ambiguous systemd state fails safely and may block new admission. Preserve finite disk/log/state limits and safe uninstall/purge blocking for both types. Do not interpret a service quota as free CPU/RAM. Prefer simple finite task/service quotas, bounded retained logs/claims and existing disk reserve. Add modest measured per-unit systemd memory/CPU limits where warranted; **do not require an adaptive host-memory prediction engine, new scheduler or dozens of config knobs** (reuse #118 only for justified operator settings). A `job_stop` acknowledgement is not proof that a service has actually terminated; verify authoritative unit status.
- Reconnection survives MCP chat/Agent/Executor disconnect while the transient systemd unit is active. **No automatic host-reboot autostart promise**. Diagnose port conflicts and capacity simply; do not create a port broker. No new privileged service capability beyond existing root-policy/approval limits.

## Accepted slice C — Browser state within existing Browser engine (implemented; bounded verification accepted)

- On relevant `browser_run`, `browser_e2e`, `browser_session_open` paths, allow opt-in `profile_mode=isolated|shared` (precise name a normal engineering choice); default stays current `shared`.
- Reuse pinned Playwright/Chromium engine, broker and **one global exclusive Browser admission**. Isolated execution uses a bounded ephemeral private profile/context with independent cookies/localStorage and cleanup after verified close/crash/expiry, **only for Agent-owned ephemeral paths and after verifying the former Browser holder is stopped**; keep shared profile untouched. Verify compatibility with existing `launchPersistentContext` before choosing mechanism. No parallel-browser guarantee, separate engine, external database isolation or cross-chat Browser state recovery promise.

## Cold successor procedure (no chat dependency)

1. Read GitHub controlling Issue/PR/approval, latest authoritative commit/review/CI.
2. Discover the exact Git remote, checkout/worktree, branch, HEAD and dirty state; do not overwrite existing work.
3. Use `runtime_list` for current workspace tasks/services/eligible same-owner PTY; call existing `browser_status` separately **only when Browser work is required**.
4. Continue safely; if a Job action has unknown completion, reconcile before starting another. Expired/different-principal sessions are not transferable.
5. Commit/push meaningful work, keep only unresolved intent/gates in GitHub. Unpushed source and lost-host browser state cannot be guaranteed recoverable.

## Owner-accepted bounded verification (Contract Revision 5, 2026-10-17)

**Owner scope decision:** The current representative, real-host and connected-client evidence is **sufficient for acceptance of the shared-runtime v1 implementation for this stage**. Do **not** keep escalating to expensive/invasive fault injection, prolonged soak, complete host-loss simulations or forced simultaneous fresh-install/client combinations merely to check every historical test-matrix box. Such work is **no longer a prerequisite for closing #137**. This is a *change to required verification depth*, not a claim that unexecuted scenarios passed or that their underlying risks disappeared.

**Verified evidence used for acceptance:**

- [x] Protected-`main` implementation and exact-candidate CI/Security plus author-separated review of [PR #168](https://github.com/ach1992/ai-server-agent/pull/168) and [PR #169](https://github.com/ach1992/ai-server-agent/pull/169); no new source patch is pending in this Issue.
- [x] **Real, fresh, temporary, local-only Agent install** of exact `main@4dab0bee8bb0afe5cab7bbdf1cec9e9ee1792b29` on supported Debian 13 / Landlock ABI 6 `hNL01-Key`: authenticated 59-tool MCP catalog; two independent seeded Git repositories plus one non-Git scratch; correct worker CWD/defaults/shared private HOME/XDG; worker project identity checks, invalid workspace rejection, same-key idempotency and differing-workspace conflict; honest passive runtime inventory; four task/two service capacity/refusal/release; foreground HTTP service surviving Agent/Executor restart and reconnected authenticated client; service stop proven by HTTP closure. **Official purge and verified complete test-owned cleanup**; other host services preserved. [Exact evidence](https://github.com/ach1992/ai-server-agent/issues/137#issuecomment-6230657776).
- [x] **Actual already-connected ChatGPT Test instance** with installed **Stable v0.1.15**: real PTY open/read/write/resize/interrupt/reconnect and same-workspace inventory, wrong-workspace denial, closure; real local Browser form and cross-call session flow, isolated cookie/localStorage non-leakage into a second isolated or shared profile; exclusive admission/busy diagnostics and post-exception release. Temp resources cleaned. [Exact evidence](https://github.com/ach1992/ai-server-agent/issues/137#issuecomment-6230878618).

**Explicitly not proven, and not acceptance blockers under this Owner decision:** one **same-host** post-PR169 fresh install with actual ChatGPT catalog re-registration/refresh; actual root/cross-principal PTY matrix; claim-publication crash injection; unusual disk exhaustion/pressure/retention edges; hour-long soak/expiry; total host-loss/reboot recreation; full-stack Browser/PTY optional-package installation on `hNL01-Key`. Some coverage exists as source tests/CI and some on distinct installed/client versions; do not present that as identical-environment E2E proof. The Go CDN had returned 404 on hNL01; the valid SHA-verified fallback binary-install path passed, not the upstream direct Go-download branch.

**Risk-driven future work:** Re-test only when an actual defect, meaningful compatibility/client change, concrete security/data-risk finding or high-consequence code change gives an actionable reason. Maintain existing relevant CI/Security and independently reviewed-source gates; this acceptance decision **does not authorize release, deploy, occupied-host reinitialization or skipping required checks for later changed source**. Keep [#99](https://github.com/ach1992/ai-server-agent/issues/99) independently scoped to conditional native file/media client delivery and [#59](https://github.com/ach1992/ai-server-agent/issues/59) as the historical broader E2E evidence owner; neither is proof of unperformed tests.

## Acceptance ownership and authority

- #137 owns shared-host multi-project and fresh-install A/B/C acceptance. #59 owns the broader GitHub source/edit/build/test/commit/push and lost-server recovery program; #99 owns genuine client-visible binary/image/file delivery; #60/#66 own Terminal/session mechanics; #63 Browser; completed #118 owns the original runtime-controls contract. Do not duplicate these full acceptance suites here.
- Durable host/process/security architecture belongs in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `docs/DEVELOPER-RUNTIME.md`. Git/PR/CI/Releases and real installed clients own current implementation and delivery proof, not historical checkpoint text in this Issue.
- **Authority:** accepted first-install design is not permission to overwrite an occupied Agent, delete unknown worktrees or unique fixtures, write another repository, merge code, release, deploy or run destructive fault tests without the applicable Owner/security gate. Use only an independently authorized disposable clean host.
- Previous completed documentation/source work in [PR #138](https://github.com/ach1992/ai-server-agent/pull/138) and [PR #139](https://github.com/ach1992/ai-server-agent/pull/139), and their historical root-test/review/CI evidence, remain recoverable from GitHub. Their previous candidate SHAs, temporary worktrees and Draft status are not live state.
