> Depends on: #131, #125, #48

## Why
Two commercially proven agent patterns exist only as proprietary silos. Outbound token brokering: Auth0 Token Vault is GA, Descope ships Outbound Apps with over 50 templates, WorkOS ships Pipes; no OSS equivalent exists, and an open vault with a template registry could become the default place agents get scoped third-party access. Human-in-the-loop approval: Auth0 (Async Authorization GA), WorkOS, and IBM with Yubico all monetize approval-gated agent actions today; an OSS implementation on a durable delivery backbone would be a first. Both are flagged exploratory bets, not core commitments, because the agent market is moving: the hedge is that they compose almost entirely from already shipped substrate (CIBA plus RAR from 13.8, exchange from 13.2, envelope encryption from M5), so a pivot strands little code. Storing users' third-party credentials also raises the stakes on at-rest protection, which is why per-tenant envelope encryption is a hard dependency, honoring the no-unexportable-data and optional-infrastructure covenants throughout.

## What
Token vault (exploratory flag):
- Store, refresh, and scope users' third-party OAuth tokens and API keys; start with generic OAuth2/OIDC and API-key connectors plus a template registry seam, not bespoke per-provider integrations.
- Exposure via RFC 8693-style exchange: an agent presents its IronAuth token and receives a downstream token scoped by per-agent policy; org-scoped grants govern which agents may access which connections.
- Encrypted at rest with per-tenant envelope encryption; refresh scheduling with per-connection failure isolation; full audit of store, exchange, refresh, and revoke.
- Data model: vault connections keyed to user, organization, and environment, with per-agent scoping rules and lifecycle (active, refresh-failed, revoked).

Async approval (exploratory flag):
- An agent's request for a seeded sensitive action creates a pending authorization; the human receives an out-of-band approval rendering the RAR authorization_details; tokens issue only on approval, via the CIBA poll and ping machinery.
- Denial and timeout paths issue nothing and are audited; approvals are bound to the specific authorization_details presented.
- IronBus is the optional durable delivery substrate for pending authorizations; a database-backed path is the default so the covenant holds.

Both features: off by default, enabled per environment behind exploratory flags with the maturity-ladder acknowledgment; audit events throughout; documented threat notes on vault compromise blast radius.

## Out of scope
- Bespoke per-provider connector catalogs (Google, Slack, Jira specifics beyond the generic connectors used in tests); templates come later.
- Agent principal modeling: owned by "Model agent identities as first-class principals" (13.7).
- CIBA and RAR protocol mechanics: owned by "Implement CIBA (poll and ping) with rich authorization requests" (13.8).
- Grant Management API endpoints (deferred per the Non-Goals and Deferred section).

## Spec references
- RFC 8693 (exchange shape for vault exposure).
- OpenID Connect CIBA Core 1.0 plus RFC 9396 (the approval composition).
- No normative vault spec exists; the vault exchange profile is documented in-repo with its exact semantics.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An agent exchanges its IronAuth token for a scoped downstream Google or GitHub token from the vault, with per-agent scoping enforced and the exchange audited.
- [ ] Vault contents are encrypted at rest with per-tenant keys; a raw database dump yields no usable third-party credentials.
- [ ] Stored-token refresh works and a failing connection isolates without affecting other connections.
- [ ] A seeded sensitive action blocks until an out-of-band approval renders its authorization_details; denial or timeout issues no tokens.
- [ ] Both features work with no IronBus configured; with IronBus enabled, pending approvals survive a delivery worker restart.
- [ ] Both features are off by default and gated by the exploratory acknowledgment.

## Verification
- Integration harness against a mock OAuth provider on every merge, plus an optional nightly job against real Google and GitHub apps.
- Failure-injection tests: worker restart mid-approval, refresh failure storms, approval timeout.
- Crypto review checklist for the at-rest path, recorded in the repo, plus a test proving dump non-usability.
- Audit contract tests covering every vault and approval event type.

## Dependency notes
- "Implement CIBA (poll and ping) with rich authorization requests": the approval flow is CIBA plus RAR; the pending-authorization machinery and details rendering come from there.
- "Implement RFC 8693 token exchange with no ambient trust": the vault is exposed through exchange semantics and reuses its revalidation discipline.
- "Implement per-tenant envelope encryption for PII and secrets": stored third-party credentials are the highest-value secret in the system and require per-tenant at-rest protection.

items.body:
# Launch QA tracker — Eliza app + Eliza Cloud, all surfaces

**Status as of 2026-07-05:** this issue is now tracker/history and high-signal launch context. It is no longer the single onboarding link for agents.

## Start Here

1. **Live kanban state:** https://github.com/orgs/elizaOS/projects/12
2. **Coordination room:** https://github.com/orgs/elizaOS/discussions/14292
3. **Agent/project workflow:** https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/develop/docs/AGENT_COORDINATION.md
4. **Evidence standard:** https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/develop/PR_EVIDENCE.md

Merged setup PR: https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/pull/14297

## Source-of-truth split

- **Project board = state and ownership.** Keep `Status` and `Claimed by` accurate.
- **Focused issues = work cards.** Scope, acceptance criteria, blockers, and durable evidence live on the work issue.
- **Pull requests = code plus proof.** Link the work issue/card and attach evidence per `PR_EVIDENCE.md`.
- **Discussion = coordination.** New agent intros, handoffs, blockers, multi-card status, and noisy chat move to Discussion #14292.
- **This tracker = launch rollup/history.** Keep only high-signal summaries here. Convert unresolved findings into focused issues/cards.

## Agent loop summary

1. Read root `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`, package-local agent docs, `PR_EVIDENCE.md`, the Project readme, and the relevant issue/card.
2. Pick an unclaimed `Todo` card or create a focused issue/card for new real work.
3. Comment `CLAIMING: <scope>` on the work issue with your lane tag, set Project `Status = Claimed`, and set `Claimed by = <tag>`.
4. Move to `In progress` when actively mutating code, config, deploys, or shared resources.
5. Post evidence on the issue and PR, then move the card to `Needs-agent-verify` or `needs-human-verify` per the board rules.
6. Do not move cards to `Done` or close this tracker unless nubs/a maintainer explicitly delegates that authority.

## Definition of done for the whole push

Every board card is `Done`; every launch finding is fixed-and-verified or explicitly deferred with a written reason; and nubs/maintainers have personally approved the required surfaces: browser console, app.elizacloud.ai, desktop app, phone APK, and relevant connector/cloud flows.

## Legacy note

The original issue body embedded the standing goal and board conventions directly in this tracker. Those durable rules moved into repo docs in PR #14297 so future agents do not need to scrape this issue comment history. Existing comments remain useful context and evidence history.

items.title: A tenant reaches a plugin on one path only, so seventeen plugins cannot be RLS-scoped
items.body:
Split out of #1277, which found that no plugin table has a row-level security policy. Writing the policies is not what blocks the other seventeen plugins. **The tenant does not reach them.**

## The measurement

`auth.WithTenantID` is the only thing that puts a tenant into a context, and it has exactly one non-test caller:

```
$ grep -rn 'WithTenantID(' --include='*.go' . | grep -v _test | grep -v 'func WithTenantID'
cmd/cleat-worker/main.go:1199:    ctx := auth.WithTenantID(r.Context(), tid)
```

HTTP middleware. Host calls from workflows and plugin background loops carry no tenant at all.

`engine.WithTenantID` is a different thing — an engine *option*, not a context value — and `cmd/cleat-worker/setup.go:1505-1511` already says so: *"there are two notions of tenant here and nothing else compares them."*

## What that costs

A fail-closed policy (`tenant_id = cleat.assert_tenant_set()`) raises when no tenant is set. So for any plugin with a background sweep, **"add a policy" and "break the sweep" are the same change**.

Classifying every non-test plugin access site by whether its context can hold a tenant — request-scoped (`r.Context()`) versus not:

| plugin | request | ctx | other |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| kvstore | 9 | 0 | 0 |
| featureflags | 7 | 1 | 0 |
| oauthprovider | 7 | 1 | 0 |
| slacknotify | 6 | 1 | 0 |
| eventstore | 3 | 2 | 0 |
| kafkaconnect | 3 | 2 | 0 |
| auditlog | 1 | 2 | 0 |
| ratelimiter | 3 | 5 | 0 |
| jobqueue | 4 | 6 | 0 |
| datadogexport | 6 | 6 | 0 |
| notifications | 8 | 7 | 0 |
| webhookingest | 8 | 7 | 0 |
| scheduler | 7 | 4 | 0 |
| scheduledbackup | 10 | 9 | 6 |
| blobstore | 7 | 15 | 0 |
| eventtriggers | 8 | 16 | 0 |
| pgvector | 0 | 13 | 0 |

Re-derive rather than quoting — this is a census of a growing population:

```
python3 - <<'PY'
import re, subprocess, collections
files=[f for f in subprocess.run(['git','ls-files','plugins/*.go'],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout.split()
       if not f.endswith('_test.go')]
call=re.compile(r'\.(?:Query|QueryRow|Exec|Begin)\(\s*([A-Za-z_][\w.()]*)')
by=collections.defaultdict(collections.Counter)
for f in files:
    for m in call.finditer(open(f).read()):
        a=m.group(1)
        by[f.split('/')[1]]['request' if a.startswith(('r.Context','req.Context'))
                            else 'ctx' if 'ctx' in a.lower() else 'other']+=1
for p in sorted(by): print(p, dict(by[p]))
PY
```

**kvstore is the only plugin whose every access site is request-scoped**, which is why #1277 adopts it and stops there.

State the limit of that classification: a `ctx` argument is a *sufficient* signal that no tenant is available, not proof the site could never have one. It is a conservative lower bound, and most of those sites are genuine cross-tenant sweeps — a scheduler scanning every tenant's due rows — which must keep working.

## The decision this needs

Not seventeen migrations. Two questions:

1. **Does a tenant belong in the context on the host-call path?** A host call happens on behalf of a workflow, and a workflow has a tenant. Today the plugin cannot see it.
2. **What does a legitimately cross-tenant sweep use?** Either a connection that is RLS-exempt by design — explicitly, so it is greppable and reviewable rather than accidental — or a loop that sets each tenant in turn and accepts the cost. Picking one is the prerequisite for every plugin after kvstore.

Until (2) is answered, adopting `TenantScoped` anywhere with a background loop converts a silent cross-tenant read into a silent empty result, which is not obviously an improvement.

## Why this is worth doing rather than leaving to the Go predicate

The predicate is what every plugin already relies on, and it is one forgotten `WHERE` from a cross-tenant read that no test can see. #1277 demonstrates the failure directly — with the policy removed, a query that names no tenant at all returns another tenant's row:

```
--- FAIL: one_tenant_cannot_read_another's_row
    tenant B sees 1 of tenant A's rows through a query that names no tenant at all, want 0
```

## Related

- #1277 — the mechanism, and kvstore as its one adopter
- #1098, #1239 — the same shape for the two memory tables
- #1157 — the dialect-skip guard, which this interacts with

Two further things found while tracing this, both worth separate consideration:

- **`admin.grant_plugin_to_tenant` and `admin.revoke_plugin_from_tenant` have zero references anywhere**, Go or test, and `RegisterPluginTables` — which feeds the `admin.plugin_tables` they read — has zero callers. There is a complete schema-per-tenant provisioning path for plugin tables that was built and never wired up, alongside the shared-table-with-`tenant_id` model every plugin actually uses. It should be removed or connected, not left ambiguous.
- **Every plugin test connects as a superuser or the table owner, and PostgreSQL lets both bypass row-level security.** A suite in that shape cannot observe a policy at all: kvstore's passed identically against a table with no policy on it. Anything asserting isolation has to go through `testutil.OpenPostgresRLSTestDB`.

items.body:
## Four-priority implementation checkpoint — 2026-10-22 UTC

**Release controls, monitoring configuration and public brand/intake work are implemented. Customer-delivery readiness is partially closed:** PermitPlate passed its live first-customer operational gate in founder-curated, score-free mode; Recovery's private-host acceptance and CaptureBrief's full source-custody/recovery acceptance remain open. No real payment, subscriber delivery or recovery outcome is asserted.

### 1. Release protection — accepted for RETALLY main

[PR #582](https://github.com/P00NSMASHER/github-value-hunt-ledger/pull/582) moved all four scheduled writers onto guarded pull requests. The active [Main ruleset](https://github.com/P00NSMASHER/github-value-hunt-ledger/rules/25608380) requires a current, successful unique `release-gate`, a pull request, zero human approvals, and no bypass. [PR #585](https://github.com/P00NSMASHER/github-value-hunt-ledger/pull/585) proved normal protected merging after all applicable checks passed, including Windows encrypted backup. The subsequent Group inquiry release below also merged through this protection. These claims apply to this repository; sibling repository protection is separate.

### 2. Delivery readiness — PermitPlate operationally ready; private acceptance remains open

- **PermitPlate:** [#124](https://github.com/P00NSMASHER/permitplate-nyc/pull/124), [#127](https://github.com/P00NSMASHER/permitplate-nyc/pull/127) and [#128](https://github.com/P00NSMASHER/permitplate-nyc/pull/128) added fresh provider/public-build evidence, ordered research refresh before readiness, and prevented rejected workflow completions from cancelling the private research queue. The actual [curated refresh](https://github.com/P00NSMASHER/permitplate-nyc/actions/runs/39713183687) and chained [live readiness run](https://github.com/P00NSMASHER/permitplate-nyc/actions/runs/39713244752) succeeded on main `a97759783c4d4df5da89f1213cee448df5f29c35`. At 02:47 UTC, the controller reported `READY_FOR_FIRST_PAID_CUSTOMER`, `FOUNDER_CURATED_NO_SCORE_V1`, all 12 internal gates passing, no required first-customer external failures, and matching current/private research at 4,279 candidates. [Sanitized evidence artifact](https://github.com/P00NSMASHER/permitplate-nyc/actions/runs/39713244752/artifacts/12397024043). `commerciallyProven=false`: real paid-subscriber acceptance, provider-backed delivery and real next-run duplicate suppression remain unproved. Separate scored-opportunity diagnostics still fail and are not certified by this founder-curated acceptance.
- **CaptureBrief:** [PR #71](https://github.com/P00NSMASHER/capturebrief/pull/71) repaired the FY2027 source observer and retired obsolete Netlify live checks. The actual [FY2027 observer run](https://github.com/P00NSMASHER/capturebrief/actions/runs/39711219762) retrieved HTTP 200, 1,607,260 bytes and 1,104 CSV rows, with a fresh checksum receipt. This proves that specific public fetch, not full original-source/catalog custody, private indexing, independent restore or customer release.
- **Recovery/private workbench:** fresh read-only inspection still found no attached policies on the separate workbench Access app and no active account tunnels. The connected operator device was offline. Actual private-host installation, encrypted off-device recovery and buyer-specific source/access acceptance remain unverified. Existing inquiry-operator access is separate and was preserved.

### 3. Monitoring and automation ownership — configuration repaired

CaptureBrief's replacement monitoring passed its actual merged-source runs. The mis-scoped research task was corrected, and the current Executive, Engineering, Evidence & Reconciliation, Website, QA & Delivery, and Applied Research roles were preserved under the concurrent owner reset. First post-reset cycles have completed for Executive and Engineering; Website, QA & Delivery and Applied Research completed with recorded `no_update`. Evidence & Reconciliation remains `in_progress` at this checkpoint, with no current result; it is not counted as a successful run. Old Roblox/wholesale result text belongs to older runs and is not evidence about the corrected cycles. No additional recurring tasks were created.

### 4. Brand and contact intake — merged and verified live

- CaptureBrief [#72](https://github.com/P00NSMASHER/capturebrief/pull/72) and PermitPlate [#125](https://github.com/P00NSMASHER/permitplate-nyc/pull/125) unified RETALLY affiliation, navigation and contact details while preserving existing offer prices, checkout links and legal operators. Both public sites were rechecked after deployment.
- RETALLY [PR #589](https://github.com/P00NSMASHER/github-value-hunt-ledger/pull/589) merged at `c46b7405d8f766334b16aede807acdbf3f2604ff`. Cloudflare Pages production deployment `fa4cfbc0-a154-4b4a-95ac-4d4e05f16757` succeeded at that exact commit.
- The [live Group contact page](https://www.retallyrecovery.com/contact/) now collects name, email, optional company, selected business, message and explicit consent. The new shared intake path uses Turnstile, bounded input, existing rate limits, durable D1 storage before notification, idempotent retries and a truthful saved-reference response. Existing freight intake behavior is retained. The [privacy disclosure](https://www.retallyrecovery.com/privacy) and operator runbook were updated.
- Validation included 37 API/client tests, existing migration/operator reconciliation checks, all applicable final-head and merged-source checks, and [65 responsive page checks with accessibility and keyboard validation](https://github.com/P00NSMASHER/github-value-hunt-ledger/actions/runs/39712603696). Independent ordinary unbusted HTTPS reads at 02:49 UTC confirmed the new canonical and immutable contact/privacy pages, matching served JavaScript and `GET /api/group-inquiry` returning `online:true`.
- No real inquiry, notification email or payment was submitted in this pass. Production availability and code validation are not a fresh end-to-end mailbox/customer acceptance.

**History convention:** this checkpoint supersedes earlier technical-state claims where they conflict, including draft-only Group intake, disabled contact flags, unprotected RETALLY main and mandatory separate human code review. It does not erase real customer/source, private-host, recovery, financial or branch-specific commercial-proof requirements. Earlier dated evidence is preserved below.

---

## Current technical closure — October 21, 2026

**RETALLY main protection is now ACTIVE.** Provider readback of [ruleset 25608380](https://github.com/P00NSMASHER/github-value-hunt-ledger/rules/25608380) confirms the default branch requires a pull request and the unique GitHub Actions `release-gate` check (integration 15368), with strict up-to-date enforcement, **zero required human approvals**, no bypass actors, no deletion and no force push. Branch metadata confirms `protected=true`; the connected user has `current_user_can_bypass=never`. The earlier zero-ruleset finding below is resolved for this repository. CaptureBrief, PermitPlate and Resonance protections are separate repository checks, not implied by RETALLY's rule.

- [PR #582](https://github.com/P00NSMASHER/github-value-hunt-ledger/pull/582) merged at `6e01088dcbab261a33a035f2c5679eaa28ea516c` after exact-head release, source, security and all six RecoveryWorks jobs passed, including Windows encrypted backup. Every scheduled writer now uses the guarded PR path, with no direct-main feature-flag fallback.
- The next actual Technology Intelligence publication completed through [PR #584](https://github.com/P00NSMASHER/github-value-hunt-ledger/pull/584), producing `7ebe4c78aec21280a4b855f0413fb6b3553f9990`. This verifies working PR-only publication; it predates ruleset activation and is not the post-protection canary.
- **Protected-release canary ACCEPTED:** [PR #585](https://github.com/P00NSMASHER/github-value-hunt-ledger/pull/585), exact head `c9cfe1606c8ae1714c0d40fc6f8061c9ee9ae866`, passed all applicable hosted checks, including Windows encrypted backup, and merged normally at `10a46e59875398bb6d77a6d761927111ab17da19` with no human review and no bypass. Post-merge API readback still shows main protected and the active strict `release-gate` ruleset. The source manifest now matches actual enforcement.
- **Public contact intake is already enabled.** Current production configuration has `FREIGHT_INQUIRY_ENABLED=1` and `FREIGHT_INQUIRY_MAILBOX_VERIFIED=1`; the existing Resend credential is bound without exposing its value. The October 17 controlled Turnstile → D1 → Resend → Zoho acceptance supersedes the October 8/14 disabled-intake instructions. See [current inquiry readiness](https://github.com/P00NSMASHER/github-value-hunt-ledger/blob/main/freight/site/INQUIRY_PRODUCTION_READINESS.md). Do not send redundant mail or restore obsolete Cloudflare Email Sending requirements.
- **Private customer work remains unaccepted.** Fresh Cloudflare metadata still shows zero attached policies on the separate workbench Access app and zero account tunnels. A green code release, enabled contact form or synthetic test does not prove customer source rights, a working private host, independent encrypted recovery, actual payment, delivery or bank/carrier settlement.

**History convention:** all dated sections below preserve earlier evidence. Where they describe disabled inquiry flags, an absent Resend path, unprotected RETALLY main or an obsolete separate human code-review requirement, this newer source/provider-backed checkpoint and the current code release policy supersede those particular statements. Real customer/source/privacy/financial evidence gates remain distinct.

---

## Current release and commercial-access gate — October 21, 2026

**Source-integrity and public-site work: largely ACCEPTED. Real-customer operations: NO-GO.** This is a dated evidence checkpoint, not an ongoing health monitor and not a replacement for the October 12 item-level scorecard preserved below.

- **RETALLY Group public:** the production Cloudflare Pages deployment was verified at exact commit `a411705d561acd5cc67da3e1bcc12fe025df2643`, matching the then-current GitHub `main`. Subsequent [PR #581](https://github.com/P00NSMASHER/github-value-hunt-ledger/pull/581) merged the two-file recursive CaptureBrief forbidden-field correction at `c7e44cb5c5a265f4d953cc2f5c02918482262195`; six exact-head and six merged-source checks passed. The corresponding Cloudflare Pages **production deployment succeeded at that exact merged commit**, independently confirmed through the provider's deployment inventory and the GitHub Cloudflare check. Provider publication is not separate HTTP/browser/device acceptance.
- **Oracle read-only monitoring:** authenticated, provider-backed GitHub OIDC/RPST [run #39632003542](https://github.com/P00NSMASHER/github-value-hunt-ledger/actions/runs/39632003542) passed exact private bucket and expected VM metadata checks; [PR #554](https://github.com/P00NSMASHER/github-value-hunt-ledger/pull/554) documented it and its post-merge CI passed. Effective denied-write/object-body operations, independent OCI Audit, encrypted off-device restore and customer-host acceptance are **not** established by that PASS.
- **Canonical database contract:** one connected **validation** instance exposes a schema-compatible `ai_business_os_prod` with an exact match to the public manifest SHA-256 and all 45 versioned migration IDs. The actual read-only RETALLY source query returned the expected structural fields; private identity-matching results remain outside this public issue. This **does not designate the validation instance as the authoritative production system**, approve its private business records, grant customer-data access, or close nine source-to-business mappings. Do not publish private IDs or counts in this issue. The live SQL access used the connected administration context, not a commissioned least-privilege production reader.
- **CaptureBrief producer:** source-locked outcome ledger handoff and same-second timestamp repairs merged in CaptureBrief PRs #66/#67. RETALLY's consumer is now pinned and recursively enforces the producer's forbidden-field policy in PR #581. The actual authenticated live outcome JSONL location, immutable custody, case/account identity and independent payment/settlement evidence remain **unverified**; keep the optional reader `NOT_CONNECTED`, not falsely empty.
- **Private workbench:** the separately configured Cloudflare Access app had **zero attached access policies** and the connected account had **zero tunnels** during read-only inspection. Do not enable a hostname or copy another app's allow policy until the actual host/service, approved operator identity, MFA and deny controls are accepted.

**Remaining external evidence, not a license to invent data:** identify the approved authoritative Business OS instance and restricted read executor; establish the genuine CaptureBrief ledger source or explicitly evidence non-initiation, then verify authorized account mapping; complete private host/tunnel/Access controls plus off-device encrypted recovery and denied-permission tests; finish actual buyer scope, contracting/compliance and independently authenticated payment/delivery evidence before real commercial actions. Do not create surrogate customer records, bind nine businesses by slug alone, remove release holds, send outreach, post payments, or incur spend.

---

## October 14 latest zero-spend technical checkpoint — current guidance

**Customer launch: NO-GO. New external spend authorized: $0.** Owner has deferred business registration/insurance purchase/legal-contract finalization and qualified independent human review until a credible first-customer opportunity. These are **deferred, not waived**; required legal contracting, insurance decisions, qualified reviewer, actual consent, access/MFA and funds controls must clear **before their corresponding commercial or confidential operations**. No prospect or carrier outreach without separate owner approval. Existing public informational website and the manual *unsent* email draft may remain; online inquiry, customer records, invoices, carrier claims, Stripe/hosted posting and production release remain disabled or unauthorized.

**Original customer-readiness scorecard remains 21 PASS / 15 BLOCKED / 1 FAIL (37), as last item-level acceptance on Oct 12.** That is 20 in-scope independently verified technical/material checks and one owner-confirmed contact-route check, not 21 live-customer approvals. Do not treat simulated human reviews or GitHub-green checks as production permission.

- **First-customer draft [#329](https://github.com/P00NSMASHER/github-value-hunt-ledger/pull/329), head `c3fd717656c0577a363c37ba78ed757dd1c69963`:** seven of seven current PR workflows passed; complete Freight **1,851 passed**. Existing source-only gate now blocks forged `VERIFIED` customer stages and false kickoff/publication authorization. R25 deferred, R37 hour/cash cap unapproved; historical hypothetical $2,500 zero-recovery exposure is **not a commitment or forecast**.
- **Invoice-reference review [#461](https://github.com/P00NSMASHER/github-value-hunt-ledger/pull/461), head `2b29356631dde93fe0b4325dcc5d1da003e14eb5`:** reconciled current #329 parent safely; 4 of 4 exact-head workflows passed, complete Freight **1,875 passed**. Synthetic duplicate-invoice review only; no live customer claims.
- **Still blocked:** R26 buyer-specific MFA/workspace; R27 signed confidentiality/source rights; R30 hosted custody **FAIL** despite separate unpublished security hardening; R31 authenticated provider/customer role proof; R34 retention/closure; R35 explicit source and permitted release; R36 old synthetic $1,650 attribution gap; R37 real effort/cash limits. R28 automated email and R29 Cloudflare Access are optional for a separately approved manual contact route, not evidence that full automation is ready. Stage-specific bank posting/fees R32–R33 cannot be proved before actual authorized events.

**Next action at zero spend:** preserve source tests, synthetic rehearsals and prepared templates. Only after an inbound qualified prospect, and with owner authorization, begin strictly nonconfidential screening and then close legally required pre-contract/service gates. No filing, vendor purchase, automated work schedule, reviewer contact, customer document ingestion, production merge/deployment or live financial operation occurred in this engineering pass.

---

## Current owner-directed update — 12 October 2026

**21 PASS / 15 BLOCKED / 1 FAIL** (20 independently verified within scope + one owner-confirmed phone/Zoho handoff). Ten separate AI simulated reviewer roles completed, defects corrected and retested. **1,409 Freight tests and all six exact-head workflows PASS.** Current draft #329 head: `7dabdd5dd928ecaa2ec255bebe2e1d6a9d094e37`.

Owner ordering: **legal identity/contracts/insurance last**. Phone/Zoho handoff is **OWNER_CONFIRMED complete**; no repeat request. Actual human reviewer appointment and buyer-specific MFA/access remain separate from simulated review. No release or real financial authority granted. See latest ten-reviewer execution comment and repository acceptance receipt. **Paying-customer activation remains NO-GO.**

---

## Current execution decision — October 12, 2026

**NO-GO for a first paying customer today.** Public information GO; prepared non-sensitive/manual operations CONDITIONAL. **20 verified requirements, 16 blocked dependencies, 1 held hosted financial-control failure**. All 15 stage decisions and exact evidence/owner actions are in the October 12 execution comment below and the existing [acceptance register](https://github.com/P00NSMASHER/github-value-hunt-ledger/blob/3729a1ad6f6d15e91bc284fb5400af599d6bf49b/freight/commercial/first_customer_acceptance_m2g.json).

**Status checked October 8, 2026. This is the authoritative consolidation of Missions 1A–1H/1Z, not a request to create another lab, scheduler, CRM or website redesign.**

Independent Gmail-to-Zoho message was actually received; this does not prove a website visitor completed the draft-and-send flow. Narrow mobile-gesture patch [#333](../pull/333) is now deployed. |

Sender-side SENT is not the sole proof. The second test message is not yet confirmed. This does **not** verify Cloudflare Email Sending eligibility, provider acceptance, or online-form-to-Zoho delivery. |

## Confirmed implemented work

Only expired non-identifying rate-limit buckets are cleaned in that code path. Regression includes 91-day-old pending/provider-accepted/delivery-verified synthetic records. All five GitHub required workflows passed at `bfacc758fd922509301b850e3f6ea8ab4a5aed27`; resulting merge commit above. Cloudflare canonical production commit and deployment success verified.

## Remaining existing drafts, not production-certified

## Closure sequence: only actual remaining gates

Independently fetched live `site.js` and confirmed corrected mobile mailto handoff. Site branding and sample disclosures preserved.

Connected Gmail SENT record for this exact subject/body confirms recipient `jay@retallyrecovery.com`. Owner must enable/onboard sending domain using Compute > Email Service > Email Sending, obtain **least-privilege Email Sending: Edit** token, and enter it only into protected Cloudflare Pages secrets. An authorized non-sensitive send and actual Zoho receipt must then be independently proved. Never paste credentials in GitHub/chat.
- [x] **Notification-source truth verified, not provider delivery:** Merged [#335](../pull/335), with 16 adversarial recipient/queue/suppression/bounce/HTTP-malformed scenarios and exact-head GitHub success. Wrong-recipient or `success:true` alone remains pending. Cloudflare Email Sending entitlement, active credential and true delivery still **NO-GO**. Provider accepted is not inbox delivered.
- [ ] **Retention and ownership:** Merged #330 prevents automatic inquiry deletion; independent read-only production D1 aggregate on October 8 returned **zero inquiry rows**. Cloudflare Access API returns `9999 access.api.error.not_enabled`: no authenticated operator application or configured two-person approver. Draft #321/#332 migrations remain **unapplied**. - [ ] **Commercial pilot gate:** The existing Google Drive folder `Freight Recovery - Controlled Pilot Environment - VERIFIED 2026-09-21` is **owner-only, unshared**, and contains the manual-review policy only; no customer files. This establishes a potential manual isolated workspace, **not** buyer-specific authorization, MFA/reviewer separation, or contractual permission. Confirm exact registered contracting name from official PA record, trade-name and USPTO/common-law review, signed 30% fee base/reversal/exclusion agreement, reviewer and cost cap, actual buyer-approved scope, secure sharing and retention, and proof-bound posted financial outcomes before accessing confidential records or contacting carriers.

## October 8 independent external gate sweep (current evidence)

| Workstream | Verified status | Next external authority |
|---|---|---|
| Cloudflare email sender | **BLOCKED**: API denies access; Pages sending secret absent | Cloudflare account owner: entitlement/onboard + least-privilege Email Sending: Edit credential |
| Business mailbox | **ONE controlled Gmail→Zoho receipt PASSED** | No redundant email needed; independently prove later Cloudflare→Zoho receipt |

| Legal/trade identity | **UNVERIFIED**: no entity filing certificate located in connected business documents/mail | Confirm PA legal party / fictitious-name filings and trademark clearance with appropriate adviser |

| Sample financial exception | **$1,650 remains UNALLOCATED** after sample $13,450 net less $11,800 eligible | Retain *unverified synthetic* classification until individual claim/credit source is provided; never invent exclusion |

**Public-only operation continues.** Leave both Cloudflare inquiry flags at `0`, existing external operator endpoints off, no financial release, no customer file upload, no credential disclosure and no automatic task changes. This is the single operational ledger; no duplicate tracking system is needed.

## Authority and safety

All feature flags stay at 0 until the whole online-intake path is proven. Keep manual email-draft mode available. items.title: [Task] Prove persisted workflow upgrades from 3.8.4 and 3.9.0 to consolidated 3.10 packages
items.body:
Parent: #8219. Program: #8194. Planning container: #8198.

## Outcome

Demonstrate that a workflow instance durably suspended by released Elsa 3.8.4 or 3.9.0 can be loaded, migrated through the normal EF Core SQLite startup path, and resumed by a separate consolidated 3.10 package-only process. Verify stored identities, typed input values, bookmark handling and terminal state/output. This task provides bounded prepublication compatibility evidence; #8219 and the wider program remain open.

## Readiness and dependencies

- #8626 is closed and #8627 merged into `codex/elsa-integration-program` as `5b6b75fdd64a22d99ac4258311a29258b559055b`. Core main remains `6dbfc58624c28e147a90e2d2b0d1a610817012e2`; do not describe this work as landed on main.
- The accepted candidate input is the nonpublishing proof artifact produced at `44083dc4f47d56aa2d5c215b0c7479c0b7290cb0`, workflow run `37410240989`, artifact `11390805430`, version `3.10.0-proof.37410240989.1`. The lead verified archive SHA256 `8317e5766591f9da2d1f83cd6a85274bd41efbfbd0039d6a1bcfaf0c9bf81636`; independently audited inventory contains 225 package/symbol pairs and 124 exclusions. Consume its exact bytes/verified manifest, without rebuilding or relabeling them as a published 3.10 release. A replacement candidate needs an equivalent exact-head proof and a separately recorded identity.
- Official NuGet metadata confirms `Elsa` and `Elsa.Persistence.EFCore.Sqlite` at both `3.8.4` and `3.9.0`, with net8.0/net9.0/net10.0 dependency groups. Their nuspec repository commits are `33181ae3048f628f591a0155b5665a8e4d1bcea2` and `6436609a1a3874d3fea7ccf690897792f5a1f702`. Stable 3.10.0 is absent from these indexes. Metadata availability does not yet prove a complete fresh restore or runtime success.
- Live #8219 APIs returned no native children or blocking dependencies. No matching persisted-upgrade implementation was found among open Core PRs. #8313 is closed descriptor/serialized-definition proof, not this persisted instance test. Secrets upgrade fixtures concern a separate database/compatibility boundary. Open #7401 concerns default-tenant propagation, not a substitute fixture; if a failure intersects it, investigate the observed cause instead of masking it.
- Activated after #8628/#8630 completed. Native parent #8219 and absence of blocking dependencies were verified; no matching open implementation PR was found. #8629 is the sole active delivery Task.

## Scope and acceptance

- [x] Run all six matrix cells: baseline 3.8.4 and 3.9.0, each on net8.0/net9.0/net10.0, upgrading directly to the recorded consolidated candidate on the same TFM. Use EF Core SQLite with explicitly separate management and runtime database files, unique disposable files per cell, and the default tenant. No chaining 3.8.4 through 3.9.0, silent skipped cells or synthetic SQL-created workflow rows.
- [x] Use standalone PackageReference consumers (`Elsa`, `Elsa.Persistence.EFCore.Sqlite`) generated outside the checkout, with no ProjectReference, repository source assembly fallback, or parent props leakage. Share fixture source/setup rather than duplicate six arrange blocks. Each baseline and candidate restore has a separate initially empty package cache and build directory. Released consumers use NuGet.org. Candidate consumers map every produced internal ID exactly to the verified local artifacts, retain only audited external exceptions, and fail missing, excluded, unknown or wrong-version internal dependencies. Record resolved dependency graphs, source mappings, lock/assets hashes, package hashes/nuspec commits and loaded assembly identities.
- [x] The baseline process uses normal Elsa APIs to publish one deterministic definition, create an explicitly identified instance, run it to an Event bookmark, persist it, and exit cleanly. Populate definition input/output metadata explicitly; `NewAsync(root)` does not transfer builder metadata. Keep `OriginalSource` unset. Use stable built-in activity IDs/types/versions and deterministic primitive typed inputs such as string, integer and boolean. Persist an input-derived sentinel/variable before suspension and require an input-derived terminal output after resumption. Avoid custom fixture activities whose assembly identity might hide relocation issues.
- [x] After the baseline process exits, take a consistent SQLite snapshot including any WAL contents, verify database integrity, and record durable definition/version, instance/correlation IDs, activity identity, serialized inputs/variable values, bookmark ID/activity/hash/payload, and applied migration histories. A fresh read-only SQLite connection must corroborate persistence; an in-memory runner response is insufficient. Preserve a baseline backup before candidate mutation.
- [x] A separate candidate process opens those same files and uses configured normal Elsa migration startup (`RunMigrationsStartupTask` -> `Database.MigrateAsync`) for each actual persistence context. Record applied/pending migrations before and after, table/history identity and integrity. Do not use EnsureCreated, manual schema edits, baseline reseeding, state import, workflow recreation, or a fixture-only warning suppression to manufacture compatibility. Inherited provider configuration may be used only when identified and documented.
- [x] Before resumption, candidate APIs/store reads must find the original definition/version, instance and bookmark with their essential identity/input/activity values intact. Resume the exact saved instance by saved `BookmarkId`, without resupplying the original workflow inputs or recreating its bookmark. Assert Finished status, the expected typed input-derived output, original definition/instance identities, and consumption of the saved bookmark. A further separate candidate verification process must find that terminal state and no remaining saved bookmark, proving durable completion.
- [x] Fail closed and preserve sanitized diagnostics for any restore, migration, load, identity, bookmark or output mismatch. Add focused negative-contract tests rejecting missing/wrong-version candidate packages, mismatched baseline receipt identities, tampered bookmark/input expectations and omitted matrix cells. Do not count a known migration failure as successful upgrade acceptance. If actual migration behavior is incompatible, retain the failing database/receipt, identify the minimal supported migration as follow-on work and leave this task unfulfilled rather than bypassing the migration.
- [x] Retain finite process timeouts, exit codes/logs, package provenance, runtime/SDK versions, SQLite snapshots/integrity and structured per-cell receipts. A repeatable command and a nonpublishing CI/manual lane must run the real matrix against supplied verified artifacts. State clearly which evidence was run and which was skipped/blocked. Relevant tooling tests and exact-head review/CI pass before merge.

## Expected implementation files and reuse

Proposed bounded files: `scripts/integration-program/run_persisted_workflow_upgrade_fixture.py`, `test_persisted_workflow_upgrade_fixture.py`, and `persisted-workflow-upgrade/{Program.cs,README.md}`; add an explicit nonpublishing workflow or integrate an existing suitable proof lane after reviewing artifact retrieval permissions. Generate version/TFM-specific projects in disposable directories. Do not modify runtime APIs/schema or package publisher settings as part of creating the fixture.

Reuse the verified artifact inventory/hash and exact-source-mapping conventions in `prove_consolidated_package_consumers.py`. Reuse the two-process SQLite snapshot/provenance discipline in `run_secrets_sqlite_upgrade_fixture.py`, but not its hard-coded expected failure or Secrets-specific schema. Existing component Event tests and `WorkflowTestFixture` are behavioral/setup references; their source-project test execution does not satisfy this package-only acceptance.

Graph-verified/public seams: `IWorkflowRuntime.CreateClientAsync`, `IWorkflowClient.CreateInstanceAsync`/`RunInstanceAsync`, `RunWorkflowInstanceRequest.BookmarkId`, `IWorkflowDefinitionPublisher.NewAsync`, `RunMigrationsStartupTask`; SQLite configuration lives in `SqliteProvidersExtensions.cs` and `DbContextOptionsBuilderExtensions.cs`. Baseline nuspec commits expose the same client/bookmark/migration seams. Actual six-cell execution remains required to establish API/schema compatibility.

## Boundaries and remaining program gates

No NuGet/npm/feed publication, external messages, deployed host changes, credentials, publisher cutover, package deprecation or source archival. Publishing the synthetic workflow definition into the disposable baseline database is required local fixture setup, not package publication. No Secrets ciphertext/database migration, multitenant matrix, Dapper/Mongo/PostgreSQL/SQL Server validation, Studio rendering or certification of every serialized activity family. Retain the accepted first lockstep 3.10 Feedz/manual-only release decision; independent connector releases and unresolved npm ownership remain separate. These limits do not reduce #8219/#8198 acceptance.

## Evidence pointers (read-only refinement, 2026-10-06)

- Feature: https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-core/issues/8219 ; prior plan comment: https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-core/issues/8219#issuecomment-6008145147
- Package proof: https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-core/pull/8627; [retained artifact](https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-core/actions/runs/37410240989/artifacts/11390805430) includes `receipt.json`, `verified-artifacts.json` and `consumers/consumer-proof.json`.
- Official indexes: https://api.nuget.org/v3-flatcontainer/elsa/index.json ; https://api.nuget.org/v3-flatcontainer/elsa.persistence.efcore.sqlite/index.json . Exact nuspec URLs follow `/<id>/<version>/<id>.nuspec`.
- Governing ADR: `doc/adr/2026-09-28-lockstep-consolidated-release-and-publisher-cutover.md` at merged feature head `5b6b75f`.
- Prior descriptor boundary: https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-core/issues/8313 . Read-only preparation does not claim a persisted-upgrade test has passed.

## Implementation preflight — 2026-10-06

Read-only comparison of baseline source commits and verified candidate source `44083dc4f47d56aa2d5c215b0c7479c0b7290cb0` found the required public APIs; actual package restores and six-cell runtime execution remain unverified.

- Configure both management and runtime EF persistence with distinct SQLite files. Use normal tenant activation/migration startup and clean deactivation/disposal.
- Every input and the sentinel must explicitly use `WorkflowInstanceStorageDriver`; otherwise state extraction omits those inputs. Use serializable built-in Input/Variable expressions, SetVariable, Event and SetOutput, with deterministic activity identities. Delegate/custom fixture activities cannot substitute for serialized compatibility.
- Candidate management has an added `WorkflowDefinitionRegistryGeneration` migration. Record actual applied/pending migrations before and after; source comparison is not successful migration evidence.
- The normal `PersistenceFeatureBase` configuration already ignores `PendingModelChangesWarning` in these baselines and candidate. Document that inherited behavior; add no fixture suppression. Require actual migration completion and durable histories.
- A nonthrowing workflow-instance store read is insufficient because deserialization can fall back to default state. Assert all original identities, typed inputs, sentinel and bookmark before resumption, and reject fallback diagnostics/default state.
- Use SQLite backup from a fresh read-only connection after subprocess exit to include committed WAL pages. Independently corroborate original and terminal persisted rows; do not copy only the main database file.
- Existing package-consumer mapping/hash helpers are reusable, but the old Secrets fixture's synthetic SQL setup, shared cache and accepted migration-failure result are not suitable for this task.

These notes refine implementation details without changing the acceptance matrix or authorizing a second active task.


## Active delivery — 2026-10-06

Assigned to Sol 6.1 High in an isolated worktree on `codex/persisted-workflow-upgrade-proof`, based on shared program commit `3413534be6803d81616ca1da1703ca8582512caf` after #8630. The lead retains integration and QA. The fixture consumes the existing verified proof artifact unchanged; its package source remains `44083dc4f47d56aa2d5c215b0c7479c0b7290cb0`. No six-cell runtime result is claimed yet.


## Accepted closeout — 2026-10-06

PR #8632 merged into `codex/elsa-integration-program` as `e69d92f57de4546a4dd9fd4015d8b8eeba7d1b92` after exact head `a5b1eb711c30331e0708719e1090bae4d280e6f9` passed independent APPROVE + HIGH, Greptile 5/5 and all applicable CI. Core main remains `6dbfc58624c28e147a90e2d2b0d1a610817012e2`; final program integration into main remains separate.

- [Hosted proof run 37421090192](https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-core/actions/runs/37421090192): all six direct 3.8.4/3.9.0 × net8/net9/net10 upgrade cells passed, with 18 runtime phases and 42 commands exiting zero without timeouts. Actual SDK 10.0.401.
- [Retained evidence artifact 11392299920](https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-core/actions/runs/37421090192/artifacts/11392299920), SHA256 `cd32bde6a61e654b0a61697993034fa6a2d041b57cecfccc28b1e796694aa9a1`, expires 2026-10-13 05:59:02 UTC. Lead independently verified archive identity, all 44 retained files, 36 database/WAL/snapshot hashes, original/terminal SQLite state, typed values, migrations and bookmark consumption. Transfer artifact 11392644052 contains only the unchanged original proof archive and metadata. [Full evidence](https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-core/pull/8632#issuecomment-6010367114).
- Package-only provenance, parent-import isolation, migration and failure contracts passed. The final fixture/shared-helper suite has 34 tests passing normally and under Python optimization. CI additionally passed 478 integration-program tests normally and under optimization, plus its separate 15-test validation suite in both modes.
- Normal Packages run 37421090138 passed: 4,834 unit/integration tests, 144 skipped, zero failures across 64 net10.0 projects; 226 component tests, one skipped, zero failures; package build and coverage succeeded. Publication/deployment jobs were intentionally skipped. Package-impact proof and source-impact selection passed; conditional unselected lanes were skipped.
- Artifact-reading credentials are isolated in a no-checkout fixed retrieval job. Fixture execution has no Actions-read permission or GH_TOKEN; repository-write push/manual authority is documented. The Greptile finding is fixed and resolved, and Cursor found no issues on the final head.

This accepts only the stated SQLite/default-tenant/built-in-activity proof against the pinned unpublished candidate bytes. #8219 remains open for its broader package/host compatibility and production-candidate acceptance; #8631 prepares different stable candidate bytes that require their own applicable compatibility verification before publication. No publication, deployment, publisher cutover or full-program completion occurred.

items.title: Move tenant-inheritable credentials out of spring.env; add tenant-default settings surface

milestone.title: v0.1
milestone.description: First public Spring Voyage release. Foundation for the hosted service. See docs/plan/v0.1/README.md.

items.body:
## Context

The current \`spring.env\` template ships placeholders for LLM provider credentials:

\`\`\`
# ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=
# OPENAI_API_KEY=
\`\`\`

These are **not used by the platform itself** — they're consumed by agents for their own inference calls. Treating them as platform-wide env vars is wrong for both single-user OSS (today, an operator can only run one "tenant" worth of models) and for hosted multi-tenant deployments (where per-tenant credentials are load-bearing). V1 behaviour had these as per-unit settings with tenant-level defaults that units could inherit or override — this issue restores that shape.

## The three config tiers

- **Tier 1 — platform-deploy config** (env / appsettings.json): platform identity, DB connection, Dapr wiring, GitHub App credentials (`GITHUB_APP_ID` / `GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` / `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` — these identify *the Spring Voyage instance itself* as a GitHub App). Stays in env / startup config.
- **Tier 2 — tenant-default config** (database, per-tenant): tenant-wide defaults that units inherit unless overridden. **This is where LLM API keys belong.**
- **Tier 3 — unit config** (database, per-unit): per-unit overrides. Already supported by `spring secret --scope unit` (PR #612) and the Secrets tab on unit detail.

## Scope

1. **Remove tier-2 credentials from `spring.env`.** Delete the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` placeholders. If bootstrap from env is retained for convenience, it must migrate to the tenant store on first startup (one-time seed) and then stop reading env. Document clearly that env vars for these are a legacy bootstrap path.
2. **Tenant-default settings surface.**
   - CLI: `spring tenant settings set/get/clear <key>` (or use `spring secret --scope tenant` from #612 if a tenant-key / tenant-secret distinction isn't needed).
   - Portal: a **Tenant defaults** panel (likely in the Settings drawer's existing extension-slot seam from PR #567, or as a new top-level route) for setting/viewing the defaults — at minimum `anthropic-api-key`, `openai-api-key`, and any other tier-2 values we surface later.
3. **Resolution chain.** When an agent needs an LLM credential, resolve in order: unit secret → tenant default → env bootstrap (if any). Fail-clean if none found ("no LLM credentials configured for this unit; set via \`spring secret --scope unit\` or configure tenant defaults").
4. **Unit-level override UX.** The existing Secrets tab on unit detail continues to let an operator override per-unit. Add visual cue ("inherited from tenant default" vs. "set on unit") so operators know what's active.
5. **Affects #597 (PR #613).** The just-landed model-catalog implementation reads `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` from env directly. After this issue lands, the model catalog must switch to the tier-2 resolver (use tenant-default credentials for model listing). Add a note in the code where this switch is required.

## Out of scope

- Tier-1 platform config validation (GitHub App credentials etc.) — separate issue.
- Hosted multi-tenant specifics (per-tenant billing, SSO, etc.) — downstream private repo.

## Documentation updates (required)

Any PR for this issue MUST update the following because credentials / config changes affect how operators start and run the platform:

- **Root `README.md`** — first-run / startup flow no longer tells operators to set LLM keys in `spring.env`; instead points them at the tenant-default surface (CLI + portal) post-startup.
- **`deployment/README.md`** — standalone deployment walkthrough; delete any "edit spring.env" step for LLM keys; add the post-deploy tenant-config step.
- **`docs/guide/secrets.md`** — rewritten to cover the three-tier model (platform / tenant / unit), resolution order, how to set tenant defaults, how units inherit / override.
- **`docs/guide/portal.md`** — document the new Tenant defaults panel if added; update the Unit secrets walkthrough with the inheritance indicator.
- **`docs/architecture/*.md`** — document the config-tier model explicitly (new doc or a new section in an existing one — `docs/architecture/security.md` or `docs/architecture/secrets.md` are natural homes).
- **Private/hosted deployment docs** (downstream tracker, cvoya-com/spring) — needs a companion update since tier-2 defaults are exactly what multi-tenant hosted deployments rely on.

Do not ship the PR with stale docs — the first-run experience is the first thing operators will see.

## Related

- PR #612 (spring secret CLI with `--scope tenant`) — the secret-CLI primitive is already in place.
- PR #613 / #597 (dynamic model retrieval) — reads env creds today; will switch to tier-2 resolver after this lands.
- #609 (GitHub connector missing / malformed credentials) — narrow, but related.
- Third V2 issue (startup config validation + system health) — complementary; tier-1 only.

items.title: Connections are a cluster-global resource with no sharing policy between workers — and workers are not enumerable, so one cannot be built today
items.body:
**Database connections are a cluster-global resource and cleat has no policy for sharing them
between workers — nor, today, any way to build one, because workers are not enumerable.** This asks
for exploration and a decision; it does not propose a design.

Sibling of #1486, which is the same question inside one worker. That one is a prerequisite: a
cluster budget cannot be apportioned to a participant that does not know its own total.

## The arithmetic that motivates it

A default single-node worker opens **75** connections (#1486 has the per-pool breakdown).
PostgreSQL's default `max_connections` is **100** — confirmed against a stock 16 container.

**Two default workers want 150.** The second fails, and nothing in either can detect it, warn about
it, or take less. Connections are opened during setup, so this happens before either worker claims
any work.

MySQL's default is 151 and SQL Server's is effectively unlimited, so **PostgreSQL is the only
binding default of the three** — which is also the deployment cleat's own principles centre on.

## Why a policy cannot be built today: workers are not enumerable

- `generateWorkerID` (`setup.go:555`) is 16 random bytes at startup, **persisted nowhere**.
- There is no worker registry table — `git grep -iE 'CREATE TABLE.*worker' migrations/` finds
  nothing.
- Heartbeats are **per-workflow**, not per-worker: `BatchHeartbeat` is
  `UPDATE ... WHERE assigned_to = $1 AND status = 'running'` (`db.go:357`).

So a worker exists in the database **only as a value on rows it currently holds**. A worker holding
no claims is invisible.

**That inverts exactly wrong.** A freshly-started or idle worker has already opened its fixed pools
and appears nowhere. The workers hardest to see are the ones consuming connections without doing
work.

## The constraint that shapes the answer

`PRINCIPLES.md` §1: *"no external coordination services, no message queues, no separate databases
for different concerns."* The only coordination substrate is the database itself.

So a cluster-global connection policy would have to be negotiated **through the resource being
rationed** — you need a connection to bid for connections. That is workable (a lease table, the
same shape as `assigned_to`) but the bootstrap case wants care: **a worker that cannot get its
first connection cannot participate in the protocol that would have told it to ask for fewer**, and
that is precisely the overloaded-cluster case the policy exists for.

## The fork, stated so it can be decided rather than drifted into

**(a) Build cluster-global admission.** Worker registry plus a leased budget in Postgres. Fits §1.
It is also real machinery, and it is the coordination layer cleat has deliberately not built.

**(b) Declare an external pooler the answer.** `docs/operations/tuning.md` already gestures at
PgBouncer. `PRINCIPLES.md` §4 supports it — *"belong in the ecosystem, not in the core"* — and the
supply-side measurements on #1470 argue for it: PostgreSQL's 100 is the only binding default and
raising it to 1000 costs roughly 1.2 GB.

**(c) Neither, but stop implying otherwise.** Remove the stub and the documented `pool_eviction_ttl`,
and say plainly in the sizing guidance that per-worker budgets are static and must be planned
against `max_connections` by hand.

## What would have to be measured before (a)

The #1470 measurements are explicit that they cover **idle** connections: ~1.19 MiB each on
PostgreSQL, linear from 400 to 800. They deliberately do **not** cover active-connection
throughput, and that is the number that would justify a specific ceiling rather than a specific
memory budget. PostgreSQL degrades past a few hundred *concurrently active* backends through lock
and snapshot contention, which is the real argument for a pooler — not memory.

So "800 idle connections cost 1 GB" must not be read as "800 active connections are fine", and
(a) should not be costed from it.

## Smallest useful step, if a decision is not ready

A worker could log its own computed budget at startup — the sum #1486 says nothing computes — and
the sizing docs could carry the per-pool table. Neither requires a policy, and both make the
problem visible to an operator who currently has no way to see it coming.
