items.title: Multi-Tenant Isolation & Authentication
items.body:
## 🎯 Execution Order: **Issue #4** (After #1, #20, #21)

**Dependencies**: #1 (Core Platform), #20 (State Tracking), #21 (Service Discovery)  
**Blocks**: #18 (Connectors need auth), #19 (Auto-scaling needs tenant provisioning)  
**Timeline**: Week 2-4 (Feb 3 - Feb 23, 2026)

---

## Overview
Implement multi-tenant isolation using **dedicated tenant NATS instances** with network policies, and basic API authentication for the platform.

**Timeline**: Week 2-4 (Feb 3 - Feb 23, 2026)  
**Team**: 1-2 engineers  
**Status**: ACTIVE - Build phase

📖 **Architecture Documentation**: [docs/NATS_ARCHITECTURE.md](../blob/main/docs/NATS_ARCHITECTURE.md)

## Consolidates
- ✅ #4: Multi-Tenancy Architecture & Data Isolation
- ✅ #7: Security & Authentication Architecture

## NATS Security Model

Our **hybrid NATS architecture** provides strong isolation:

### Tenant NATS Isolation
- ✅ Each tenant has **dedicated NATS instance(s)** (not shared NATS accounts)
- ✅ **Kubernetes NetworkPolicy** prevents cross-tenant network access
- ✅ **Unique credentials** per tenant (auto-generated)
- ✅ **JWT-based authentication** for workers
- ✅ Physical isolation = No noisy neighbor issues

### Platform NATS Security
- ✅ **Only Control Plane** can access Platform NATS
- ✅ Service account authentication (not exposed to tenants)
- ✅ **TLS encryption** for all NATS communication (in-cluster)
- ✅ No direct tenant access to Platform NATS

### Credential Management
- ✅ NATS credentials stored in **Kubernetes Secrets**
- ✅ **Automatic rotation** (monthly)
- ✅ Revocation on tenant deletion
- ✅ Audit log for NATS authentication events

## Deliverables

### Week 2 (Feb 3 - Feb 9)
- [ ] Multi-tenancy design document
- [ ] **Tenant NATS instance provisioning** design
- [ ] **Kubernetes NetworkPolicy** design (tenant isolation)
- [ ] Tenant data model (PostgreSQL schema)
- [ ] Authentication strategy (API keys + JWT tokens)

### Week 3-4 (Feb 10 - Feb 23)
- [ ] Tenant CRUD API:
  - Create tenant → **Auto-provision first NATS instance**
  - Get tenant details
  - Update tenant settings
  - Delete tenant → **Cleanup NATS instances**
- [ ] **NATS instance provisioning**:
  - Create Kubernetes Deployment + Service
  - Generate unique NATS credentials
  - Store credentials in Kubernetes Secret
  - Register in PostgreSQL \`nats_instances\` table
- [ ] **Kubernetes NetworkPolicy** enforcement:
  - Tenant A pods cannot reach Tenant B NATS
  - Workers only connect to their tenant's NATS
- [ ] API key generation and management
- [ ] **JWT token generation** for worker authentication to NATS
- [ ] API key authentication middleware
- [ ] Basic quota management:
  - Message throughput limits
  - Integration count limits (50 per NATS instance)
  - Storage limits
- [ ] **NATS credential rotation** mechanism
- [ ] Tenant isolation validation tests

## Technical Implementation

**Tenant NATS Isolation**:
- Each tenant gets dedicated NATS instance(s)
- Naming: \`nats-{tenant-id}-{instance-number}\`
- Subject namespacing: \`{tenant-id}.{integration-id}.{event-type}\`
- Network-level isolation via Kubernetes NetworkPolicy

**Authentication**:
- **API authentication**: API key-based (Bearer token)
- **NATS authentication**: JWT tokens (generated per worker)
- API keys scoped to tenant
- Key rotation support (API keys: manual, NATS creds: automatic monthly)
- Rate limiting per tenant

**Database Isolation**:
- Row-level tenant_id in all tables
- PostgreSQL RLS policies (optional)
- Indexed tenant_id for performance
- Table: \`nats_instances\` (tracks tenant NATS instances - created in #21)

**Network Isolation**:
\`\`\`yaml
# Example NetworkPolicy
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-nats-isolation
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nats
      tenant: tenant-a
  ingress:
  - from:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          tenant: tenant-a  # Only tenant-a pods can connect
\`\`\`

## Acceptance Criteria

**Multi-Tenancy**:
- [ ] Tenants can be created via API
- [ ] Each tenant automatically gets dedicated NATS instance
- [ ] Tenant NATS instances are network-isolated (A cannot reach B)
- [ ] Tenant data is completely isolated in PostgreSQL
- [ ] Integration tests validate isolation (tenant A cannot access tenant B's data/NATS)

**Authentication & Authorization**:
- [ ] API keys authenticate API requests
- [ ] JWT tokens authenticate workers to NATS
- [ ] Workers can only connect to their tenant's NATS instances
- [ ] NATS credentials stored securely in Kubernetes Secrets

**Security**:
- [ ] All NATS communication encrypted (TLS)
- [ ] Platform NATS only accessible by Control Plane
- [ ] NATS credentials rotated monthly (automatic)
- [ ] Audit log tracks NATS authentication events

**Quotas**:
- [ ] Integration count limit enforced (50 per NATS instance)
- [ ] Message throughput limits enforced
- [ ] Quota exceeded returns 429 (rate limit) response

**Performance**:
- [ ] Tenant isolation adds <5ms overhead
- [ ] NATS instance provisioning completes in <60 seconds

## Security Scope for POC

**IN SCOPE**:
- API key authentication
- **Dedicated tenant NATS instances** (physical isolation)
- **Kubernetes NetworkPolicy** isolation
- **JWT authentication** for NATS
- **TLS encryption** (NATS)
- **Credential rotation** (NATS)
- Basic quotas

**OUT OF SCOPE (post-POC)**:
- SSO / OAuth / SAML
- Advanced RBAC (roles, permissions)
- Detailed audit logging
- Customer-managed encryption keys
- Compliance certifications (GDPR, HIPAA, SOC2)

## Dependencies & Blockers

**Depends On**:  
- #1 - Core Platform (NATS infrastructure working)
- #20 - State Tracking (for quota enforcement)
- #21 - Service Discovery (workers need to discover NATS instances)

**Blocks**:  
- #18 - Connector SDK (needs authentication)
- #19 - Auto-scaling (needs tenant provisioning logic)

**Parallel**: None - this depends on #1, #20, #21 being substantially complete

## Related Issues
- #21 - Service Discovery for Tenant NATS Instances
- #19 - NATS Instance Auto-Scaling & Lifecycle Management

## Notes
**Key Architecture Change**: We're using **dedicated NATS instances per tenant** instead of shared NATS with accounts. This provides:
- ✅ Stronger isolation (physical separation)
- ✅ No noisy neighbor issues
- ✅ Simpler security model (network policies > NATS ACLs)
- ✅ Easier capacity management (scale per tenant)

Related issues merged: #7

items.title: SRD-R1B: GHL Two-Way Commercial Operations + Stitchi CRM Tools
items.body:
# GHL Two-Way Commercial Operations + Stitchi CRM Tools

Parent issues: #126, #124
Related: #128, #131, #140, #145, #214

## Purpose

Deliver the customer requirement that commercial and sales users operate their normal GoHighLevel workflows from Tanaghum instead of repeatedly switching to GHL. GoHighLevel remains the external CRM source of truth; Tanaghum becomes the governed operating surface, approval layer, AI assistant, audit ledger and reporting layer.

The current controlled acceptance proves GHL -> Tanaghum read sync. This sprint adds the missing Tanaghum -> GHL command path and provider reconciliation.

## Current Implementation Truth

- Customer-owned GHL credentials and location are stored in the tenant vault.
- Read-only validation, mapping, preview, sync, idempotent lead mirrors, Event Operations, Historical Assessment and read-only Stitchi summaries are proven for controlled purchase/partial-payment and meeting/no-show scenarios.
- Existing write-back is a narrow, disabled `/contacts/upsert` call for already-linked leads. It does not provide complete CRM operation.
- Tanaghum does not currently create/update opportunities, move stages, create/update appointments, manage payment/ticket fields, send GHL WhatsApp messages, or expose those actions through Stitchi.
- The current private integration token is read-only. Production execution remains blocked until the customer grants and approves exact write scopes.

## Product Outcome

A permitted user can remain in Tanaghum to:

1. Create or update a GHL contact.
2. Add or remove approved GHL tags.
3. Create or update an opportunity.
4. Move an opportunity between approved pipeline stages and statuses.
5. Set total sale value and approved opportunity custom fields for amount paid, payment status, payment date and ticket quantity.
6. Book, reschedule or cancel an appointment.
7. Record Showed/Completed/No Show outcomes.
8. Draft, approve and send an authorized WhatsApp message through the customer GHL provider.
9. See the provider-confirmed result, reconciliation status and audit evidence without raw credentials or unnecessary PII.
10. Ask Stitchi to prepare the same work in natural language; Stitchi must ask for missing critical fields, show a structured preview, require approval and then execute only through governed Tanaghum services.

## Architecture

```text
Hybrid UI / Stitchi
  -> structured command draft
  -> tenant + RBAC + business validation
  -> immutable preview
  -> human approval
  -> idempotent GHL command job
  -> HighLevel API
  -> sanitized provider result
  -> webhook/read-back reconciliation
  -> Tanaghum mirror refresh
  -> audit and user-visible outcome
```

GHL remains CRM source of truth. Tanaghum never silently overwrites provider state and never reports a write as successful until provider confirmation is recorded.

## Backend Scope

### Governed Command API

Add a dedicated `ghl-operations` module with preview/approve/execute/read endpoints for:

- contact upsert
- contact tag add/remove
- opportunity create/update
- opportunity stage/status/value/custom-field update
- appointment create/update/cancel/status
- WhatsApp message send

Every command must include:

- tenant key
- actor user and role
- command type
- target GHL location
- linked Tanaghum lead/event/commercial plan when applicable
- sanitized structured payload
- provider endpoint family
- idempotency key
- preview hash/version
- approval state and approver
- execution state
- provider object IDs
- attempts and timestamps
- sanitized error/result summary
- reconciliation state

### Required State Machine

`draft -> previewed -> pending_approval -> approved -> executing -> provider_accepted -> reconciled`

Terminal/exception states:

- rejected
- cancelled
- blocked
- failed
- reconciliation_failed
- expired

No state may skip required approval. Repeated execute calls with the same idempotency key must not create duplicate contacts, opportunities, appointments or messages.

### HighLevel Adapter

Implement typed client methods for:

- `POST /contacts/upsert`
- contact tag add/remove endpoints
- opportunity create/upsert/update/status endpoints supported by current HighLevel API version
- `POST /calendars/events/appointments`
- `PUT /calendars/events/appointments/:eventId`
- `POST /conversations/messages` for authorized WhatsApp sends
- read-back endpoints required to verify provider state

Use tenant-owned sub-account/private integration credentials only. No global credential fallback.

### Reconciliation

- Add signed/verified GHL webhook ingress where supported.
- Store provider event IDs and deduplicate webhook deliveries.
- Reconcile contact, opportunity, appointment and message outcomes.
- When webhook coverage is unavailable, perform bounded read-back verification.
- Never trust client-supplied provider success.
- Surface stale, pending, failed and drifted states honestly.

## Permissions And Approval

- Read: commercial/sales roles permitted by existing tenant policy.
- Prepare/preview: marketing manager, sales manager, lead qualification manager, department head, CCO, admin according to action type.
- Approve external CRM mutation: CCO, department head or admin by default; customer policy may narrow this.
- Execute: system service only after a valid approved command.
- WhatsApp send requires message approval, consent/DND checks and customer provider readiness.
- No role receives broad provider access merely because it can read GHL data.

## Stitchi Scope

Add governed executable Stitchi actions for:

- prepare GHL contact
- prepare/apply tags
- prepare opportunity
- prepare stage/status/value/payment update
- prepare appointment
- prepare appointment outcome
- prepare WhatsApp follow-up

Stitchi must:

- know tenant/user/role context
- resolve event, commercial plan, lead and GHL mapping context
- ask one concise follow-up when critical data is missing
- never invent provider IDs, pipeline stages, payment amounts, ticket quantities or consent
- show a structured action card with effects and warnings
- require approval
- execute through the same backend command service as the UI
- report provider-confirmed outcome and refresh relevant views
- never expose raw PII in AI prompts beyond the minimum approved context

## Hybrid UI Scope

Provide task-first controls in Sales & Leads / Event Operations:

- Create/update CRM contact
- Create opportunity
- Change stage/status
- Book/update meeting
- Record outcome
- Update payment/ticket evidence
- Draft/approve/send WhatsApp
- Command history and reconciliation status

Use business wording. Hide API endpoints, flags and raw provider data from customer-facing views. Keep advanced connector diagnostics under Settings/Integrations.

## Security And Reliability

- Secrets never returned, logged or placed in command payload records.
- Strict tenant isolation on commands, approvals, provider IDs, webhook events and mirrors.
- Validate all GHL IDs against the tenant location and approved mapping.
- Prevent arbitrary endpoint or field injection.
- Respect GHL DND/consent and WhatsApp template/provider rules.
- Apply retry with bounded exponential backoff only to retry-safe operations.
- Add correlation/request IDs and idempotency keys.
- Encrypt any sensitive command metadata at rest where required.
- Redact provider errors before returning them to clients.

## Tests

### Unit/Contract

- request schemas and allowed field lists
- RBAC and approval boundaries
- state machine
- idempotency and duplicate prevention
- preview hash/version mismatch
- tenant isolation
- provider error sanitization
- contact/opportunity/appointment/message client contracts
- payment/ticket custom-field mapping
- consent/DND/no-send rules
- webhook signature/deduplication
- read-back reconciliation

### Integration

- create contact -> provider accepted -> mirror reconciled
- create opportunity -> stage/value/custom fields -> reconciled
- appointment create -> showed/no-show update -> dashboard refresh
- WhatsApp draft -> approval -> send -> message status reconciliation
- provider timeout/retry/failure paths
- command rejected/expired/cancelled paths
- no raw secrets or unnecessary PII in API, logs, audit or Stitchi prompts

### Browser/E2E

- sales manager prepares a contact/opportunity but cannot self-approve when policy forbids it
- CCO approves and the command executes once
- UI shows provider-confirmed result and refreshed lead/event state
- Stitchi performs the same governed flow
- no hidden 401/403/500 or console errors
- responsive layout at desktop and mobile widths

## Definition Of Done

- All listed CRM command types have preview, approval, execution, audit, idempotency and reconciliation.
- Hybrid users can complete the controlled attended, fully-paid and lost scenarios without opening GHL after initial provider administration.
- Stitchi can prepare and execute those same scenarios after approval.
- GHL remains source of truth and Tanaghum reflects provider-confirmed state.
- WhatsApp send remains blocked unless the customer GHL WhatsApp provider, required write scope, consent policy and execution authorization are present.
- Full backend/frontend test suites, focused GHL contract tests and Playwright customer workflow pass.
- CI is green and deployment evidence is attached.
- Controlled live acceptance is performed with customer-approved write scopes before production write capability is claimed complete.

## Customer Dependencies

The customer must provide/approve:

- a GHL sub-account Private Integration Token with the exact required write scopes
- location, calendar, pipeline, stage, tag and custom-field mappings
- roles allowed to approve each mutation type
- WhatsApp channel/provider readiness, templates and consent rules
- whether Tanaghum may trigger GHL workflows or send messages directly

These dependencies do not block implementing and testing the production adapter with contract fixtures; they block only live write acceptance.

## Non-Goals

- Replacing GHL as CRM source of truth
- Exposing full GHL administration in Tanaghum
- Creating customer pipelines/calendars/phone providers without explicit scope
- Autonomous external writes without approval
- Storing provider credentials outside the tenant vault

items.title: chore(infra): production environment — app.portalsai.io + api.portalsai.io + www.portalsai.io + AWS infra + Auth0/Stripe/Azure/Google vendor provisioning

type.name: Epic
type.description: A parent ticket grouping feature/bugfix children coordinated on an epic branch

items.body:
> **This is an epic.** Epic branch: **`epic/prod-environment`**. Children branch from it and PR back into it — never into `main`, which auto-deploys to app-dev and must not receive a half-finished production standup. The whole epic reaches `main` as one release-cut merge. The sections below are the full contract; the children carve it up.
>
> **Pre-work: #382** lands on `main` **before** any child branch — three config bugs (`PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` unset, the `api-${Environment}` OAuth callbacks, and the missing Mapbox catalog entry) that are live in dev today and would otherwise be debugged for the first time against production.

## Status

| Ticket | Role | State |
|---|---|---|
| #382 — deployed-env config gaps | **Pre-work, merged to `main`** — fixed the three dev-affecting bugs the prod templates inherit | **Closed** |
| #383 — AWS infrastructure + `deploy-prod.yml` | The compute/storage/network layer and the release-triggered pipeline that owns it | **Merged into epic** |
| #384 — vendor tenants + secret/SSM provisioning | Auth0 prod tenant, Google + Entra OAuth clients, Anthropic/Tavily/Mapbox keys, the whole `portalai/prod/*` catalog | **Merged into epic** |
| #385 — Stripe live mode | Verification, restricted keys, products, webhook, tax, billing portal | **Merged into epic** |
| #386 — `www.portalsai.io` activation | Provisions and ungates the existing prod site pipeline | **Merged into epic** |
| #325 — production pricing + allocations | The numbers: live amounts in Stripe, production tier allocations in the catalog | **Merged into epic** |
| #387 — CLI activation + doc sweep | Registry entry, live guard verification, every "pending #83" doc rewritten | **Merged into epic** |

_States: `Todo` → `In progress` → `Merged into epic` → `Closed` (close-out only). This table is the record of truth — it moves with every child state change._

**Merged into the epic branch so far** (child issues stay open — auto-close only fires on the default branch): #384 ([PR #389](https://github.com/EnterpriseBT/portal-ai/pull/389)), #383 ([PR #390](https://github.com/EnterpriseBT/portal-ai/pull/390)) and #385 ([PR #392](https://github.com/EnterpriseBT/portal-ai/pull/392)) #386 ([PR #393](https://github.com/EnterpriseBT/portal-ai/pull/393)), #325 ([PR #394](https://github.com/EnterpriseBT/portal-ai/pull/394)) and #387 ([PR #395](https://github.com/EnterpriseBT/portal-ai/pull/395)).

### ✅ All children merged — and production does not exist yet

Every child is on `epic/prod-environment` and CI is green. **Merging them provisioned nothing.** The remaining work is operator work, in this order:

1. **`docs/PROD_PROVISIONING.runbook.md`** — vendor accounts, the 24 config values, and the `CREATE DATABASE portal_ai` bootstrap that nothing in the repo performs.
2. **`docs/PROD_DEPLOY.runbook.md`** — create the `prod` GitHub Environment **with required reviewers** (it does not exist; referencing a missing environment auto-creates it unprotected, so today's gate is nominal) and the prod-scoped OIDC role. Then cut a release.
3. **`docs/PROD_STRIPE_LIVE.runbook.md`** — the restricted keys, the webhook's **six** events (the `price.*` trio is what republishes the marketing site), and §6e's verification that tax is actually *collected*, not merely enabled.
4. Set `PROD_SITE_CONFIG_URL` **last**, then publish a release to bring up `www.portalsai.io`.

Three steps prove themselves only once and cannot be casually retried: the first-deploy `DesiredCount=0` bootstrap, the `CREATE DATABASE` step wedged between two halves of that first release, and the first live invoice carrying a non-zero tax line.

Then the epic smoke, then one final `epic/prod-environment` → `main` PR carrying `Closes #83` and every child, **rebase-merged** per the epic convention. #382's pre-work is on `main` and its issue is closed.

### Smoke: one epic-level walk, not per-child (decided 2026-08-16)

Children are **not** smoked individually. That is not a shortcut — it is what the work allows: #383, #384 and #385's acceptance criteria all require a production environment that does not exist until all three have merged **and** their runbooks have been executed. There is nothing to walk before then.

So the merge gate for the children is CI + review; the human gate moves to close-out, where a single `/smoke` covers the epic. Two consequences worth holding on to:

- **The epic smoke is gated on operator work, not just on merges.** `docs/PROD_PROVISIONING.runbook.md` (#384), `docs/PROD_STRIPE_LIVE.runbook.md` (#385) and `docs/PROD_DEPLOY.runbook.md` (#383) have to be *executed* first. Merging every child leaves prod still nonexistent.
- **The checklist has to be assembled from all children's acceptance criteria**, not scaffolded from one spec — including the criteria that only prove themselves once: the first-deploy `DesiredCount=0` bootstrap, the `CREATE DATABASE portal_ai` step, and the live invoice carrying a non-zero tax line.

**Filed along the way, out of scope and independent of this epic:** [#391](https://github.com/EnterpriseBT/portal-ai/issues/391) — jobs stranded in a non-terminal status after a Redis loss hold their entity locks until cancelled by hand. Affects app-dev today.

## Children & dependencies

```
#382 (main) ──▶ #384 ──▶ #383 ──▶ #386 ──▶ #385 ──▶ #325 ──▶ #387
                  vendors   infra    www     stripe   prices    cli+docs
```

- **#382 first, onto `main`.** #384 must not run `portalops vars apply --env prod` before it lands, or the Mapbox key is silently omitted from the catalog and #383's task definition fails to resolve a secret ARN.
- **#384 before #383.** `backend.yml` takes eleven secret ARNs as parameters; the stack cannot deploy against values that don't exist.
- **#383 before #386.** `PROD_SITE_CONFIG_URL` may only be set once the prod API returns 200 on `/api/public/site-config`.
- **#386 before #385's submission.** Stripe's live-mode business review expects a public site describing the product and pricing. **Start the Stripe account application on day one regardless** — it is the epic's longest external lead time, and only the submission waits on the site.
- **#385 before #325.** `tier apply` fails closed on an unresolvable lookup key, so the live prices must exist before the allocations converge onto them.
- **#387 last.** It documents what the others shipped, so it can only be truthful at the end.
- **Also on the critical path but not a child:** Google's OAuth consent-screen verification for an external-user app (inside #384) carries vendor lead time of its own — check its current state early rather than discovering it at go-live.

## Goal

Stand up a production environment mirroring dev (`app-dev.portalsai.io` / `api-dev.portalsai.io`) at the unprefixed names `app.portalsai.io` and `api.portalsai.io`. The dev stack is fully infrastructure-as-code (CloudFormation templates parameterized on `Environment=…`, GitHub Actions `deploy-dev.yml` orchestrating the stacks), so the bulk of the work is: provision the per-env config catalog (Secrets Manager + SSM), stand up the prod vendor tenants and accounts (Auth0, **Stripe live**, Google + **Microsoft/Azure Entra** OAuth, Anthropic, Tavily, **Mapbox**, and the GitHub dispatch token), file the prod deploy workflow, **provision and trigger the production marketing site at `www.portalsai.io`** (the reusable pipeline already exists — `deploy-site-prod.yml`, built by #311/#319 — but is gated off until the prod API config URL is set), and fix the few places that bake the dev subdomain convention into the templates.

Prod is also the last unactivated leg of the CLI-first operations contract: `packages/cli-env` treats `prod` as first-class (`kind: "production"` guards are written and unit-tested) but the registry has no prod entry, and every vendor runbook carries a "pending #83" section. Landing this ticket activates those.

> **Audited 2026-08-02** against `main` — corrections and additions since the 2026-05-30 filing are marked **[audit]**. See the audit log at the bottom.
>
> **Re-audited 2026-08-14** against `main` @ `411ce46a` — vendor / webhook / infra coverage sweep. New findings are marked **[2026-08-14]**. Three structural decisions were taken with the ticket owner and are recorded in the amendment log: **prod shares dev's AWS account**; **the three dev-affecting config bugs land in their own PR first**; **this ticket becomes an epic** with children.

## In scope

### AWS infrastructure (per dev parity)

Deploy the existing CloudFormation stacks with `Environment=prod`, all under stack-name prefix `portalai-prod-…`. Every template already declares `AllowedValues: [dev, prod]`, so no template gains a new env value.

- [ ] `portalai-prod-network` (`infra/cloudformation/network.yml`) — VPC, subnets, NAT, IGW
- [ ] `portalai-prod-dns-certs` (`dns-certs.yml`) — wildcard ACM cert. **[audit]** The template requests `portalsai.io` + `*.portalsai.io` with `DomainValidationOptions.HostedZoneId`. A second cert for the same names in the same account/zone shares one validation CNAME — confirm the prod stack's record write is an upsert and doesn't collide with the dev stack's. Alternative: skip the prod stack and thread the existing cert ARN through as a parameter (backend/frontend consume it via the `${Environment}-CertificateArn` export today, so that path needs a parameter override rather than an import)
- [ ] `portalai-prod-database` (`database.yml`) — RDS PostgreSQL. **[audit]** `InstanceClass`, `AllocatedStorage`, and `MultiAZ` are already parameters (defaults `db.t4g.micro` / 20 / `false`); the prod deploy passes larger values + `MultiAZ=true`. `BackupRetentionPeriod: 7` and `DeletionProtection` are **hardcoded/absent** — the template needs a parameter (or a prod condition) for both before prod can raise retention to ≥ 14 days and turn deletion protection on
- [ ] `portalai-prod-bastion` (`bastion.yml`) — SSM-managed bastion. Keep it: `portalops db tunnel/psql/reset` route through it and are the only operator path to the prod DB
- [ ] `portalai-prod-cache` (`cache.yml`) — ElastiCache. `NodeType` / `NumCacheNodes` are parameters (defaults `cache.t4g.micro` / 1); decide prod sizing + whether we want a replica
- [ ] `portalai-prod-frontend` (`frontend.yml`) — S3 + CloudFront, fronted by `app.portalsai.io`
- [ ] `portalai-prod-backend` (`backend.yml`) — ECS/ECR + ALB, fronted by `api.portalsai.io`

### Subdomain decoupling (template fix)

**[audit] The parameter is `Subdomain`, not `SubdomainPrefix`** — `frontend.yml:9-12` (default `app-dev`) and `backend.yml:9-11` (default `api-dev`). Both already drive the Route 53 record, the CloudFront alias, and the frontend bucket name. `deploy-dev.yml` never passes it (it rides the defaults); **the prod workflow must pass `Subdomain=app` / `Subdomain=api` explicitly**.

- [ ] **Gotcha (still live):** **[2026-08-14] now `backend.yml:502-505`** (the block moved when the GIS geocoding secret landed) hard-templates the OAuth callback URLs as `https://api-${Environment}.portalsai.io/...`, which resolves to `api-prod.portalsai.io` — wrong. Fix by reusing the existing parameters:

```yaml
Value: !Sub "https://${Subdomain}.${DomainName}/api/connectors/google-sheets/callback"
Value: !Sub "https://${Subdomain}.${DomainName}/api/connectors/microsoft-excel/callback"
```

This is a **dev-affecting change** (dev's value is unchanged in content, but the stack updates) — it lands and deploys to dev before prod first runs.

- [ ] **[2026-08-14] `PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` is never set — anywhere.** `apps/api/src/environment.ts:65` defaults it to `http://localhost:3001`, and **no CloudFormation template or workflow sets it**. `webhook.tool.ts:233,303` hands that value to third-party toolpack runtimes as the `writeUrl` / `readUrl` for `GET|POST /api/webhook/handle/:id` (#124's pull-on-read grant), so every custom webhook toolpack in a deployed environment is currently told to call back to *its own localhost*. This is **broken in dev today**, not just latent for prod. Fix alongside the callback URLs, from the same parameters:

```yaml
- Name: PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL
  Value: !Sub "https://${Subdomain}.${DomainName}"
```

Also **dev-affecting**, and it lands in the pre-work PR (see the amendment log).

### GitHub Actions workflow

- [ ] **[audit] Coordinate with #311, don't duplicate it.** #311 (public marketing site) ships **the repo's first production pipeline** — a manual tag/release cut from `main` — and is explicitly scoped to "structure the workflow so the same trigger pattern is reusable for `app.portalsai.io` (and the API) when their prod deploys land later." Whichever ticket lands second consumes the other's shape. If #311 lands first, `deploy-prod.yml` **calls** its reusable workflow / copies its trigger; if #83 lands first, it defines the reusable shape and #311 adopts it. This supersedes the trigger-choice analysis below, which reached the same conclusion independently.
- [ ] New `.github/workflows/deploy-prod.yml` mirroring `deploy-dev.yml`. Differences:
  - `Environment=prod` everywhere; stack names `portalai-prod-…`; `concurrency.group: deploy-prod`
  - `Subdomain=app` / `Subdomain=api`; URLs `app.portalsai.io` / `api.portalsai.io`
  - Reads `PROD_*` GitHub Actions secrets (counterparts of every `DEV_*` secret used in `deploy-dev.yml`)
  - **[audit] A separate deploy identity.** `deploy-dev.yml` assumes a single unprefixed `secrets.AWS_ROLE_ARN`. Prod gets its own OIDC role (`PROD_AWS_ROLE_ARN`) whose trust policy is scoped to the release trigger / a protected GitHub Environment — not the same role dev pushes with. ~~Decide up front whether prod lives in the **same AWS account** as dev or its own~~ **[2026-08-14] Decided: same AWS account as dev.** Isolation is IAM/tag/stack-name based, not account based. Consequences, all now settled: the existing `portalsai.io` hosted zone is reused (`PROD_HOSTED_ZONE_ID` = `DEV_HOSTED_ZONE_ID`'s value), the existing wildcard cert can be threaded by ARN instead of standing up a second `dns-certs` stack, and `portalai/prod/*` vs `portalai/dev/*` path separation plus a distinct deploy role is what keeps dev credentials from touching prod
- [ ] **[2026-08-14] No GitHub Environments exist on the repo at all** (`gh api repos/…/environments` → empty). `deploy-site-prod.yml:87` already passes `gh-environment: prod` and its header claims "required reviewers on the `prod` environment are the human gate on a public deploy" — referencing a missing environment **auto-creates it with no protection rules**, so that gate is currently fictional. Create the `prod` Environment with required reviewers, and scope `PROD_AWS_ROLE_ARN`'s OIDC trust policy to it
  - **[audit] Drop the `tag-deploy` job.** Dev's final job pushes a `dev-<timestamp>-<sha>` tag; under a release trigger the release tag already is the marker
  - **Deploy trigger: `on: release: types: [published]`** (lean). Draft a release in the GitHub UI → pick/create a tag → write release notes → Publish. Composes cleanly with the PR-per-feature flow, gives a free deployment journal via the release-notes field, and one-click rollback by re-running the previous release's workflow run. Stack a GitHub Environment with required reviewers on top later if we want a second human gate
    - Rejected alternatives: `workflow_dispatch` (no version/changelog/audit story); tag push `on: push: tags: ['v*']` (same audit benefit, worse UX); a `release` branch (a branch convention we don't otherwise need); auto-deploy on `main` push + Environment approval (keeps prod tied to merge cadence — the release flow batches a week of merges into one deployable artifact)

### Production marketing site (`www.portalsai.io`) **[2026-08-05 amendment — folded in from #311's out-of-scope]**

The reusable prod site pipeline already exists — `.github/workflows/deploy-site-prod.yml` (release/dispatch/manual triggers, `prod` GitHub Environment, `subdomain: www`, `site-url: https://www.portalsai.io`, `portalops-env: prod`) calling `deploy-static-site.yml`. It is **gated off**: its `resolve` job exits with a notice while the `PROD_SITE_CONFIG_URL` repository variable is unset (the guard explicitly names this ticket). So the work here is **provisioning + activation**, not building the pipeline.

- [ ] **Provision the prod site stack** `portalai-prod-site` (`infra/cloudformation/site.yml`) — S3 + CloudFront fronted by `www.portalsai.io`, consuming the `${Environment}-CertificateArn` export (the wildcard cert already covers `*.portalsai.io`, so no new cert). `deploy-static-site.yml` deploys this stack itself when a prod deploy runs; confirm it resolves the prod cert ARN and writes the `www` A-alias without colliding with dev's `site-dev` record (different name, same zone)
- [ ] **Set the `PROD_SITE_CONFIG_URL` repository variable** = `https://api.portalsai.io/api/public/site-config`. This is the switch that ungates the pipeline — set it only **after** the prod API is live and its `/api/public/site-config` returns 200
- [ ] **Provision the site-config inputs the prod preflight fail-closes on (#319).** The prod site build runs a preflight that refuses to publish on unresolved contacts or empty tiers, and **prod is deliberately not auto-seeded** (non-prod-only by design). So an operator must, before the first prod site deploy:
  - `portalops vars set SUPPORT_EMAIL <addr> --env prod --yes --confirm-prod` and the same for `SALES_EMAIL` **and [2026-08-14] `ADMIN_EMAIL`** (writes `/portalai/prod/{support,sales,admin}-email`; see the SSM list below)
  - `portalops tier apply --env prod --yes --confirm-prod` so the pricing page renders the live paid tiers (depends on the live Stripe prices existing — see the Stripe section)
- [ ] **Trigger:** publishing a GitHub release runs `deploy-site-prod` (same release event the app/api prod deploy keys off). Confirm a release, with `PROD_SITE_CONFIG_URL` set and contacts/tiers provisioned, publishes `www.portalsai.io` green — the preflight passes, no fixture stamp reaches production
- [ ] **The rebuild loop needs a prod dispatch token.** `portalops vars set` / `tier apply --env prod` fire a `site-config-changed` `repository_dispatch` (via `GITHUB_DISPATCH_TOKEN`) that re-runs `deploy-site-prod` — so a prod price/contact change republishes the site with no code change, exactly as dev does. This requires the `github-dispatch-token` secret in prod (added to the secret list below)

### AWS Secrets Manager + SSM (the `portalops vars` catalog)

**[audit] The ticket's original list was Secrets-Manager-only and predates two Stripe secrets.** The full managed set is `packages/devops-cli/src/catalog.ts` (**[2026-08-14]** now 11 secrets + 10 SSM parameters); paths are `portalai/prod/<name>` (Secrets Manager) and `/portalai/prod/<name>` (SSM).

> **[2026-08-14] The catalog is not actually complete — fix it before provisioning prod.** `GEOCODING_API_KEY` (Mapbox, #315) is wired into `backend.yml:62,524` and `deploy-dev.yml:164` and has a `DEV_SECRET_ARN_GEOCODING_API_KEY` repo secret, but **it was never added to `catalog.ts`**. So `portalops vars template/apply --env prod` silently omits it and the prod task definition would fail to resolve a required secret ARN. Adding the entry is part of the pre-work PR (see the amendment log), and it must land **before** anyone runs `vars apply --env prod`. Provision with `portalops vars set/apply --env prod --yes --confirm-prod` once the registry entry exists (below), and capture the secret **ARNs** as GitHub Actions secrets — `backend.yml` takes secrets by ARN parameter, but reads SSM parameters by convention path (no parameter to thread).

Secrets Manager → `PROD_SECRET_ARN_*` GitHub secret:

- [ ] `database-url` → `PROD_SECRET_ARN_DATABASE_URL`
- [ ] `encryption-key` → `PROD_SECRET_ARN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (column encryption for `connector_instances.credentials` — **generate fresh, never reuse dev's**)
- [ ] `auth0-webhook-secret` → `PROD_SECRET_ARN_AUTH0_WEBHOOK_SECRET`
- [ ] `anthropic-api-key` → `PROD_SECRET_ARN_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
- [ ] `tavily-api-key` → `PROD_SECRET_ARN_TAVILY_API_KEY`
- [ ] **[2026-08-14]** `geocoding-api-key` → `PROD_SECRET_ARN_GEOCODING_API_KEY` — the **Mapbox** access token behind `geocode` / `reverse_geocode` / `bulk_geocode_records` (#315). A ninth vendor the earlier audits missed entirely. Portal-paid, `expensive` cost class alongside Tavily, so the prod Mapbox account needs its own plan/limit. Absent, the geocode tools simply aren't constructed (`tools.service.ts:544-548`) and maps still render — a silent capability loss in prod, not a boot failure
- [ ] `google-oauth-client-secret` → `PROD_SECRET_ARN_GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`
- [ ] `microsoft-oauth-client-secret` → `PROD_SECRET_ARN_MICROSOFT_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`
- [ ] `oauth-state-secret` → `PROD_SECRET_ARN_OAUTH_STATE_SECRET`
- [ ] **[audit]** `stripe-secret-key` → `PROD_SECRET_ARN_STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` (live-mode restricted key — see Stripe section)
- [ ] **[audit]** `stripe-webhook-secret` → `PROD_SECRET_ARN_STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`
- [ ] **[2026-08-05 amendment]** `github-dispatch-token` → `PROD_SECRET_ARN_GITHUB_DISPATCH_TOKEN` — a fine-scoped GitHub token (`repository_dispatch` write on `EnterpriseBT/portal-ai`) that `portalops vars set`/`tier apply --env prod` uses to fire the `site-config-changed` rebuild of `www.portalsai.io`. Was added to the catalog after the audit (`catalog.ts:59`); a prod config change won't republish the site without it. **[2026-08-14] The dev counterpart does not exist either** — `deploy-dev.yml:170` passes `secrets.DEV_SECRET_ARN_GITHUB_DISPATCH_TOKEN`, but no such repo secret is set, so `backend.yml`'s `HasGithubDispatchToken` condition is false and **the site-rebuild dispatch loop has never run in any environment**. Prove it in dev first; prod must not be the first place it is exercised

SSM Parameter Store (read by path, no GitHub secret needed) — **[audit] entirely missing from the original ticket, and the API will not boot correctly without them**:

- [ ] `/portalai/prod/auth0-domain`, `/portalai/prod/auth0-audience`
- [ ] `/portalai/prod/cors-origin` = `https://app.portalsai.io`. **Load-bearing beyond CORS:** `billing.service.ts:29` derives Stripe checkout `success_url`/`cancel_url` and the billing-portal `return_url` from `CORS_ORIGIN[0]`, so the prod app URL must be **first** in the list
- [ ] `/portalai/prod/google-oauth-client-id`, `/portalai/prod/microsoft-oauth-client-id`, `/portalai/prod/microsoft-oauth-tenant`
- [ ] `/portalai/prod/namespace` (dev uses `portalsai-staging`; prod needs its own), `/portalai/prod/system-id`
- [ ] `/portalai/prod/auth0-cli-client-id` — the device-flow app id `portalai login` reads (#194); not consumed by `backend.yml`, but required for CLI access to prod
- [ ] **[2026-08-05 amendment]** `/portalai/prod/support-email`, `/portalai/prod/sales-email` — the public site-config contact addresses (`siteConfig`-marked). The prod `/api/public/site-config` **fail-closes (503)** and the prod marketing-site deploy is blocked until both are set (prod is not auto-seeded — #319). Set via `portalops vars set --env prod --yes --confirm-prod`
- [ ] **[2026-08-14]** `/portalai/prod/admin-email` — the third `siteConfig` contact key, added by #369/#380 after the last amendment (`catalog.ts:80`). It is the legal / data-controller address on the site's terms and privacy pages **and the DMARC `rua=` reporting destination** on the mail stack. Prod values for all three are the real inboxes — `support@` / `sales@` / `admin@portalsai.io` — where every non-prod environment deliberately uses `qa@portalsai.io` so no non-prod surface can advertise a customer-facing address (`docs/PORTALSAI_MAIL.spec.md`, D3). **A prod build with these unset silently advertises `qa@`** — the design's stated weakest point, caught only by the smoke step
- [ ] **[2026-08-14]** Prod is where the three addresses first diverge from `qa@`, so this is also where the mailbox/alias side must already exist: confirm `support@`, `sales@` and `admin@portalsai.io` deliver in Google Workspace before the values are written

### GitHub Actions secrets

- [ ] `PROD_AWS_ROLE_ARN` **[audit]**
- [ ] `PROD_HOSTED_ZONE_ID` (Route 53 zone for `portalsai.io` — the same zone dev uses, unless prod gets its own account)
- [ ] `PROD_VITE_AUTH0_DOMAIN`, `PROD_VITE_AUTH0_CLIENT_ID`, `PROD_VITE_AUTH0_AUDIENCE`
- [ ] All `PROD_SECRET_ARN_*` above
- ~~**[audit]** The web build surface is confirmed unchanged since filing~~ **[2026-08-14] The web build surface has grown.** It is now `VITE_APP_VERSION`, `VITE_APP_SHA`, `VITE_AUTH0_{DOMAIN,CLIENT_ID,AUDIENCE}`, `VITE_API_BASE_URL`, **`VITE_SUPPORT_EMAIL`, `VITE_SALES_EMAIL`** (#369 — resolved from SSM *at build time* by `deploy-dev.yml:196-215`, not passed as repo secrets). Still no `VITE_STRIPE_*` (checkout is entirely server-driven). **The prod workflow must reproduce the SSM-resolution step**, not just the secret list — a prod bundle built without it advertises the `qa@` fallback on the in-app Help view

### Stripe production account **[audit — new section]**

Everything in this section postdates the original ticket: Stripe subscription billing (#176), Stripe Tax (#217), the declarative tier catalog + `portalops tier apply` (#218), the sandbox wiring (#239), the webhook subscription guard (#230), and in-app plan change via the billing portal (#260) all shipped between June and July 2026. **Each Portal environment is a separate Stripe account** — `local` runs test mode, `app-dev` has its own Sandbox, and prod is the first **live-mode** account. Nothing crosses envs except lookup keys.

- [ ] **Business verification / account activation.** Live mode requires a completed Stripe account: legal entity, business representative, bank account for payouts, statement descriptor, support contact. **This is the one part of the ticket with an external dependency and a lead time** — start it first. Stripe's review also expects a **public website describing the product and pricing**, which is #311 (`site.portalsai.io`); sequence #311's site to be live, or at least publicly reachable, before submitting
- [ ] **Restricted API key.** Create a live-mode restricted key (`rk_live_…`) for the app with write access limited to what billing uses (customers, checkout sessions, billing portal sessions, subscriptions read, prices/products read) → `portalai/prod/stripe-secret-key`. Per the standing vendor rule, operator/agent inspection uses a **separate read-only** restricted key — mutation safety is the credential, not a prompt
- [ ] **Products + prices in the live account** carrying the catalog's lookup keys — `plus_monthly` and `pro_monthly` (`packages/core/src/registries/tier-catalog.ts`). Amounts are set in Stripe only; no price amount is ever committed to this repo
- [ ] **Real pricing decision → split out as #325.** The catalog's allocations are *test-grade* magnitudes (`pro` has unlimited `metered`) and no live amounts exist. The production pricing + allocation pass is now **#325** (configure production tier catalog & pricing); go-live blocks on it. - Publishing a GitHub release from `main` deploys end-to-end without manual intervention beyond the initial vendor + Secrets Manager bootstrap; a plain push to `main` deploys **only** to dev and never touches prod
- `https://app.portalsai.io` loads the production frontend; Auth0 login works; the SPA calls `https://api.portalsai.io` (no `app-dev` / `api-dev` string survives in the prod bundle)
- `https://api.portalsai.io/api/health` returns 200
- A test connector (public REST API, no credentials) syncs end-to-end on prod
- Google Sheets + Microsoft Excel OAuth round-trip against the prod callback URLs

- **[audit]** `portalops tier apply --env prod --yes --confirm-prod` reports the paid rows converged onto live-mode price ids; the Settings plan cards render the live tiers

Tax is applied per the account's configuration

- Every "pending #83" doc section is rewritten as shipped behavior

- Custom domains other than `app.portalsai.io` + `api.portalsai.io` + `www.portalsai.io`. **[2026-08-05 amendment]** apex / bare-`portalsai.io` redirect is still out of scope
